cultural_serving_suggestions: This salad can be served as a refreshing side dish or a light main course.
It pairs well with other traditional Peruvian dishes.
instructions: Wash and peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Place potatoes in a large pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil.
Cook until tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Let cool slightly.
While potatoes cook, prepare dressing. In a bowl, combine ají amarillo paste, Dijon mustard, vegan mayonnaise, lime juice, minced garlic, and vegetable oil.
Whisk dressing until smooth. Season with salt and pepper.
In a large mixing bowl, combine cooled diced potatoes, thinly sliced red onion, julienned red bell pepper, and julienned yellow bell pepper.
Pour dressing over vegetables. Gently toss to coat all ingredients evenly.
Stir in chopped fresh cilantro. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Arrange lettuce leaves on serving plates if desired. Spoon salad onto plates.
Garnish with halved Kalamata olives. Serve immediately or chill before serving.
notes: This recipe is a vegan adaptation of classic Peruvian potato dishes like 'Papa a la Huancaína' or 'Causa Rellena', replacing dairy and eggs with plant-based alternatives while retaining the core flavors of ají amarillo and lime.
traditional_techniques: The use of ají amarillo paste and lime is central to Peruvian cuisine, representing a traditional flavor profile.
The precise cutting of vegetables (thinly sliced onion, julienned bell pepper) reflects attention to detail common in Peruvian cooking.

recipes.recipe_name: Indonesian-Spiced Chicken Bitterballen
recipes.special_requests: Indonesian cuisine, Fusion, crispy, Indonesian, fastfood, unique, Dutch
recipes.visual_description: A casual sharing platter presents a generous portion of Indonesian-Spiced Chicken Bitterballen. The bitterballen are uniformly golden-brown with a visibly crispy Panko crust, each a small, perfectly rounded ball. They are arranged in a natural, slightly mounded pile on a rustic wooden board or an oblong white ceramic plate, allowing for moderate negative space. Beside the main pile, a small white porcelain ramekin holds a vibrant, creamy orange-red Sambal Aioli. A few fresh cilantro sprigs are scattered lightly around the bitterballen, adding a pop of green color, or a delicate sprinkle of finely sliced red chili. The overall composition is balanced and appealing, showcasing the inviting texture and color of the snack. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. White ceramic side plates are casually placed nearby. Natural, even lighting highlights the crispness and rich color of the food. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a restaurant atmosphere with subtle textures of dark wood.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally, bitterballen are served as a 'borrelhapje' (snack with drinks) in the Netherlands.
The addition of Sambal Aioli provides an Indonesian-inspired accompaniment, offering a spicy and tangy counterpoint to the rich, savory bitterballen.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass stalk, white part only, bruised and finely sliced
Fresh cilantro or red chili, for garnish

instructions: Boil or roast chicken until fully cooked. Shred chicken finely. Set aside.
In a large pan, melt butter over medium heat. Add minced shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, lemongrass, and kaffir lime leaves. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Stir in ground turmeric, coriander, and cumin. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add 80g plain flour to the pan. Cook, stirring, for 2 minutes to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in chicken broth and milk until the mixture is thick and smooth. Continue whisking to prevent lumps.
Fold in the shredded chicken. Mix well. Season with salt and white pepper to taste.
Transfer the chicken mixture to a shallow dish. Cover tightly. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or overnight, until firm.
Prepare a breading station: Place 200g plain flour in one shallow dish, beaten eggs in a second, and Panko breadcrumbs in a third.
Scoop approximately 25g of the chilled chicken mixture. Roll into small, uniform balls, about 3cm in diameter.
Dredge each ball first in flour, ensuring full coating. Then dip in beaten egg, allowing excess to drip off. Finally, roll thoroughly in Panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere.
Heat neutral oil in a deep pot or fryer to 175°C (350°F).
Carefully fry bitterballen in batches. Cook until golden brown and crispy, approximately 3-4 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove fried bitterballen with a slotted spoon. Drain on a wire rack lined with paper towels.
For the Sambal Aioli: In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, sambal oelek, and lime juice. Mix well.
Serve Indonesian-Spiced Chicken Bitterballen hot with the Sambal Aioli.
notes: Ensure the chicken mixture is thoroughly chilled before forming the balls; this makes them easier to handle and prevents them from falling apart during frying.
Maintain a consistent oil temperature for even browning and proper cooking through. Overcrowding the fryer will drop the oil temperature.
For an extra crispy crust, consider double-breading: after the first breading, dip again in egg and then Panko.
traditional_techniques: Roux (Dutch culinary technique for thickening sauces)
Deep Frying (common in both Dutch and Indonesian cuisines for snacks)
Spice Grinding/Blending (fundamental to Indonesian flavor profiles)

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tempeh Kroketten with Quick Pickled Cucumber
recipes.special_requests: Indonesian cuisine, Fusion, crispy, Indonesian, fastfood, unique, Dutch
recipes.visual_description: A rustic, reclaimed wooden board holds an inviting arrangement of golden-brown Fermented Tempeh Kroketten, each a perfectly cylindrical form, showcasing a uniform, crisp exterior. The kroketten are artfully scattered, some slightly overlapping, allowing for natural shadows and highlights. Their surface boasts a beautiful deep golden hue, hinting at their satisfying crunch. Adjacent to the kroketten, a small, handcrafted ceramic bowl in an earthy cream tone holds a vibrant, translucent quick-pickled cucumber relish. The relish features thin, delicate slices of cucumber interspersed with small, bright red chili rings and a few fresh cilantro leaves, adding a pop of fresh green. The entire composition is set against a backdrop of soft, diffused natural light, casting gentle shadows that enhance the textural details. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone subtly peeks from beneath the board, adding a touch of organic texture. The focus is entirely on the food, presented simply and elegantly, celebrating its natural ingredients and sustainable preparation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light snack (gorengan) or appetizer.
Often enjoyed with a small bowl of sambal (chili sauce).
Can be eaten plain or with a simple side of fresh bird's eye chilies.
instructions: Prepare Vegetable Broth (Zero-Waste): Collect vegetable scraps (carrot peels, onion ends, herb stems). Place in a pot with 500ml water. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain. Set aside 200ml.
Prepare Tempeh: Steam tempeh blocks 15 minutes until tender. Mash thoroughly. Set aside.

Make Aromatic Paste: In a food processor, combine roughly chopped shallots, garlic, peeled galangal slices, thinly sliced white part of lemongrass, peeled turmeric slices, kaffir lime leaves, and red chilies (if using). Blend until a smooth paste forms. Add a little oil or water if needed.
Cook Filling: Heat 2 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pan over medium heat. Sauté aromatic paste 5-7 minutes until fragrant.

Combine Filling: Add mashed tempeh to the pan. Stir well. Add coconut milk, 200ml vegetable broth, salt, white pepper, and freshly grated nutmeg. Simmer gently 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until liquid is absorbed and mixture is thick.

Prepare Potato: Boil peeled potatoes until very tender. Mash thoroughly. Add mashed potato to the tempeh mixture. Mix well to combine and form a cohesive, firm dough. Taste and adjust seasoning. Let cool completely.
Shape Kroketten: Once cool, take small portions (approx. 40-50g) of the mixture. Roll into cylindrical shapes, about 6-7 cm long and 2-3 cm thick. Place on a tray.
Prepare Breading Station: Set up three shallow dishes: one with all-purpose flour, one with aquafaba/plant milk, and one with panko breadcrumbs.

Bread Kroketten: Roll each kroketten first in flour, shaking off excess. Then dip in aquafaba/plant milk, ensuring it's fully coated. Finally, roll generously in panko breadcrumbs, pressing gently to adhere. Repeat for all kroketten.
Chill: Refrigerate breaded kroketten 30 minutes to firm up the coating.

Prepare Pickled Cucumber Relish: In a bowl, combine rice vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Stir until sugar and salt dissolve. Add thinly sliced cucumber and sliced red chili (if using). Let sit 15 minutes.
Fry Kroketten: Heat cooking oil in a deep pot or fryer to 175°C. Fry kroketten in batches, 3-4 minutes per batch, until golden brown and crispy. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Drain: Remove fried kroketten with a slotted spoon. Place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Serve: Arrange crispy Fermented Tempeh Kroketten on a serving board or platter. Serve immediately with the Quick Pickled Cucumber Relish and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro.
notes: Tempeh is a fermented soybean product, making this recipe naturally fermentation-focused.
Using vegetable scraps for broth reduces food waste.
The quick pickled cucumber adds a refreshing, tangy contrast and uses seasonal produce.
Ensure the kroketten mixture is firm and well-chilled before breading and frying for best results.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef Ragu with Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of rigatoni is arranged on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. The thick, tubular pasta is thoroughly coated in a rich, deep red beef ragu, showcasing visible pieces of tender, slow-cooked ground beef. The sauce has a hearty, rustic texture. A light scattering of vibrant green, freshly chopped parsley rests atop the ragu, providing a subtle color contrast. A small mound of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano cheese is placed on the side of the pasta. The dish sits on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A casually placed, simple linen napkin in a neutral tone is beside the plate. The scene is lit with soft, warm light, creating a cozy, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a lived-in dining space.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano at the table.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery. Cook 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add ground beef to the pot. Break apart with a spoon. Cook until browned, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.
Stir in minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and beef broth. Add oregano and bay leaf. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 60 minutes, or up to 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
While ragu simmers, cook rigatoni according to package instructions until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 120 ml pasta water.
Remove bay leaf from ragu. Stir cooked pasta into the ragu. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
notes: For a richer flavor, simmer the ragu longer, up to 2 hours.
A splash of red wine can be added before the tomatoes for deeper flavor, if desired.

recipes.recipe_name: Ayam Geprek Popcorn Chicken
recipes.special_requests: Indonesian cuisine, Fusion, crispy, Indonesian, fastfood, unique, weird
recipes.visual_description: A generous pile of golden-brown, irregularly shaped crispy Ayam Geprek popcorn chicken pieces is presented on a simple, round woven bamboo basket lined with light parchment paper. The chicken has a craggy, textured crust from deep frying. Beside the chicken, in a small, rustic, off-white ceramic bowl, sits the creamy, pale orange Sambal Matah Mayo Dip, flecked with vivid green kaffir lime leaves and red chili bits. A few fresh lime wedges are casually placed near the dip. The entire arrangement rests on a warm, well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by soft, natural kitchen light, creating a cozy, inviting, and unpretentious homestyle scene. The focus is entirely on the food, with ample negative space around the central dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a communal sharing snack for casual gatherings.
Offer small individual dipping bowls for each person.

ingredients.name: Lemongrass
ingredients.quantity: 8 stalks, white part only, thinly sliced

ingredients.name: Kaffir lime leaves
ingredients.quantity: 15 leaves, central vein removed, thinly sliced

instructions: Cut chicken breast into irregular bite-sized chunks. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a large bowl, combine chicken chunks with 5g salt, 5g garlic powder, and 2g white pepper. Mix well. Marinate for 15 minutes.
Prepare dredging station: In a shallow dish, whisk eggs. In another shallow dish, combine all-purpose flour, cornstarch, 15g garlic powder, 3g white pepper, and 10g salt. Mix well.
Dip each chicken chunk into egg, then dredge thoroughly in flour mixture. Ensure full coating. Set aside on a wire rack.
Heat cooking oil in a large pot or deep fryer to 175°C (350°F).
Fry chicken chunks in batches for 5-7 minutes, or until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Do not overcrowd the pot.
Remove fried chicken with a slotted spoon. Drain on a wire rack over paper towels. Season lightly with extra salt immediately.
Prepare Sambal Matah: In a heatproof bowl, combine sliced shallots, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and bird's eye chilies. Add 5g salt.
Heat 50ml cooking oil until very hot. Pour hot oil over the Sambal Matah ingredients. Stir well.
Add lime juice to the Sambal Matah. Mix well.
In a separate bowl, combine Sambal Matah with mayonnaise. Stir until well blended.
Serve crispy Ayam Geprek Popcorn Chicken hot with Sambal Matah Mayo Dip on the side.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust chili quantity in Sambal Matah to preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Ayam Geprek Bites
recipes.special_requests: Indonesian cuisine, Fusion, crispy, Indonesian, fastfood
recipes.visual_description: A generous pile of golden-brown, crispy Ayam Geprek Bites is artfully arranged on a rustic, round ceramic sharing platter, slightly off-center. Each chicken piece, cut into irregular 3-4 cm cubes, boasts a visibly crunchy, craggy coating with hints of seasoned flour. The chicken's interior is tender, juicy, and white. Next to the chicken, in a small, rough-hewn ceramic bowl, sits a vibrant, coarse-textured red sambal, glistening with oil and flecked with red chili seeds and small pieces of garlic and shallot. A few fresh green bird's eye chili slices and a bright green lime wedge are casually placed near the sambal for garnish. The platter rests on a well-used, light brown wooden kitchen table, showing natural grain and minor imperfections. The background is simple and uncluttered, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen with soft, warm, natural light illuminating the dish. A casually folded, plain cloth napkin in a neutral tone is placed to the side. The overall presentation is homely, inviting, and unpretentious, emphasizing comfort and shared eating.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Traditionally served with warm white rice.
Often accompanied by fresh cucumber slices or blanched vegetables like cabbage or green beans.
Eaten by hand for a true street food experience.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm cubes. Pat dry with paper towels.
In a bowl, mix chicken with 5 g garlic powder, 2 g white pepper, and 5 g salt. Marinate for 30 minutes.
Prepare dry coating: In a large bowl, combine flour, cornstarch, remaining garlic powder, white pepper, and 10 g salt. Mix well.
Prepare wet batter: In a separate bowl, whisk eggs with cold water.
Dip marinated chicken cubes into wet batter, ensuring full coverage.
Transfer chicken cubes to dry coating. Press firmly to coat completely. Ensure no wet spots. Repeat for all chicken.
Heat vegetable oil in a large deep pot or wok to 170°C.
Carefully add chicken cubes in batches. Do not overcrowd the pot.
Fry chicken for 6-8 minutes, or until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Use a meat thermometer.
Remove chicken from oil. Place on a wire rack over paper towels to drain excess oil. Keep warm.
Prepare sambal: Roughly chop chilies, garlic, and shallots.
Heat 50 ml of the hot frying oil in a small pan. Add chopped chilies, garlic, and shallots. Fry for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Do not burn.
Transfer fried aromatics to a mortar and pestle. Add 5 g salt and 5 g sugar. Grind into a coarse paste.
Squeeze juice from half a lime into the sambal. Stir to combine.
Serve crispy chicken bites piled high on a platter. Serve sambal alongside in a small bowl for dipping or spooning over.
notes: For extra heat, a small amount of the hot frying oil can be poured over the sambal just before grinding.

The 'geprek' (smashed) technique is traditionally done by mashing the fried chicken with the sambal in a mortar and pestle. For bites, serving the sambal on the side allows for individual customization and easier snacking, or small batches can be 'geprek-ed' just before serving.
traditional_techniques: Making sambal ulek (grinding fresh chili paste in a mortar and pestle)
Deep frying to achieve crispy texture

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Banana with Herbed Cottage Cheese and Toasted Pecans
recipes.visual_description: The starter is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a single, elegantly arranged portion. Two to three thick, diagonally cut grilled banana slices, bearing distinct golden-brown grill marks, form the base. Each slice is topped with a generous, creamy dollop of bright white herbed cottage cheese, creating a pleasing contrast in color and texture. The cottage cheese is studded with vibrant green flecks of fresh chives and parsley. Scattered over the top are coarsely chopped, toasted pecan pieces, adding a warm, earthy brown hue and a textural crunch. A light drizzle of golden olive oil glistens on the plate, with a subtle dusting of red chili flakes for a pop of color. The dish is framed by moderate negative space, sitting on a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. Natural, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's fresh ingredients and appealing presentation in a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Drain cottage cheese if excessively watery. Combine cottage cheese, chives, parsley, minced garlic, lemon juice, salt, and pepper in a small bowl. Mix well. Set aside.
Heat a grill pan or large frying pan over medium-high heat.
Slice bananas diagonally into 1.5 cm thick pieces.
Brush banana slices lightly with olive oil.
Place banana slices on the hot grill pan. Grill for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown grill marks appear and bananas are slightly softened. Do not overcook.
While bananas grill, toast pecan halves in a dry pan over medium heat for 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Chop coarsely.
Arrange grilled banana slices on a serving plate.
Spoon a dollop of herbed cottage cheese onto each banana slice.
Sprinkle generously with toasted pecans.
Drizzle lightly with a small amount of olive oil. Garnish with a pinch of red chili flakes if desired. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Cheddar Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast medallions forms the centerpiece, golden-brown with a light crust, arranged neatly on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A rich, creamy, pale yellow cheddar sauce generously coats the chicken and pools elegantly around its base. Alongside, vibrant green asparagus spears, cooked to crisp-tender perfection, are neatly arranged, providing a striking color contrast. Freshly chopped bright green parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce for a final pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. The composition is balanced with appropriate negative space, showcasing a refined restaurant portion. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and colors of the food in a modern bistro atmosphere.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 190°C. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside to rest.
In the same skillet, melt butter over medium heat. Add diced shallot and cook for 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in flour to create a roux. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Gradually whisk in chicken stock until smooth. Bring to a simmer.
Pour in double cream. Simmer for 2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until completely melted and smooth. Season sauce with salt and pepper to taste.
While chicken cooks, blanch asparagus spears in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes until crisp-tender. Drain immediately.
Slice rested chicken breasts into thick medallions.
Arrange sliced chicken on plates. Spoon creamy cheddar sauce generously over chicken. Place blanched asparagus alongside.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Thighs with Savory Tomato-Onion Ragu
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is centered on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken thigh, golden-brown and crisp-skinned, is presented whole, not sliced. It is generously topped with a rich, deep red tomato and onion ragu. The ragu is thick and glossy, featuring tender, slightly caramelized sliced onions and crushed tomatoes. A few vibrant green fresh basil leaves are scattered over the ragu, adding a fresh contrast. The plate has ample negative space, allowing the vibrant colors and textures of the dish to stand out. The setting is a modern bistro, with the plate resting on a simple light wooden table. A neatly folded cotton napkin and standard flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rustic elegance and inviting textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the ragu.
Serve with a simple side of polenta or rice.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Place chicken thighs skin-side down. Sear until skin is golden brown and crispy, about 8-10 minutes.
Flip chicken. Sear other side for 5 minutes. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onion to the same skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly caramelized, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and dried oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the skillet, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken reaches 75°C (167°F).
Cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and tender.
Uncover. Simmer for an additional 5-10 minutes to thicken the sauce if needed.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Parmesan Toasts
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Chicken Parmesan Toasts is presented on a simple, round off-white ceramic plate. Three thick-cut slices of rustic Italian bread, golden-brown and irregular, form the base. Each is generously piled with tender, shredded chicken simmered in a vibrant red San Marzano tomato sauce. The chicken mixture is slightly mounded, showcasing its hearty texture. A layer of melted, bubbly Parmesan cheese, golden and slightly caramelized, blankets the chicken and toast. Fresh green basil leaves, torn casually, scatter over the top, adding a pop of color. The plate sits on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table, reflecting natural, warm light. A crumpled linen napkin in a neutral tone and a simple glass tumbler are placed casually beside the plate, creating a homely, inviting scene.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a warm appetizer.
Often enjoyed as part of an antipasto spread.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add chicken breasts to the skillet. Cook until browned on all sides. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from skillet. Shred chicken using two forks or by hand. Set aside.
Add crushed tomatoes and dried oregano to the skillet. Bring to a simmer.
Season sauce with salt and pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir shredded chicken back into the tomato sauce. Mix well.
Arrange bread slices on a baking sheet.
Spoon generous amounts of the chicken mixture onto each bread slice.
Top each toast with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until cheese is melted and bubbly and bread is lightly toasted.
Garnish with fresh basil leaves before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked to an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo alla Parmigiana
recipes.visual_description: A single whole golden-brown pan-fried chicken breast serves as the centerpiece on a clean white porcelain plate. The chicken is topped with a generous layer of rich, vibrant red tomato sauce and a thick medallion of melted, slightly charred fresh mozzarella cheese. The breading on the edges remains visible and crispy. A delicate garnish of whole fresh basil leaves and finely grated parmesan adds contrast. The dish is presented in a modern bistro setting on a dark oak table with a white cotton napkin. To the side, a small nest of herb-tossed spaghetti provides balance. The lighting is natural and soft, highlighting the textures of the melted cheese and the golden crust.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small portion of al dente spaghetti with olive oil
Accompany with a simple arugula salad and balsamic vinaigrette
Provide a side of crusty Italian bread to mop up the tomato sauce
instructions: Flatten chicken breasts to 1.5cm thickness using a meat mallet.
Season both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper.
Combine breadcrumbs with 25g of parmesan in a shallow bowl.
Dredge each chicken breast in flour, dip in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly in breadcrumbs.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Fry chicken for 4 minutes per side until the coating is golden and crisp.
Combine passata, garlic, and oregano in a small saucepan over medium-low heat.
Simmer sauce for 10 minutes and season to taste.
Place fried chicken breasts into a baking dish.
Spoon tomato sauce over each breast and top with mozzarella slices.
Bake at 200°C for 10 minutes until cheese is melted and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Garnish with fresh basil and remaining parmesan before serving.
notes: Always verify the internal temperature of the chicken reaches 75°C.
Use low-moisture fresh mozzarella to prevent the breading from becoming soggy.
Press the breadcrumbs firmly into the chicken to ensure a consistent crust.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Tomato Braised Chicken Thighs
recipes.visual_description: A single, generously portioned boneless chicken thigh, golden-brown from searing, rests in a pool of rustic, deep red tomato sauce on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. The sauce is thick with visible bits of diced onion and crushed tomatoes, hinting at its rich texture. A sprinkle of vibrant green, chopped fresh parsley adds a touch of color. The plate sits on a well-worn, light wooden kitchen table, bathed in warm, natural light. A sturdy fork and knife with plain handles are placed casually beside the plate, on a slightly wrinkled linen napkin. The setting evokes a cozy, lived-in family kitchen, emphasizing comfort and hearty home cooking.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Serve alongside simple rice or roasted potatoes
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent, scraping up any browned bits.
Add minced garlic, oregano, and basil. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Taste sauce and adjust seasoning if needed.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken and Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken and Pasta is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. Roasted chicken chunks, golden-brown with slightly crispy edges, are nestled among a generous portion of al dente short pasta. The pasta is coated in a vibrant, rustic red tomato sauce. Interspersed are roasted potato cubes, tender and slightly browned, and strips of colorful bell peppers (red, yellow, orange) with soft, caramelized edges. Burst cherry tomatoes add pops of bright red and juicy texture. The dish is garnished simply with a few fresh green thyme sprigs and a light sprinkle of finely chopped parsley, enhancing its fresh appeal. The composition is organized but natural, allowing for moderate negative space on the plate. The setting features a simple, light wooden table surface. A clean, light beige cotton napkin is folded neatly beside the bowl. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its rich colors and varied textures. The background is minimally blurred, suggesting a casual, inviting bistro atmosphere without distracting from the food.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Peel potatoes. Cut into 2cm cubes.
Core bell peppers. Cut into 2cm strips.
Halve cherry tomatoes.
Mince 2 garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, toss chicken, potatoes, bell peppers, halved cherry tomatoes, 3 thyme sprigs, 30ml olive oil, and dried oregano. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread mixture in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Roast for 25-30 minutes. Chicken should reach 75°C internal temperature. Vegetables should be tender and slightly caramelized.
While chicken roasts, prepare sauce. Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat.
Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add remaining 3 thyme sprigs. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 15 minutes.
Cook pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 120ml pasta water.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Add roasted chicken and vegetables to the sauce. Toss gently to combine.
Add cooked pasta to the pot. Toss with the sauce, chicken, and vegetables. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken and Tomato Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single, browned chicken thigh rests centrally on an off-white ceramic plate. It is generously coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce with visible chunks of tomato and softened diced onion. The sauce has a deep red hue, contrasting with the golden-brown chicken. Fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are scattered casually over the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The chicken is whole, showing its tender, cooked texture. The plate is positioned on a well-worn wooden dining table, revealing its grain. A simple, folded cloth napkin and standard silver fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, natural light illuminates the dish from above, creating soft shadows and highlighting the comforting textures. The overall scene is homely and inviting, typical of a family kitchen.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 4-5 minutes per side until browned. Remove chicken from skillet.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to skillet. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, and oregano. Bring to a simmer.
Return seared chicken to skillet. Reduce heat to low. Cover.
Simmer 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature.
Season sauce with more salt and pepper if needed.
Garnish with fresh basil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Chicken with Tomatoes and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of rustic chicken with tomato and herbs is presented on a simple, off-white ceramic plate. One or two whole, bone-in chicken thighs, seared to a deep golden-brown, rest nestled in a rich, chunky tomato sauce. The sauce, made from crushed tomatoes with visible pieces of diced onion and minced garlic, is a vibrant reddish-orange, coating the chicken and pooling invitingly on the plate. Freshly chopped green basil and oregano leaves are scattered over the dish, adding specks of verdant color. The chicken skin appears slightly crisp, contrasting with the tender, moist meat beneath. The scene is set on a well-worn, natural wood dining table, evoking a cozy, homely kitchen. A simple, dark-colored cloth napkin is casually placed beside the plate. The lighting is warm and inviting, suggesting an intimate family meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
Serve alongside simple pasta like spaghetti or penne.
Offer a sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, oven-safe pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip. Sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged in the sauce.
Stir in chopped fresh oregano and basil. Cover the pan.
Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Uncover the pan. Increase heat slightly. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes to thicken the sauce to your desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed. Serve hot.
notes: This dish can be prepared ahead of time and reheated; flavors often deepen overnight.
For a spicier kick, add a pinch of red pepper flakes with the garlic.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Sausage and Tomato Bake
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Hearty Sausage and Tomato Bake is presented on an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic plate, showcasing a comforting, rustic appeal. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, reflecting a lived-in family atmosphere. The dish features plump, browned sausage pieces (not sliced), interspersed with vibrant, burst cherry tomatoes, soft red onion wedges, and substantial chunks of red and yellow bell peppers. The ingredients are casually arranged, allowing them to touch and slightly overlap, creating a natural, inviting pile. A rich, slightly thickened sauce, formed from the roasted tomatoes, coats the ingredients. Freshly torn green basil leaves are scattered over the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. A piece of rustic crusty bread is casually placed beside the plate. The background is minimal, hinting at a comfortable kitchen with natural clutter, reinforcing the homely comfort food theme. The focus is entirely on the inviting textures and natural colors of the baked dish.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Grease a large baking dish or cast iron skillet.
Cut each sausage into 2-3 substantial pieces. Cut red onion into thick wedges. Cut bell peppers into substantial chunks. Roughly chop garlic cloves.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage pieces. Brown sausages on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Remove sausages and set aside.
Add onion wedges, bell pepper chunks, and chopped garlic to the same pan. Sauté for 5 minutes until slightly softened.
Return sausage pieces to the pan. Add whole cherry tomatoes and dried oregano. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Stir to combine.

Transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish if not using an oven-safe pan. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until sausages are cooked through and vegetables are tender. The tomatoes will burst and create a rustic sauce.
Remove from oven. Tear fresh basil leaves and scatter over the bake.
Serve hot directly from the baking dish or scoop modest portions onto individual plates. Serve with crusty bread for dipping.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallions with Mushroom & Potato Hash
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centrally composed. A generous, slightly mounded portion of golden-brown mushroom and potato hash forms the base, its diced potato cubes exhibiting crispy edges and a fluffy interior, interspersed with earthy brown sliced cremini mushrooms and softened golden onion. Beside the hash, a perfectly pan-seared beef medallion, approximately 150g, rests as a whole, un-sliced piece, displaying a rich, dark brown crust. A glossy, rich brown pan sauce is subtly drizzled over the beef and a small portion of the hash, adding depth. The dish is vibrantly garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped bright green parsley, contrasting beautifully with the warm tones of the beef and hash. The overall presentation is professional and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a softly blurred bistro-style background visible.
cultural_serving_suggestions: A side of simple green salad with vinaigrette
A glass of dry red wine
instructions: Dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Place in a pot. Cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until just tender, about 8-10 minutes. Drain well.
While potatoes cook, thinly slice mushrooms. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.

Heat 30ml olive oil and 20g butter in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add drained potatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, until golden and crispy, about 10-12 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Remove potatoes from pan. Set aside.

Add 15ml olive oil and 10g butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until browned and liquid evaporates, about 7-9 minutes. Add minced garlic and thyme sprigs. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return crispy potatoes to the pan with onions and mushrooms. Stir to combine. Keep warm over low heat.
Pat beef medallions dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on all sides.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 30g butter in a separate heavy-bottomed skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add beef medallions to the hot skillet. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Cook in batches if necessary.
Remove beef from skillet. Place on a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Deglaze the beef skillet with red wine. Scrape up any browned bits. Reduce by half. Add beef broth. Simmer until slightly thickened, about 3-5 minutes. Adjust seasoning.

To serve, spoon a portion of mushroom and potato hash onto each plate. Place a seared beef medallion beside or on top of the hash. Drizzle with pan sauce. Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Mushroom and Potato
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty braised beef is presented in a clean, wide-rimmed white porcelain bowl. Large, tender chunks of rich brown beef are nestled amongst creamy white potato cubes and whole or halved brown mushrooms. A glossy, deep brown sauce generously coats all ingredients, showcasing its rich texture. The beef shows a beautiful seared crust, while the potatoes are soft but hold their shape. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley provides a fresh contrast on top. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the bowl. Standard European-style stainless steel flatware (a fork and spoon) rests to the side. The lighting is natural and even, creating a clean, inviting bistro atmosphere with a minimal, unobtrusive background.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 4-5 cm chunks. Pat dry. Season beef generously with salt and pepper. Dredge beef in flour, shaking off excess.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef chunks in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pot. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add roughly chopped onions to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste and cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in beef stock. Add fresh thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot tightly. Transfer to a preheated oven at 160°C. Braise for 1.5 hours.
While beef braises, scrub potatoes. Cut larger potatoes into 2-3 cm cubes. Keep smaller potatoes whole. Halve or quarter larger mushrooms.
After 1.5 hours, remove pot from oven. Stir in potatoes and mushrooms. Ensure they are mostly submerged in liquid.
Return pot to oven. Continue braising for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef is fork-tender and potatoes are cooked through.
Remove pot from oven. Discard thyme sprigs and bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Rest the braise for 10 minutes before serving. Ladle into individual bowls. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Scallops, Sweet Corn Velouté, Crispy Garlic
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated, minimalist composition featuring twelve perfectly seared scallops arranged artfully on a large, polished white stone sharing platter. Each scallop, with its golden-brown caramelized crust and translucent center, rests delicately on a flowing, organic pool of vibrant yellow Sweet Corn Velouté. The velouté is rich and smooth, forming a soft, inviting base. A scattering of golden-brown, finely crushed Crispy Garlic Crumble provides textural contrast, sprinkled precisely over the scallops and around the velouté. Delicate trails of vivid green Chive Oil are artfully drizzled, adding a fresh aromatic and visual accent. The platter is set on a pristine white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a precisely folded white linen napkin. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft, intentional shadows, highlighting the contours and textures of the dish. The background is ultra-minimalist, emphasizing abundant negative space to showcase the dish as a culinary masterpiece of precision and restraint.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an elegant appetizer or amuse-bouche for a refined tasting menu.
Present on a large, unadorned sharing platter to encourage communal enjoyment.
instructions: Prepare Garlic Confit: Place 8-10 peeled garlic cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with olive oil. Simmer gently over very low heat for 30-40 minutes until garlic is very tender and golden. Do not brown. Cool garlic in oil.

Make Crispy Garlic Crumble: Remove 4-5 confit garlic cloves from oil. Reserve oil. Thinly slice the selected confit garlic cloves. Heat a small non-stick pan over medium heat. Fry sliced confit garlic until golden brown and crispy. Remove with slotted spoon. Drain on paper towel. Lightly crush into a crumble. Season with a pinch of salt.

Prepare Sweet Corn Velouté: Finely dice the shallot. Melt 20g butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add diced shallot. Cook until translucent, about 2 minutes. Add corn kernels and vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5-7 minutes until corn is tender. Add heavy cream. Simmer for 2 minutes.

Blend Velouté: Transfer corn mixture to a high-speed blender. Blend until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Press solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Season velouté with salt and white pepper. Keep warm over low heat.

Make Chive Oil: Blanch chives in boiling water for 10 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice water bath. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water. Blend blanched chives with 20ml olive oil until smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve or coffee filter for a clear oil. Set aside.

Sear Scallops: Pat scallops very dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and white pepper. Heat a large heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat. Add 10ml olive oil and 40g butter. Once butter foams, add scallops in a single layer. Do not overcrowd. Sear for 2 minutes per side until deep golden brown and caramelized. Scallops should be translucent in the center.

Plate and Serve: Ladle a generous pool of warm Sweet Corn Velouté onto the center of a large sharing platter. Arrange the 12 seared scallops artfully on top of the velouté. Sprinkle Crispy Garlic Crumble over and around the scallops. Drizzle Chive Oil in delicate lines or dots around the velouté and scallops. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Spanish chicken and rice served in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. The rice is moist and fluid, colored a vibrant golden-orange from the smoked paprika and broth. Thick 4cm chunks of seared chicken thighs are nestled into the rice, showing a crisp, dark golden-brown exterior. Small dices of softened red bell pepper and translucent onions are evenly distributed throughout the grains. The dish is finished with a scatter of bright green chopped parsley. A single yellow lemon wedge sits on the side of the plate. The background features a rustic wooden table, a folded white cotton napkin, and natural side-lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in a traditional terracotta cazuela
Accompany with crusty bread and aioli
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine like Albariño

ingredients.name: Chicken thighs, boneless, cut into 4cm chunks

instructions: Season chicken chunks with salt, pepper, and half the paprika.
Heat olive oil in a wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Brown chicken chunks for 5 minutes until golden. Remove from pan.
Add onion and red pepper to the same pan. Sauté until softened.
Stir in garlic and remaining paprika. Cook for 1 minute.
Add rice. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken chunks to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Simmer uncovered for 18 minutes. Do not stir.
Verify chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove from heat. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Garnish with parsley and serve with lemon wedges.
notes: Use short-grain rice to ensure the correct starchy consistency.
Avoid stirring the rice once the broth is added to allow a slight crust to form.
Ensure the broth is hot before adding it to the pan to maintain cooking temperature.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Beef with Pastis and Swiss Chard
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Braised Beef with Pastis and Swiss Chard is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The composition is balanced and inviting. Two or three large, irregular chunks of dark, tender braised beef, approximately 5 cm each, are placed slightly off-center. A rich, glossy, dark brown sauce, reduced from the braising liquid, is generously spooned over and around the beef, pooling slightly on the plate. Beside the beef, a vibrant pile of emerald green Swiss chard leaves, lightly wilted from sautéing, provides a contrasting color and texture. The chard maintains some of its natural crinkle and volume. The overall presentation is natural and organic, with moderate negative space. The dish sits on a simple wooden table surface, suggesting a modern bistro setting. A neatly folded cotton napkin and polished silver flatware are placed to the side. Natural, even lighting highlights the food's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the sauce.
Pair with a glass of red wine, such as a Côtes du Rhône or Cabernet Sauvignon.

ingredients.name: Swiss chard
ingredients.quantity: 2 bunches (approx. 500 g), stems removed, leaves roughly chopped

instructions: Preheat oven to 160°C.
Pat beef chunks dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef in batches until deeply browned on all sides. Remove beef from pot.
Add diced onion, carrots, and celery to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add minced garlic and tomato paste. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in Pastis. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Cook until liquid is almost evaporated.
Return beef to the pot. Add Worcestershire sauce, beef stock, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf.
Bring liquid to a simmer. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 2.5 to 3 hours, or until beef is fork-tender.
Remove beef from pot. Strain braising liquid through a fine-mesh sieve into a saucepan. Discard solids.
Skim any fat from the braising liquid. Reduce liquid over medium-high heat until it thickens slightly into a rich sauce. Season with salt and pepper.
While sauce reduces, heat a separate pan with a splash of olive oil. Sauté chopped Swiss chard leaves until wilted, about 3-5 minutes. Season with salt.
Serve beef chunks with reduced sauce and sautéed Swiss chard.
notes: Browning the beef thoroughly is crucial for deep flavor.
The sauce can be made ahead and reheated.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Saffron Risotto, Garlic Jus
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white bone china plate cradles a masterfully composed individual serving. At its heart, a flowing, golden-yellow pool of creamy saffron risotto, its al dente grains hinting at perfect texture, spreads organically across the plate. Perched elegantly upon or beside the risotto are two or three thick, succulent pieces of pan-seared chicken breast, their skin rendered to a deep, lustrous golden-brown crisp, contrasting beautifully with the tender, white interior. Each chicken piece is a substantial, unsliced chunk, showcasing impeccable cooking. A glossy, rich amber garlic jus is artfully drizzled around the components, creating delicate pools and streaks that catch the light. A sparse scattering of vibrant green, finely minced chives provides a precise pop of color and freshness. The plate is surrounded by abundant negative space, highlighting the dish's sophisticated simplicity. The setting features a cool, veined white Carrara marble surface, a precisely folded white linen napkin, and subtle, professional lighting casting gentle shadows, creating an ultra-minimalist, luxury dining experience.

ingredients.name: Garlic cloves
ingredients.quantity: 6, 4 crushed for jus, 2 minced for risotto

instructions: Prepare Garlic Jus: Crush 4 garlic cloves. Heat 10ml olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Add crushed garlic and 1 thyme sprig. Sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Do not brown. Deglaze with 50ml white wine. Reduce by half. Add 200ml chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 15-20 minutes until slightly thickened and flavorful. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Discard solids. Return strained jus to clean saucepan. Keep warm.

Prepare Saffron Risotto: Heat 20ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium heat. Add diced shallots and 2 minced garlic cloves. Sauté until translucent, 3-4 minutes. Add Arborio rice. Toast, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes until edges are translucent. Pour in remaining 50ml white wine. Stir until completely absorbed. Add a ladle of warm chicken stock. Stir continuously until absorbed. Continue adding stock one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. After 15 minutes, add steeped saffron and its liquid. Continue stirring and adding stock. Cook for 18-20 minutes total, or until rice is creamy and al dente. Remove from heat. Stir in 40g cold butter and grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Season with salt and pepper. Stir vigorously (mantecatura) until creamy and cohesive. Cover and let rest 2 minutes. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.

Cook Chicken Breast: Pat chicken breasts dry thoroughly with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper on both sides. Heat a large, oven-safe skillet (cast iron recommended) over medium-high heat. Add 10ml olive oil. Place chicken breasts skin-side down in the hot skillet. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken breasts. Add 20g butter and 2 thyme sprigs to the pan. Baste chicken with melted butter and pan juices. Transfer skillet to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from oven. Rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes before slicing. Slice each breast into 2-3 thick pieces/medallions.

Assemble Dish: Reheat jus gently if needed. Whisk in remaining 20g cold butter until glossy. Spoon a generous portion of creamy saffron risotto onto the center of each plate, allowing it to spread naturally. Arrange 2-3 thick pieces of pan-seared chicken breast artfully on top of or beside the risotto. Do not fan slices. Drizzle garlic jus around and over the chicken and risotto. Garnish sparingly with finely minced chives. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Parsnip Purée, Chicken Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an elegantly plated Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme. The chicken supreme, with its perfectly golden and crispy skin, is presented whole as the focal point, positioned slightly off-center on a pristine, round white bone china plate with a subtle, thin rim. Adjacent to the chicken is a meticulously placed, silky smooth quenelle or organic swirl of pale yellow parsnip purée, its texture gleaming. A rich, deep amber chicken jus forms a delicate, glossy pool or a precise, artful drizzle around the main components, catching the light. The dish is garnished with a few precisely placed, vibrant green microgreens or finely snipped chives, adding a touch of color and freshness without clutter. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the dish's minimalist and architectural precision. The plate rests on a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, complemented by a neatly folded, pristine white linen napkin in a precise triangle. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the textures and contours of the food, set against an ultra-minimalist background to ensure the dish remains the sole focus.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken supremes dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Add a tablespoon of neutral oil. Place chicken supremes skin-side down. Sear for 8-10 minutes until skin is deeply golden and crispy.

Flip chicken. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 12-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and rest on a cutting board, tented loosely with foil, for 10 minutes.

While chicken roasts, prepare parsnip purée. Peel parsnips. Cut into 2cm thick chunks. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, until very tender.

Drain parsnips thoroughly. Transfer to a blender. Add 50g butter and cream. Blend until completely smooth. Season with salt. For ultimate smoothness, pass purée through a fine-mesh sieve or tamis. Keep warm.
To make the jus, pour off excess fat from the chicken pan, leaving a thin layer. Return pan to medium heat. Add white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce by half.

Add diced shallot, crushed garlic, and thyme sprig to the pan. Sauté for 1-2 minutes until fragrant. Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat and gently simmer for 10-15 minutes, until liquid has reduced by two-thirds and is slightly syrupy.

Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean small saucepan, pressing on solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Return jus to low heat. Whisk in 20g cold butter until melted and incorporated, creating a glossy emulsion. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
To plate, spoon a deliberate, artistic swirl or quenelle of parsnip purée onto one side of each warm plate. Place a rested chicken supreme next to the purée, ensuring the crispy skin faces up.
Spoon a precise pool or drizzle of the chicken jus around the chicken and purée. Garnish with a few tiny microgreens or finely snipped chives placed with intention.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Gnocchi Salad with Roasted Cherry Tomatoes and Garlic Vinaigrette
recipes.visual_description: The Potato Gnocchi Salad presents an artful, flowing composition on a pristine white bone china plate set on a premium grey veined marble surface. Golden-brown seared potato gnocchi pieces, crisp on the exterior and tender within, are elegantly scattered. Alongside, vibrant halved roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly blistered and caramelized, add bursts of deep red. Fresh, delicate mixed baby salad greens provide a contrasting verdant backdrop, creating an organic arrangement. A glistening garlic and basil vinaigrette lightly coats the elements, enhancing their colors. The plate features abundant negative space, highlighting the precise placement of each component. A few crispy basil leaves serve as a refined garnish. The scene is bathed in dramatic professional lighting with subtle shadows, ensuring a sophisticated, ultra-minimalist presentation.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Halve cherry tomatoes. Slice 2 garlic cloves thinly. Toss tomatoes and sliced garlic with 15 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 20-25 minutes until softened and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Boil potatoes in their skins until very tender, about 25-30 minutes. Drain and peel immediately while hot. Pass potatoes through a potato ricer onto a clean work surface.
Form a well in the center of the riced potatoes. Add flour, egg yolk, a pinch of salt. Gently mix with a fork, then knead briefly until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix.

Divide dough into several portions. Roll each portion into a long rope, 1.5 cm thick. Cut ropes into 2 cm pieces. Roll each piece lightly on a gnocchi board or fork tines to create ridges. Place gnocchi on a lightly floured tray.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil. Cook gnocchi in batches until they float to the surface, about 2-3 minutes. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain well.

Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Finely chop basil leaves. In a small bowl, whisk together 45 ml olive oil, white wine vinegar, minced garlic, chopped basil, salt, and pepper to create the vinaigrette.

Heat a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat with a drizzle of olive oil. Add cooked gnocchi in a single layer. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly crisp. Work in batches to avoid overcrowding.
To serve, arrange seared gnocchi, roasted cherry tomatoes, and mixed baby salad greens artistically on individual plates. Drizzle generously with the garlic and basil vinaigrette. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Orecchiette with Braised Beef Cheek and San Marzano Tomato Sugo
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Orecchiette with Braised Beef Cheek and San Marzano Tomato Sugo is presented in a deep, clean white porcelain bowl. Al dente orecchiette are coated in a rich, rustic red San Marzano tomato sugo. Generous chunks of dark brown, tender shredded beef cheek are artfully nestled among the pasta, creating a comforting yet refined composition. A vibrant sprinkle of bright green gremolata, featuring finely chopped parsley and lemon zest, adds a fresh color contrast and aromatic lift. A light dusting of pale yellow grated Parmesan cheese finishes the dish. The pasta is naturally mounded, showcasing its inviting texture. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded linen napkin and a silver fork. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's rich colors and textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for 'scarpetta' (mopping up the sauce)
Offer additional grated Parmesan or Pecorino cheese at the table
instructions: Preheat oven to 150°C. Season beef cheeks generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot over medium-high heat. Sear beef cheeks on all sides until deeply browned. Remove beef and set aside.
Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto) to the pot. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Deglaze the pot, scraping up any browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Crush San Marzano tomatoes by hand and add to the pot. Add beef stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return seared beef cheeks to the pot. Ensure beef is mostly submerged. Cover the pot tightly.
Transfer pot to the preheated oven. Braise for 3 to 4 hours, or until beef cheeks are fork-tender.
Remove beef cheeks from the pot. Discard rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Shred beef using two forks. Return shredded beef to the sauce.
Simmer sauce on stovetop over medium heat for 10-15 minutes to reduce slightly and thicken to desired consistency.
While sauce simmers, cook orecchiette pasta in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml of pasta cooking water.
Drain pasta. Add pasta to the pot with the beef sugo. Toss to combine. Add a splash of reserved pasta water if needed to loosen the sauce.
Prepare gremolata: Combine finely chopped parsley, lemon zest, and minced garlic in a small bowl.
Serve pasta immediately. Garnish each portion with a sprinkle of gremolata and freshly grated Parmesan cheese.

recipes.recipe_name: Tuscan Chicken & Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Tuscan Chicken & Sun-Dried Tomato Pasta is artfully presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple light wooden table. Golden-brown pan-seared chicken breast medallions, cut into thick, irregular chunks, are nestled among al dente penne pasta. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, light orange sauce, vibrant with halved cherry tomatoes and wilted dark green spinach leaves. Sliced sun-dried tomatoes add deeper red notes and texture. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated white Parmesan cheese covers the dish, with bright green chopped fresh basil leaves scattered over the top as a final garnish. The composition is organic and flowing, with moderate negative space. Beside the plate rests a folded white cotton napkin and classic silver flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty focaccia bread
Pair with a dry white wine like Vermentino or Pinot Grigio
Finish the meal with a classic Italian espresso
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken 6-8 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked to 75°C. Remove chicken. Rest 5 minutes. Slice into thick medallions.
Add diced onion to pan. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in sun-dried tomatoes and halved cherry tomatoes. Cook 3 minutes until cherry tomatoes soften slightly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 5 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Add fresh spinach. Cook 1-2 minutes until wilted.
Meanwhile, cook penne pasta according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 60ml pasta water.
Add drained pasta and 60g grated Parmesan to the sauce. Toss to combine. Add reserved pasta water if needed for desired consistency.
Return sliced chicken medallions to the pan. Toss gently to coat. Cook 1 minute to heat through.
Serve immediately. Garnish with remaining grated Parmesan and fresh basil.
notes: Ensure chicken is cooked through to 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust sauce consistency with reserved pasta water as needed.
Use fresh, quality Parmesan cheese for best flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Breast, Slow-Roasted Tomato, Garlic Jus, Herb Tuile
recipes.visual_description: The dish is plated on a large, pristine round white bone china plate, emphasizing negative space. An organic pool of shimmering amber garlic jus anchors the center. A thick, perfectly seared chicken breast, sliced into two robust angled pieces, rests on the jus, showcasing its crispy golden skin and succulent interior. Around the chicken, five slow-roasted cherry tomato halves are artfully scattered. A delicate, irregular herb tuile, translucent and crisp, leans gracefully against the chicken, adding height and texture. A small, vibrant cluster of fresh micro basil is precisely placed, providing a pop of green. The composition is asymmetrical and refined. The setting features grey-veined Carrara marble, a folded white linen napkin, and minimalist silver flatware under dramatic, focused lighting.

ingredients.name: Micro Herbs (e.g., micro basil or chervil)

instructions: Preheat oven to 120°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, pinch of salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray. Roast for 45-60 minutes until slightly shriveled.

Peel garlic cloves from 1 head. Place cloves in a small saucepan. Cover with 30ml olive oil. Cook over very low heat for 20-30 minutes until cloves are tender. Do not brown. Strain cloves, reserving oil. Mash 2-3 confit cloves into a paste for the jus.

In a saucepan, combine chicken stock, thyme, and rosemary. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently until liquid reduces by half (approx. 250ml). Skim any foam. Stir in mashed garlic confit paste. If using, deglaze the chicken searing pan with white wine after searing, then add the wine reduction to the jus. Strain jus through a fine-mesh sieve. Keep warm.

Pat chicken breasts very dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add 10ml olive oil. Place chicken breasts skin-side down. Sear for 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden brown and crispy. Flip chicken. Add 30g unsalted butter to the pan. Baste chicken continuously with melted butter for 5-7 minutes. Transfer chicken to a baking tray. Finish in a preheated oven at 180°C for 5-8 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

In a bowl, whisk together 50g flour, 100ml water, 30g melted unsalted butter, and a pinch of salt until smooth. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Pour a small amount of batter (approx. 15ml) into the pan, swirling to create a very thin, irregular circle. Cook until edges are crispy and golden, and center is dry. Carefully lift with a spatula. Place on paper towel to drain. Repeat for 4 tuiles. Garnish tuiles with a few micro herbs immediately after removing from pan, pressing gently to adhere.

Spoon a pool of warm garlic jus onto the center of each plate. Slice each rested chicken breast into 2-3 thick, diagonal pieces. Arrange chicken pieces artfully on top of the jus. Scatter 5-6 slow-roasted cherry tomato halves around the chicken. Lean one herb tuile against the chicken. Garnish with a small cluster of fresh micro herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Roasted Chicken and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of hearty roasted chicken and root vegetables is presented on a simple, round off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown roasted chicken thigh sits prominently, its skin slightly crispy. Around the chicken, thick chunks of orange sweet potato display tender, caramelized edges from roasting. Vibrant orange carrot batons are interspersed, showing a slight char and tender texture. Dark green beans, roasted until tender-crisp, add a contrasting color and texture, naturally scattered among the other ingredients. The components are arranged casually, touching and overlapping, filling the plate without overcrowding. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table. A standard metal fork and knife are placed beside the plate. A casually folded beige cloth napkin rests nearby. Warm, inviting lighting from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting appeal. The background is simple and slightly blurred, suggesting a relaxed, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Carrots
ingredients.quantity: 4 medium (about 300g), peeled, cut into 2cm thick batons

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season chicken with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and rosemary.
In a large bowl, toss sweet potato chunks and carrot batons with 15ml olive oil, 2g salt, and 1g pepper.
Spread seasoned vegetables in a single layer on a large baking sheet.
Arrange seasoned chicken thighs among the vegetables on the baking sheet.
Roast for 25 minutes.
Remove baking sheet from oven. Add green beans to the baking sheet. Drizzle remaining 15ml olive oil over green beans. Toss gently to coat.
Return baking sheet to oven. Continue roasting for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C and vegetables are tender.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Aromatic Mushroom Consommé with Crispy Shallots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of crystal-clear, golden-amber mushroom consommé is presented in a deep, wide, elegant white bone china bowl with a subtle rim. Delicate, precisely cut mushrooms (thinly sliced shiitake, delicate oyster strips, and small enoki clusters) are artfully arranged at the bottom of the bowl, visible through the translucent broth. A few precise drops of vibrant yellow lime-infused oil float on the surface, creating a subtle sheen. A small, artful cluster of golden-brown crispy shallots is placed near the edge of the bowl, offering a textural contrast. A single, fresh sprig of micro-cilantro or micro-Thai basil rests delicately on the consommé surface. The bowl sits on a premium dark polished wooden table. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, is placed to the side. The background is ultra-minimalist with abundant negative space, highlighting the dish as the sole focus. Dramatic professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing depth and elegance.

ingredients.name: Neutral oil (e.g., grapeseed or rice bran)

instructions: Clean mushrooms. Slice 200g mushrooms thinly for broth. Reserve remaining 200g. Cut reserved shiitake into thin slices, oyster into delicate strips, enoki into small clusters.
Slice 100g shallots thinly. Slice garlic. Bruise lemongrass stalks. Slice galangal. Tear kaffir lime leaves.
In a large pot, heat 15ml neutral oil. Add sliced shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal, and kaffir lime leaves. Sauté until fragrant, about 3 minutes.
Add 200g sliced mushrooms to the pot. Sauté 5 minutes until softened.
Pour in 1.5L filtered water. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat. Simmer gently for 45 minutes to extract flavor. Do not boil vigorously.
Strain the broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Strain again through cheesecloth for a crystal-clear consommé. Season with soy sauce, palm sugar, and salt to taste. Keep warm.

For crispy shallots: Thinly slice remaining 50g shallots. Heat 150ml neutral oil in a small saucepan to 160°C. Fry shallots in batches until golden brown and crispy. Remove with a slotted spoon. Drain on paper towels. Season lightly with salt.
For lime-infused oil: Zest half a lime. Combine zest with 35ml neutral oil. Gently warm over low heat for 5 minutes. Do not fry. Strain the oil to remove zest.

To serve: Place reserved cooked mushrooms (shiitake, oyster, enoki) artfully at the bottom of each warm soup bowl. Ladle hot consommé over the mushrooms. Drizzle a few drops of lime-infused oil onto the surface. Garnish with a small cluster of crispy shallots and a sprig of micro-cilantro or micro-Thai basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Spiced Apple Maple Layer Cake with Coconut Cream Frosting
recipes.visual_description: A single, elegant slice of two-layer cake is centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The cake layers are a warm, golden-brown, revealing a tender crumb studded with small, softened apple cubes. A generous, smooth layer of creamy white coconut cream frosting separates the cake layers and coats the top. A delicate drizzle of amber maple syrup cascades over the top and down the sides of the slice. The plate is garnished simply with a light dusting of ground cinnamon and a small, vibrant green mint leaf. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate, all bathed in soft, natural, even lighting.

ingredients.name: Medium apples (e.g., Gala, Honeycrisp), peeled, cored, diced into 1 cm cubes

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 15 cm round cake pans. Line bottoms with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together flour, granulated sugar, baking powder, baking soda, 5 g cinnamon, and salt.
In a separate bowl, whisk together 100 ml maple syrup, applesauce, plant milk, melted coconut oil, and 5 ml vanilla extract.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.

In a small saucepan, combine diced apples, remaining 50 ml maple syrup, and remaining 2 g cinnamon. Cook over medium heat for 5-7 minutes, until apples are slightly softened but still hold their shape.
Fold the cooked apple mixture gently into the cake batter.
Divide batter evenly between prepared cake pans. Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans for 10 minutes. Invert onto a wire rack to cool completely.
For the frosting, scoop the solid coconut cream from the chilled can into a large bowl. Discard any liquid.
Add powdered sugar and 5 ml vanilla extract to the solid coconut cream. Beat with an electric mixer on high speed until light and fluffy, about 3-5 minutes.
Once cakes are completely cool, place one layer on a serving plate. Spread half of the coconut cream frosting evenly over the top.
Place the second cake layer on top. Spread the remaining frosting over the top of the cake.
Serve immediately or refrigerate.
notes: Ensure coconut cream is thoroughly chilled overnight to allow the solid cream to separate from the liquid, which is crucial for whipping a firm frosting.
Do not overmix the cake batter; mix only until ingredients are just combined to keep the cake tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & Roasted Garlic Salad
recipes.visual_description: A minimalistic and vibrant Fermented Tomato & Roasted Garlic Salad is presented on a round, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The plate, resting on a light, reclaimed wood table, is purposefully uncluttered, allowing the natural beauty of the ingredients to shine. Halved fermented tomatoes, their skins slightly softened and vibrant red, are loosely scattered across the plate, interspersed with fresh, thinly sliced rounds of ripe red and yellow tomatoes for textural contrast. A creamy, golden-brown roasted garlic dressing is artfully drizzled over the tomatoes, coating them lightly. Scattered across the top are delicate, irregular shavings of off-white Parmesan cheese, adding a contrasting texture and a pop of lighter color. Fresh, roughly chopped basil leaves and small oregano sprigs are nestled among the tomatoes, providing bursts of green and aromatic freshness. The arrangement is organic and unforced, with ample negative space around the central composition. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish from the side, enhancing the colors and subtle textures. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone is casually folded beside the plate. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural greenery suggesting an eco-conscious setting.
instructions: Wash tomatoes. Halve small tomatoes. Place in a clean 1-liter jar.
Dissolve 15g sea salt in 500ml filtered water to make a brine. Pour brine over tomatoes, ensuring they are fully submerged.

Use a fermentation weight or small clean bag filled with water to keep tomatoes submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 1-2 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily.

Preheat oven to 180°C. Place unpeeled garlic cloves on a small baking tray. Drizzle with 10ml olive oil. Roast for 25-30 minutes until very soft. Let cool. Squeeze softened garlic pulp from skins into a small bowl.
Combine roasted garlic pulp, remaining 90ml olive oil, and 30ml of the tomato fermentation liquid in a small blender or food processor. Blend until smooth. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Drain fermented tomatoes. Combine fermented tomatoes with fresh basil and oregano in a large bowl.
Arrange the tomato mixture on a serving platter or individual plates. Drizzle generously with the roasted garlic dressing.
Using a vegetable peeler, shave thin slices of parmesan cheese directly over the salad. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Tagliatelle with Creamy Potato-Parmesan Sauce and Crispy Prosciutto
recipes.visual_description: Tagliatelle pasta is artfully coiled into a refined mound within a clean white porcelain pasta bowl. It is generously coated in a luxurious, velvety pale-yellow potato-Parmesan sauce, which provides a rich, creamy texture without being overly thick. Scattered across the top are crisp, golden-brown irregular bits of pan-fried prosciutto, offering a delightful textural contrast.
