Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's rich colors and textures, creating an inviting, refined presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty baguette slices for dipping in the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
Pair with a glass of the same dry red wine used in the reduction.
instructions: Pat beef medallions dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Sear beef medallions for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare. Adjust time for desired doneness.
Remove beef from pan. Set aside on a plate, tent with foil to rest.
Reduce heat to medium. Add minced shallots to the same pan. Sauté until softened, about 2 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce wine by half. Add beef broth and thyme sprigs. Simmer until sauce thickens slightly, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs. Whisk in cold butter, one cube at a time, until sauce is glossy and emulsified.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Spoon red wine reduction over beef medallions. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Potato & Dill Bites
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a light, reclaimed wood board. Handcrafted ceramic plates in earthy cream tones hold individual servings. Each "bite" features a vibrant green cucumber round as the base. Neatly mounded on top is a small portion of the potato salad. The potatoes are soft white cubes, subtly coated in a creamy, off-white dressing, flecked with bright green dill. Small, translucent cubes of cucumber are interspersed, adding texture. The overall color palette is natural and inviting: crisp green, soft white, and hints of creamy beige. Minimalistic presentation emphasizes the fresh ingredients. Negative space surrounds each bite, creating a clean, unforced composition. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures. A few stray dill sprigs are casually placed on the board as a natural garnish.
instructions: Wash potatoes. Boil whole with skins until tender. Cool completely.
Dice cooled potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Slice half the cucumber into thin rounds for serving. Set aside.
Dice remaining cucumber into small cubes.
In a bowl, combine diced potatoes and diced cucumber.
Mince garlic clove.
Finely chop fresh dill.
In a separate bowl, whisk together yogurt, sour cream, minced garlic, apple cider vinegar, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Pour dressing over potato and cucumber mixture. Add chopped dill. Gently fold to combine.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to allow flavors to meld and slight fermentation to occur. Overnight is ideal.
To serve, spoon potato mixture onto individual cucumber slices.
notes: For enhanced fermentation, allow the dressed potato salad to sit at room temperature for 4-6 hours before refrigerating. This promotes beneficial bacteria.
Use organic, locally sourced ingredients when possible.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Chicken Roulade with Black Garlic Aioli
recipes.visual_description: Thick, seared medallions of golden-brown smoked chicken roulade are artfully arranged on a smooth, cool white Carrara marble slab, creating an organic, flowing composition. Each medallion showcases a tender, moist interior. Alongside, small, precise dollops of creamy, off-white black garlic aioli provide a subtle color contrast. Scattered over the dish are irregular, amber-gold shards of shatteringly crisp chicken skin, adding textural intrigue and a rich hue. A delicate sprinkle of vibrant green, finely minced chives provides a fresh pop of color and aromatic lift. The presentation emphasizes abundant negative space, with each component intentionally placed to create a sophisticated, minimalist aesthetic. The scene is bathed in dramatic professional lighting, casting subtle shadows that highlight the textures, set against an ultra-minimalist background.
instructions: Prepare chicken breast: Carefully debone chicken breasts, keeping skin attached. Pound breasts gently to even thickness (about 1 cm). Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Make chicken farce: Dice chicken thigh into small pieces. Blend chicken thigh, heavy cream, and egg white in a food processor until smooth paste forms. Season with salt and pepper.
Form roulade: Spread farce evenly over pounded chicken breast. Roll tightly into a cylinder. Secure with butcher's twine.

Cook roulade: Preheat oven to 120°C. Place roulade on a wire rack over a baking sheet. Smoke roulade for 20 minutes (if using a smoker). Alternatively, use liquid smoke sparingly on the chicken. Then, roast until internal temperature reaches 75°C, approximately 30-40 minutes depending on thickness. Let rest 10 minutes.

Crisp chicken skin: Carefully remove skin from roulade after cooking and resting. Place skin between two sheets of parchment paper and two baking sheets. Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until deeply golden and crisp. Break into irregular shards.
Make black garlic aioli: Peel black garlic cloves. Mash with a fork until smooth. Whisk black garlic paste into mayonnaise. Add lemon juice. Season with salt and pepper.
Prepare garnish: Finely mince fresh chives.

Slice and serve: Remove twine from roulade. Slice roulade into 2 cm thick medallions. Arrange medallions on a sharing platter. Dollop black garlic aioli alongside. Scatter crispy chicken skin shards and minced chives over and around.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Bell Pepper and Mustard Bread Bake
recipes.visual_description: The Savory Bell Pepper and Mustard Bread Bake is presented in a well-used, rectangular ceramic baking dish, slightly rustic with natural imperfections. A single generous portion is served on a round, everyday ceramic plate with a subtle off-white glaze. The bake features a golden-brown, slightly crusty top from the toasted bread cubes and melted cheddar cheese. Beneath, the interior reveals a soft, custardy texture with vibrant diced red and yellow bell peppers and small diced onion pieces interspersed throughout. The mustard subtly tints the custardy base a pale yellow. There are no garnishes; the dish appears as if just scooped from the communal baking dish onto a family plate. The plate sits on a well-worn wooden dining table. A simple, folded cloth napkin and a standard fork are casually placed beside the plate. Warm, cozy lighting from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, creating a lived-in, comfortable atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Lightly grease a 20x30 cm baking dish.
Cut stale bread into 2.5 cm cubes. Spread bread cubes on a baking sheet. Toast in the oven for 10 minutes until slightly dry.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add diced onion and bell peppers. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the skillet. Cook for 1 minute more. Remove skillet from heat.
In a large bowl, whisk eggs, milk, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper until well combined.
Add toasted bread cubes, sautéed vegetables, and shredded cheese to the egg mixture. Stir gently to ensure all bread is coated.
Pour the mixture into the prepared baking dish. Press down gently to level.
Bake for 35-45 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let the bake rest for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: This dish is excellent for meal preparation and can be reheated easily.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Sausage Penne with Roasted Carrots
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Creamy Chicken and Sausage Penne is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The penne pasta is coated in a rich, creamy, pale yellow sauce, generously interspersed with golden-brown, irregular chunks of seared chicken and rustic, browned pieces of Italian sausage. Bright orange roasted carrot batons are strategically placed among the pasta, adding vibrant color and texture. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan cheese provide a fresh finish. The dish is arranged naturally, allowing the creamy sauce to flow. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, a white linen napkin beside the plate, and standard polished silver flatware. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting colors against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Cut carrots into 2 cm batons. Toss with 10 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 20 minutes until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook penne according to package directions until al dente. Drain, reserving 100 ml pasta water.
Cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Remove sausage from casings, break into 2 cm pieces.

Heat 10 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides and cooked to 75°C internal temperature. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add sausage pieces to the same skillet. Cook, breaking up with a spoon, until browned and cooked through. Remove sausage from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add remaining 10 ml olive oil to skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese and mayonnaise until smooth and combined.
Add cooked penne, seared chicken chunks, and cooked sausage pieces to the sauce. Toss to coat evenly. If needed, add reserved pasta water to reach desired consistency.
Chop fresh parsley. Stir half into the pasta. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley and roasted carrot batons.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Watermelon & Herb Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A casual wooden cutting board, well-worn, holds a generous arrangement of Roasted Watermelon & Herb Crostini. Each crostini features a golden-brown, thinly sliced baguette base, toasted to a light crisp. Piled atop are slightly caramelized, 2 cm diced watermelon cubes, their vibrant red softened to a deeper hue from roasting. Interspersed among the watermelon are small pieces of finely minced garlic, dark green flecks of fresh thyme leaves, and slender, deep green fragments of chopped rosemary. A light sheen of olive oil coats the roasted fruit and herbs, reflecting the warm kitchen light. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with crostini touching and overlapping slightly, suggesting a bountiful home snack. A few stray fresh thyme sprigs are casually placed on the board, adding a touch of fresh green. The scene is set on a simple, well-used wooden dining table, with a casually folded off-white linen napkin visible in the background, creating a relaxed and homely atmosphere. Warm, soft light from an overhead kitchen fixture illuminates the dish, highlighting the inviting textures and colors.

ingredients.name: Watermelon
ingredients.quantity: 500 g, rind removed, cut into 2 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Fresh Rosemary
ingredients.quantity: 1 sprig, leaves picked and finely chopped

ingredients.name: Baguette
ingredients.quantity: 1 (approx. 250 g), sliced diagonally into 1.5 cm thick pieces

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Combine watermelon cubes, minced garlic, thyme leaves, chopped rosemary, and 30 ml olive oil in a bowl. Toss to coat.
Spread watermelon mixture in a single layer on a baking tray.
Roast for 20-25 minutes. Watermelon should be slightly caramelized and tender.
While watermelon roasts, arrange baguette slices on a separate baking tray.
Drizzle baguette slices with remaining 30 ml olive oil.
Bake baguette for 8-10 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Remove watermelon and baguette from oven.
Season roasted watermelon with salt and pepper.
Spoon roasted watermelon mixture onto toasted baguette slices.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary Thyme Potato & Bell Pepper Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A collection of 8-12 elegant Rosemary Thyme Potato & Bell Pepper Crostini are artfully arranged on a light wooden serving board. Each crostini features a perfectly golden, crisp baguette slice as its base. A creamy, off-white spicy garlic aioli, with subtle flecks of red from hot sauce and green from herbs, is spread evenly over the bread. Piled on top are small, roughly 1.5 cm roasted potato cubes, showcasing a slightly browned, crisp exterior, intermingled with vibrant 1 cm diced red and yellow bell peppers, tender-crisp from sautéing. A delicate cluster of bright green microgreens crowns each canapé, adding a fresh, contrasting pop of color and texture. The overall presentation is clean and professional, with moderate negative space, highlighting the rich colors and varying textures of the plant-based ingredients. The scene is set on a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting, conveying a modern bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as an appetizer for a casual gathering.
Offer alongside other small bites on a charcuterie-style board.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Wash and dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, half of the fresh rosemary and thyme (chopped), salt, and black pepper.
Spread potatoes in a single layer on the prepared baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and golden brown. Flip halfway through.
While potatoes roast, dice red and yellow bell peppers into 1 cm cubes. Mince 1 clove of garlic.
Heat 10 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add diced bell peppers and minced garlic. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until peppers are tender-crisp. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Slice baguette into 1.5 cm thick rounds. Brush lightly with remaining 5 ml olive oil. Toast in a dry pan or under a grill until lightly golden and crisp.
For the spicy garlic aioli, mince remaining 2 cloves of garlic. Finely chop remaining fresh thyme and rosemary.
In a small bowl, combine vegan mayonnaise, minced garlic, chopped herbs, hot sauce, lemon juice, and a pinch of salt. Mix well until smooth.
To assemble, spread a generous layer of spicy garlic aioli onto each toasted crostini.
Top each crostini with a small mound of roasted potatoes and sautéed bell peppers.
Garnish each canapé with a delicate cluster of microgreens. Arrange 8-12 pieces on a serving platter.

recipes.recipe_name: Homestyle Beef and Mushroom Stroganoff
recipes.visual_description: A single, homely portion of Beef and Mushroom Stroganoff is presented on a simple, slightly off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table. The dish features a generous mound of creamy, rich brown beef and mushroom sauce, naturally coating tender beef batons and sliced earthy brown mushrooms. The sauce has a smooth, velvety texture. Beneath the stroganoff, a bed of pale yellow, al dente egg noodles is visible, absorbing the sauce. A sprinkle of bright green, chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top, adding a pop of color. The arrangement is casual and organic, as if served directly from a pot onto a family dinner plate. A standard silver fork rests beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by warm, cozy kitchen lighting, creating a lived-in, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen.
instructions: Slice beef sirloin into thin strips, approximately 5 cm long and 1 cm thick. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml vegetable oil and 30 g butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef strips in batches until browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml vegetable oil and 30 g butter to the pan. Reduce heat to medium.
Add finely diced onion to the pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until mushrooms release their liquid and begin to brown, about 7-10 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms and onions. Stir constantly for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in beef broth, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Bring to a simmer, stirring until sauce thickens.
Return seared beef and any accumulated juices to the pan. Reduce heat to low.
Stir in sour cream until fully combined. Do not boil after adding sour cream.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Serve immediately over cooked egg noodles or rice. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato, Bell Pepper, and Crouton Warm Salad
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Potato, Bell Pepper, and Crouton Warm Salad is presented on a simple, slightly imperfect white ceramic dinner plate, placed on a well-used wooden dining table. Diced roasted potatoes and julienned red bell peppers, still warm, are casually mixed with fresh, vibrant green salad leaves. The components are naturally intertwined, with some overlapping, showcasing their varied textures and colors—golden-brown potatoes, bright red peppers, and deep green leaves. Crispy, golden-brown bread croutons are scattered generously on top, adding a textural contrast. The warm, slightly glossy dressing coats the ingredients, making them appear inviting. The scene is lit by warm, cozy kitchen light, with a casually placed cloth napkin nearby, evoking a comfortable, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere.

ingredients.name: Stale Bread
ingredients.quantity: 2 slices, crust removed, cubed into 1.5 cm pieces

ingredients.name: Fresh Thyme
ingredients.quantity: 2 sprigs, leaves picked (or 1 tsp dried thyme)

instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Toss diced potatoes and julienned bell pepper with 45 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on the baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.
While vegetables roast, heat 15 ml olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add bread cubes and cook, stirring frequently, until golden brown and crispy croutons form. Set aside.

In a small saucepan, combine 30 ml olive oil, red wine vinegar, minced garlic, thyme leaves, and hot sauce. Heat gently over low heat for 3-4 minutes, just until warmed through and fragrant. Do not boil.
In a large serving bowl, place the salad greens.
Add the warm roasted potatoes and bell pepper to the greens. Pour the warm dressing over the salad.
Toss gently to combine. Top with crispy croutons. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Greek Yogurt Chicken with Lemon Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Golden-brown roasted chicken chunks, tender and juicy, are arranged neatly. Alongside are perfectly roasted potato wedges, their skins slightly crisp and interiors fluffy, seasoned with herbs. A generous dollop of creamy white tzatziki sauce is placed beside the chicken, ready to be scooped. Fresh green oregano leaves are scattered lightly over the chicken and potatoes, and a bright yellow lemon wedge sits at the edge of the plate, offering a pop of color and freshness. The setting is a simple wooden table with natural, even lighting. A clean white linen napkin and silver flatware rest beside the plate. The overall presentation is inviting, natural, and authentically Greek, focusing on fresh ingredients and balanced textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple Greek salad of chopped cucumber, tomato, red onion, feta cheese, and Kalamata olives, dressed with olive oil and oregano.
Offer warm pita bread for scooping up the tzatziki and juices.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 5cm chunks. Place in a bowl.

For the marinade, finely mince 2 garlic cloves. Chop 10g fresh oregano. In a separate bowl, combine 100g Greek yogurt, juice of 1 lemon, minced garlic, chopped oregano, 5ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well.
Pour marinade over chicken. Toss to coat thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 4 hours.
Preheat oven to 200°C (392°F).
Wash and cut potatoes into 2-3cm wedges. Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Chop remaining 5g fresh oregano.
In a large bowl, toss potato wedges with 55ml olive oil, minced garlic, chopped oregano, salt, and pepper. Spread potatoes in a single layer on a large baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 20 minutes.
While potatoes roast, prepare tzatziki. Grate half a cucumber. Squeeze out excess water using a clean cloth or paper towel.

Finely chop fresh dill and fresh mint. In a bowl, combine remaining 150g Greek yogurt, grated cucumber, chopped dill, chopped mint, a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mix well. Refrigerate until serving.
After 20 minutes, remove potatoes from oven. Add marinated chicken chunks to the same baking tray, spreading them evenly among the potatoes.
Return tray to oven and roast for another 20-25 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and potatoes are tender and golden-brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken and potatoes immediately. Spoon a generous amount of tzatziki alongside. Garnish with fresh oregano sprigs and lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Stroganoff
recipes.visual_description: The Beef Stroganoff is presented as a single, hearty individual portion in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Tender beef strips, seared to a rich brown, are nestled within a creamy, golden-brown mushroom sauce. Sliced mushrooms, sautéed until caramelized, are visibly mixed throughout the dish. The sauce has a smooth, rich texture, generously coating the beef and mushrooms. A vibrant green sprinkle of freshly chopped dill garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, alongside a simple ceramic plate holding a modest mound of fluffy egg noodles, ready to be combined with the Stroganoff. Warm, inviting light from kitchen fixtures illuminates the scene, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere. A plain, light-colored cloth napkin is casually placed nearby. The overall presentation is comforting and unpretentious, typical of a home-cooked meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve over egg noodles, rice, or mashed potatoes.
Traditionally garnished with fresh dill or parsley.
instructions: Cut beef sirloin into 2cm strips. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear beef strips in batches until well browned on all sides. Do not overcrowd the pan. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion and sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add sliced mushrooms to the pan. Cook, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are tender and browned, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Sprinkle plain flour over the vegetables. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute to create a roux.
Gradually whisk in the beef broth until smooth. Bring the mixture to a simmer, stirring, until the sauce thickens.
Return the seared beef strips to the pan. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 5-7 minutes to allow flavors to meld.
Remove the pan from heat. Stir in the sour cream and Dijon mustard until well combined. Do not boil after adding sour cream to prevent curdling.
Taste the sauce and adjust seasoning with more salt and pepper if needed.
Serve the Beef Stroganoff hot over cooked egg noodles. Garnish each serving with chopped fresh dill.
notes: For best results, do not boil the sauce after adding the sour cream to prevent it from curdling.
Sear beef in batches to ensure browning and avoid steaming.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Chicken and Tomato Rice is presented in a shallow, wide ceramic bowl. A golden-brown, seared bone-in chicken thigh, with crispy skin, is nestled prominently on top of a vibrant orange-red bed of short-grain rice. The rice is tender, studded with soft, diced tomato pieces and flecks of minced garlic and onion. The grains are separate yet moist. Fresh, bright green chopped parsley is generously scattered over the chicken and rice, providing a contrasting color and fresh aroma. A bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the rim of the bowl, ready to be squeezed. The overall composition is rustic yet refined, showcasing the rich colors and textures of the dish. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and standard flatware. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve directly from the pan if serving family style, or in individual wide, shallow bowls.
Offer crusty bread to sop up the flavorful juices.
Serve with a simple green salad dressed with olive oil and vinegar.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, wide, shallow pan or paella pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 6-8 minutes until golden and crisp. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the pan. Cook for 5-7 minutes until softened, stirring occasionally.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Stir in diced tomatoes and saffron threads. Cook for 5 minutes, mashing tomatoes slightly, to form a sofrito.
Add rice to the pan. Stir for 1-2 minutes to coat rice grains evenly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the rice mixture.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan loosely or leave uncovered if using a traditional paella pan. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not stir excessively.
Remove from heat. Cover tightly with foil or a lid. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Avoid stirring the rice too much once the broth is added to allow the rice to cook evenly and prevent it from becoming sticky.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Vegetable Couscous
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of fluffy couscous is mounded in a rustic, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. A generous ladle of rich, reddish-brown vegetable stew is spooned over the couscous. The stew contains tender, green okra pods, vibrant red and yellow bell pepper chunks (2cm), bright yellow corn kernels, and diced tomatoes. All ingredients are coated in a savory, aromatic sauce. A light sprinkle of fresh, chopped green parsley garnishes the top. The bowl sits on a well-worn wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, natural light from a nearby window. A simple, folded linen napkin and a rustic fork are placed beside the bowl, suggesting a casual, comforting meal.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve family-style from a large communal pot.
Offer crusty bread for dipping.
Serve with a side of plain yogurt or harissa for those who prefer more spice.
instructions: Dice onion. Mince garlic. Chop bell peppers into 2 cm chunks. Trim okra ends.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Sauté diced onion until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic; cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in bell pepper chunks, trimmed okra, diced tomatoes, corn kernels, cumin, coriander, paprika, and turmeric.
Pour in vegetable broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until vegetables are tender.
While stew simmers, prepare couscous: In a separate heatproof bowl, combine couscous with 250 ml boiling water or hot broth and a pinch of salt. Cover tightly. Let stand 5 minutes.
Fluff couscous with a fork.
Taste vegetable stew; adjust seasoning with salt and black pepper as needed.
Serve hot vegetable stew generously spooned over fluffy couscous. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Adjust spice levels to taste.
Fresh okra should be trimmed, frozen okra can be added directly.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Steaks with Forest Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef steak is prominently featured on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centrally positioned. The steak, a robust piece, is either served whole or cut into thick, substantial medallions, showcasing a perfectly seared, dark brown crust and a juicy, pink interior. Beside the beef, a neat mound of earthy brown forest mushrooms, quartered or halved, glistens with a rich, savory sheen. A deep, glossy red wine reduction sauce is artfully spooned around the beef and mushrooms, creating a defined pool of rich color. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley, adding a vibrant contrast. The composition is balanced, with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. Standard European flatware (fork and knife) is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, with a subtly blurred, unobtrusive restaurant background maintaining focus on the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted potatoes or creamy mashed potatoes.
Offer a side of crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
instructions: Pat beef steaks dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add 20g butter.
Sear steaks 3-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness. Adjust time for thickness. Do not overcrowd the pan. Cook in batches if necessary.
Remove steaks from pan. Transfer to a cutting board. Tent loosely with foil. Let rest 10 minutes.
While steaks rest, add remaining 40g butter to the same pan. Add quartered or halved mushrooms. Sauté 5-7 minutes until golden brown and tender.
Add finely diced shallots and minced garlic to the pan with mushrooms. Sauté 2-3 minutes until fragrant. Add 2 sprigs of fresh thyme.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce wine by half, about 3 minutes.
Add beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce sauce until slightly thickened, about 5-7 minutes.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning. Keep warm.
Slice rested steaks into thick medallions, if desired. Alternatively, serve whole or in thick chunks.
Plate each steak portion on a clean white porcelain plate. Arrange sautéed mushrooms neatly beside the beef.
Spoon red wine sauce generously over the beef and mushrooms. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley.
notes: Resting the beef after searing is crucial for tenderness and juiciness.
Adjust searing time for desired doneness; use a meat thermometer for accuracy.
Use a good quality dry red wine for the sauce, such as Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Potato Croquettes with Tomato Dipping Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A rustic wooden board holds 8-12 golden-brown chicken potato croquettes. Each croquette is cylindrical, about 5 cm long, with a visibly crisp, textured Panko crust. They are arranged casually, some touching, some slightly overlapping, filling the platter adequately without overcrowding. A small, simple ceramic bowl, slightly imperfect, sits alongside, filled with a rich, deep red tomato dipping sauce. Finely chopped fresh parsley is sprinkled over the croquettes and lightly over the sauce, adding a vibrant green contrast. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light, evoking a comforting, homely atmosphere. A casually placed cloth napkin completes the relaxed, approachable presentation.
instructions: Boil chicken breast in salted water until cooked through. An internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) is required. Shred the cooked chicken finely. Set aside.
Peel and dice potatoes into 2 cm chunks. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well and mash thoroughly until smooth. Do not add milk or butter.
In a large bowl, combine shredded chicken and mashed potatoes. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well. Form the mixture into 8-12 cylindrical croquettes, about 5 cm long and 2.5 cm thick.

Prepare a breading station: Place flour in one shallow dish, beaten egg in another, and Panko breadcrumbs in a third. Lightly coat each croquette first in flour, then in egg, then thoroughly in Panko breadcrumbs. Press gently to ensure crumbs adhere.

For the tomato dipping sauce: Finely dice the small onion and mince the garlic clove. Heat 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a small saucepan over medium heat. Sauté onion until softened, about 3-5 minutes. Add garlic; cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in crushed tomatoes. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until slightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper. Stir in 1 tablespoon of chopped fresh parsley.

Heat vegetable oil in a deep pan or pot to 175°C (350°F). Fry croquettes in batches for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure they are heated through. Remove with a slotted spoon and place on a wire rack lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Arrange the golden croquettes on a serving platter or wooden board. Serve immediately with the warm tomato dipping sauce on the side. Garnish croquettes and sauce with remaining fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Poire Vanille Cannelle Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, precisely cut slice of Poire Vanille Cannelle Entremet stands architecturally centered on a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a subtle gold rim. The slice reveals distinct, immaculate layers: a delicate, light brown cinnamon génoise sponge base, followed by a translucent, pale amber poached pear insert with visible pear pieces, topped by a creamy, pale yellow vanilla bean mousse. The entire entremet is enveloped in a flawless, ultra-glossy white mirror glaze, reflecting light beautifully. A small, perfectly formed cluster of golden-brown cinnamon crumble is artfully placed to one side of the slice. A single, exquisitely thin candied pear slice, translucent and amber-hued, is positioned delicately near the crumble. A tiny, almost imperceptible speck of edible silver leaf adds a touch of understated luxury. Abundant negative space surrounds the dessert, emphasizing its sculptural form. The setting is a haute patisserie shop: a pristine white marble surface, under dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows, with an ultra-minimalist background to maximize focus on the dessert.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled with a small demitasse of strong espresso.
Pair with a glass of a sweet dessert wine, such as a Sauternes or a late harvest Riesling.
instructions: For Cinnamon Crumble: Combine 30g flour, 20g caster sugar, 20g diced cold butter, and 1g ground cinnamon. Rub until crumbly. Bake at 160°C for 10-12 minutes until golden. Cool.

For Cinnamon Génoise Sponge: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line an 18cm round cake tin. Whisk 2 eggs and 60g caster sugar over a bain-marie until warm and thick. Remove from heat. Continue whisking until cool and very voluminous. Fold in 60g sifted flour and 2g ground cinnamon. Gently fold in 15g melted butter and 2ml vanilla extract. Pour into tin. Bake for 15-18 minutes until golden. Cool. Cut a 16cm disc.

For Poached Pear Insert: Bloom 1.5g gelatin in cold water. Peel, core, and dice 2 medium pears. Combine 150ml water, 50g caster sugar, 10ml lemon juice, 1/2 split vanilla bean, and 1 small cinnamon stick in a saucepan. Bring to a simmer. Add diced pears. Poach gently until tender but still firm. Remove pears with a slotted spoon. Reduce liquid by half. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Add pears back. Pour into a 16cm silicone mould. Freeze until solid.

For Vanilla Bean Mousse: Bloom 3g gelatin in cold water. Whisk 3 egg yolks and 40g caster sugar until pale. Heat 100ml milk with 1/2 split vanilla bean until simmering. Temper hot milk into yolk mixture, whisking constantly. Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until thickened (nappe consistency). Do not boil. Remove from heat. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Strain into a clean bowl. Cool completely over an ice bath. Whip 200ml cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into cooled vanilla base.

For Assembly: Place the 16cm génoise disc at the bottom of an 18cm entremet ring or silicone mould. Place the frozen pear insert on top of the génoise. Pour vanilla mousse over and around the pear insert, filling the mould. Tap gently to remove air bubbles. Freeze for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.

For White Chocolate Mirror Glaze: Bloom 5g gelatin in cold water. In a saucepan, combine 50ml water, 100g glucose syrup, and 65g sweetened condensed milk. Bring to a simmer. Remove from heat. Add 100g finely chopped white chocolate and 1g titanium dioxide (if using). Stir until chocolate is melted and smooth. Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Blend with an immersion blender, keeping the head submerged to avoid air bubbles. Strain. Cool to 32-35°C.

To Glaze: Place frozen entremet on a wire rack over a baking tray. Pour the mirror glaze evenly over the entire frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Gently transfer the glazed entremet to a serving plate. Allow to thaw in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving.

To Serve: Slice the entremet with a hot, dry knife. Place a single slice on an elegant dessert plate. Garnish with a small, perfect piece of cinnamon crumble and a delicate, thin candied pear slice. Add a tiny speck of edible silver leaf for refinement.
notes: Precision in measurements and temperature control is crucial for entremet success.
Ensure each component is properly chilled or frozen before assembly and glazing.
Use high-quality silicone moulds for best results in shaping and demoulding.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Chicken and Rice Soup is presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. The golden, aromatic broth holds tender 2 cm cubed chicken pieces, distinct al dente Arborio rice grains, thinly sliced cremini mushrooms, and vibrant 1 cm diced tomatoes. The surface of the soup is lightly speckled with fresh, bright green chopped parsley, with a delicate swirl of extra virgin olive oil adding a subtle sheen. A thin lemon slice rests gracefully on the rim of the bowl, offering a touch of bright color contrast. The bowl sits on a simple, light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded white cotton napkin and an elegant silver soup spoon. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and clean presentation in a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping
A small side of green olives can complement the flavors
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice cremini mushrooms. Dice tomatoes into 1 cm pieces. Mince onion and garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add minced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Sauté for 5 minutes until mushrooms are tender.
Stir in diced tomatoes and dried oregano. Cook for 2 minutes.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add Arborio rice. Cook for 15-20 minutes, or until rice is tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes, ensuring chicken reaches 75°C (167°F) internal temperature.
Chop fresh parsley. Squeeze juice from 1/2 lemon into the soup. Stir.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Ladle soup into bowls. Garnish each serving with fresh chopped parsley and a thin lemon slice.

recipes.recipe_name: Matcha Honey Mousse, Almond Financier, Orange Blossom Gelee
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of a sophisticated Japanese dessert is artfully plated on a premium, smooth white bone china plate. A perfectly molded, pale green Matcha Honey Mousse serves as the focal point, its surface impeccably smooth. Adjacent, a golden-brown Almond Financier, a small, precise rectangle, provides textural contrast. Several small, translucent amber cubes of Orange Blossom Gelee are delicately arranged. A single, thin, curled strip of vibrant orange candied peel adds a pop of color and height. Abundant negative space frames the minimalist composition. A faint dusting of vibrant green matcha powder subtly graces the plate. The setting includes a luxurious grey-veined marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows. A pristine white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, completes the elegant, culturally authentic presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a delicate finale to a multi-course omakase meal.
Pair with a light, unsweetened sencha or hojicha tea.
instructions: For the Almond Financiers: Preheat oven to 180°C. Melt butter until golden brown (beurre noisette). Sift almond flour, all-purpose flour, and 50g sugar. Whisk egg whites until foamy. Fold dry ingredients into egg whites. Gently fold in brown butter. Pour batter into small rectangular financier molds. Bake 12-15 minutes until golden and set. Cool completely.

For the Matcha Honey Mousse: Bloom 3 gelatin sheets in ice water. Heat 100ml cream and honey until honey dissolves. Whisk in matcha powder until smooth. Squeeze excess water from gelatin, dissolve in warm matcha cream mixture. Let cool to room temperature. Whip remaining 200ml cream to soft peaks. Gently fold matcha mixture into whipped cream. Pour into desired molds (e.g., small spheres or cylinders). Chill 4 hours minimum, or until set.

For the Orange Blossom Gelee: Bloom 2 gelatin sheets in ice water. Combine orange juice, sweet white wine, orange zest, and 20g sugar in a small saucepan. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Squeeze excess water from gelatin, dissolve in warm orange mixture. Stir in orange blossom water. Pour into a shallow dish or mold to a thickness of about 0.5 cm. Chill 2 hours minimum, or until set.

To Assemble: Unmold Matcha Honey Mousse. Cut Orange Blossom Gelee into small, precise cubes or desired shapes. Plate one mousse per serving. Arrange one financier next to the mousse. Place a few gelee cubes artfully on the plate. Garnish with a thin strip of candied orange peel. Lightly dust the plate with matcha powder using a fine sieve. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto with Roasted Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Mushroom Risotto is presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl, allowing the fluid risotto to spread naturally. Diced chicken pieces, approximately 2-3 cm, are visibly integrated, alongside finely diced red bell pepper (1 cm) and sliced brown mushrooms. A vibrant scattering of whole roasted cherry tomatoes, their skins slightly burst, adorns the surface. Fresh basil leaves, torn, are generously sprinkled over the dish, adding a pop of bright green. The colors are rich: golden-brown chicken, deep earthy mushrooms, bright red bell pepper and tomatoes, all against the creamy, pale yellow risotto. The texture is invitingly smooth and tender. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded white cotton napkin. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, creating a clean, inviting bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto is best enjoyed fresh.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Toss cherry tomatoes with 5 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 15-20 minutes until softened and slightly burst. Set aside.
Heat chicken broth in a saucepan; keep it hot over low heat.

Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Internal temperature must reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet; set aside.

Finely chop onion and mince garlic. Dice red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Slice mushrooms. Add remaining 10 ml olive oil and 15 g butter to the same skillet. Add onion, bell pepper, and mushrooms. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the skillet. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add one ladleful (about 250 ml) of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir continuously until almost completely absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly and waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
When rice is al dente (creamy but still firm to the bite), stir in cooked chicken and roasted tomatoes.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in remaining 15 g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until creamy. Check seasoning; adjust with salt and pepper.
Tear fresh basil leaves. Stir most into the risotto. Reserve some for garnish.
Serve immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish with reserved fresh basil.
notes: The key to creamy risotto is to add hot broth gradually and stir constantly.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
traditional_techniques: Risottare (toasting rice and gradually adding liquid)
Mantecare (finishing risotto with butter and cheese for creaminess)

recipes.recipe_name: Khao Pad Sapparot Gai (Thai Pineapple Fried Rice with Chicken)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Thai Pineapple Fried Rice with Chicken is presented in a hollowed pineapple half, set on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The golden-yellow fried rice is mounded neatly within the pineapple shell, showcasing the diverse textures and colors. Tender, diced chicken pieces are interspersed with glistening, diced pineapple chunks, bright green spring onion slices, and chopped cilantro leaves. Scattered roasted cashews add a contrasting crunch and nutty color. The rice itself has a slightly crispy, fluffy texture. A vibrant lime wedge is placed beside the pineapple. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin rests beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, creating a clean, appealing presentation. A small, traditional ceramic dish with prik nam pla (fish sauce with sliced chilies) is subtly placed nearby, along with a pair of elegant chopsticks, emphasizing the authentic Thai dining experience.
instructions: Halve the fresh pineapple lengthwise. Scoop out all flesh from one half. Reserve the empty shell for serving. Dice half of the scooped pineapple flesh into 1.5 cm cubes. Set aside.
Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Dice yellow onion and red bell pepper into 1 cm pieces. Mince garlic and grate ginger.
Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or high-sided skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Add diced chicken to the wok. Stir-fry for 4-6 minutes until chicken is cooked through and lightly browned. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from wok. Set aside.
Add diced onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger to the hot wok. Stir-fry for 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add diced red bell pepper (if using). Stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add cold cooked jasmine rice to the wok. Break up any clumps. Stir-fry vigorously for 3-4 minutes until rice is slightly crispy.
Push rice to one side of the wok. Add curry powder to the empty space. Cook for 30 seconds until fragrant. Mix curry powder into the rice.
Return cooked chicken to the wok. Add diced pineapple, roasted cashews, and raisins.
Pour in fish sauce, soy sauce, and oyster sauce. Add white pepper. Toss all ingredients to combine thoroughly.
Continue to stir-fry for 2-3 minutes until all ingredients are heated through and flavors are well distributed.
Serve hot. Spoon the fried rice into the hollowed pineapple half for presentation. Garnish generously with sliced spring onions and fresh cilantro. Serve with lime wedges on the side.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Roulade with Cashew-Mushroom Duxelles, Parmesan Risotto, Mozzarella Foam
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a pristine white bone china plate, centered with abundant negative space. A thick, perfectly seared chicken roulade, sliced into two substantial medallions, reveals a rich, earthy cashew-mushroom duxelles filling, showcasing a beautiful cross-section. The chicken is golden-brown and moist. Adjacent, a pool of creamy, free-flowing Parmesan risotto, al dente and shimmering, anchors the composition. A delicate cloud of airy mozzarella foam rests lightly atop the roulade and spills subtly onto the risotto. A single vibrant sprig of fresh micro-thyme provides a final, verdant touch. The plate rests on a polished dark wood table, with a precisely folded white linen napkin to the side. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the textures and creating depth against a minimalist, uncluttered background.
instructions: Prepare the Duxelles: Finely chop mushrooms and shallot. Heat 15ml olive oil in a pan. Sauté mushrooms and shallot until all moisture evaporates and they are golden. Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute. Remove from heat. Grind cashews into a fine meal. Stir cashew meal into the mushroom mixture. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside to cool.

Prepare the Chicken Roulade: Pound each chicken breast between two sheets of cling film until 5mm thick. Season both sides with salt and pepper. Spread an even layer of the cooled duxelles over each chicken breast, leaving a small border. Tightly roll each breast into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine or toothpicks.

Sear and Bake Chicken: Preheat oven to 190°C. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil and 20g butter in an oven-safe pan over medium-high heat. Sear chicken roulades until golden-brown on all sides, about 6-8 minutes total. Transfer pan to the preheated oven. Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from oven, loosely tent with foil, and rest for 5 minutes.

Prepare Parmesan Risotto: While chicken bakes, melt 15g butter in a separate saucepan over medium heat. Add finely diced shallot and cook until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add Arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly. Pour in white wine and stir until fully absorbed. Begin adding hot chicken stock, one ladleful at a time, stirring continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. Continue for 18-20 minutes, until rice is al dente and creamy. Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 15g butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Season with salt and pepper.

Prepare Mozzarella Foam: In a small saucepan, combine fresh mozzarella, heavy cream, and whole milk. Heat gently over low heat, stirring until mozzarella is fully melted and smooth. Do not boil. Blend mixture with an immersion blender until smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Pour into a culinary siphon. Charge with one N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep warm.

Assemble and Serve: Slice each rested chicken roulade into two thick medallions. Ladle a generous portion of free-flowing Parmesan risotto onto the center of each plate. Arrange two chicken roulade medallions artistically on top of the risotto. Dispense a delicate cloud of mozzarella foam over the chicken and risotto. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh thyme or a few perfectly roasted wild mushroom caps. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best results, serve the dish immediately after plating to maintain the ideal texture of the risotto and foam.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Ballotine with Morel Farce, Cashew Emulsion, and Parmesan Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly cylindrical chicken ballotine, seared to a deep golden-brown, rests elegantly on a pristine white bone china plate. The chicken, a compact 'chunk' of refined culinary art, is positioned slightly off-center. Beneath or alongside it, a delicate, pale beige 'tear' of the smooth cashew emulsion provides a soft, organic line. A thin, abstractly shaped Parmesan crisp leans gracefully against the chicken, adding a subtle golden accent and textural contrast. A few vibrant green chervil sprigs are precisely placed for a final pop of color and freshness. Abundant negative space surrounds the components, emphasizing the minimalist composition and meticulous execution. The plate sits on a premium white Carrara marble surface, illuminated by dramatic professional lighting that casts subtle shadows, enhancing depth and sophistication. A precisely folded white linen napkin completes the ultra-minimalist, high-end setting.
instructions: Preheat a water bath to 63°C (145°F) for sous vide cooking.
Clean morel mushrooms. Finely dice mushrooms, shallot, and garlic.
Melt 15g butter in a sauté pan over medium heat. Add shallot and garlic. Cook until translucent, about 2 minutes.
Add diced morels and thyme. Sauté until moisture evaporates and mushrooms are tender, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat. Let cool.
In a bowl, combine cooled mushrooms with 20g grated Parmesan and mozzarella. Season with salt and pepper. This is the mushroom farce.
Butterfly each chicken breast. Place between two sheets of plastic wrap. Gently pound to an even 0.5 cm thickness.
Season chicken lightly with salt and pepper. Spread a quarter of the mushroom farce evenly over each chicken breast, leaving a 1 cm border.
Carefully roll each chicken breast tightly into a cylinder. Secure with kitchen twine or wrap tightly in plastic wrap to maintain shape.
Place each rolled chicken ballotine in a vacuum-sealable bag. Vacuum seal the bags.
Submerge sealed chicken bags in the preheated water bath. Cook for 1 hour and 30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
While chicken cooks, prepare cashew emulsion. Toast cashews lightly in a dry pan until fragrant. Do not burn.
Blend toasted cashews with chicken stock and heavy cream until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Season with salt. If desired, whisk in xanthan gum for stability.

To make Parmesan crisps, preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Line a baking sheet with parchment paper. Sprinkle remaining 30g Parmesan in thin circles or abstract shapes. Bake for 5-7 minutes, or until golden and crisp. Let cool completely.
Once chicken is cooked, remove from water bath. Cut away plastic wrap or twine. Pat chicken dry with paper towels.
Heat remaining 15g butter and olive oil in a sauté pan over medium-high heat. Sear each chicken ballotine for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and crisp. Baste with pan drippings.
Rest chicken for 5 minutes.

To plate, spoon a generous 'tear' or swirl of cashew emulsion onto the center of each plate. Place one seared chicken ballotine elegantly on top or beside the emulsion. Garnish with a Parmesan crisp and a few chervil sprigs or microgreens.
Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
For best results, use a high-speed blender for the cashew emulsion and strain it thoroughly.

recipes.recipe_name: Cordero con Mole de Manzana y Cacao
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of rich, savory Cordero con Mole is presented on a rustic, matte terracotta-colored ceramic plate. Three to four substantial, tender chunks of braised lamb, cut into irregular 4-5 cm cubes, are nestled together, generously coated in a glossy, deep reddish-brown mole sauce. The sauce is thick and smooth, with subtle flecks of green from finely chopped cilantro and a scattering of toasted sesame seeds on top. The lamb itself shows no slicing, maintaining its whole, braised form. The sauce has a complex, earthy sheen. A small pile of fluffy white rice sits neatly beside the lamb, and a stack of warm, pliable corn tortillas are arranged on the side of the plate. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A clean, white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the sauce's depth and the lamb's tenderness. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the mole.
Accompany with a side of traditional Mexican white rice.
instructions: Toast dried ancho and mulato chilies in a dry pan over medium heat until fragrant, about 1-2 minutes per side. Do not burn. Remove from pan.
Place toasted chilies in a bowl. Cover with hot water. Soak for 20 minutes until softened. Drain, remove stems and seeds.
Heat 15ml lard or oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear lamb chunks until browned on all sides. Remove lamb and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml lard or oil to the pot. Sauté chopped onion, garlic, tomatoes, and apple until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add almonds, 15g sesame seeds, cinnamon stick, cloves, cumin seeds, and oregano to the pot. Cook for 2-3 minutes, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Transfer sautéed mixture and softened chilies to a blender. Add 250ml chicken stock. Blend until very smooth. For a finer mole, pass the sauce through a fine-mesh sieve into a bowl, pressing solids.
Return the strained mole sauce to the pot. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly, for 10-15 minutes until it thickens and darkens.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Add remaining 500ml chicken stock and chipotle chili (if using). Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 2 to 2.5 hours, or until lamb is very tender. Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
During the last 15 minutes of cooking, add chopped chocolate to the mole. Stir until melted and fully incorporated.
Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh cilantro and toasted sesame seeds.
traditional_techniques: Molido (grinding/blending ingredients for the mole paste)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Polenta, Roasted Asparagus, and Spinach
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Polenta, Roasted Asparagus, and Spinach is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A generous mound of golden, fluid creamy polenta forms the base. A perfectly seared, whole chicken breast, golden-brown and tender, rests atop the polenta. Alongside, vibrant green roasted asparagus spears, slightly charred at the tips, are neatly arranged. A delicate cluster of deep green, gently wilted spinach adds a soft texture and color contrast. The dish is garnished simply with a sprinkle of fresh, chopped flat-leaf parsley. The composition is balanced with moderate negative space, showcasing the natural colors and textures. It sits on a simple wooden table, with a linen napkin and classic silver flatware beside it, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty ciabatta bread to soak up any remaining polenta or pan sauce.
Pair with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
instructions: Prepare polenta: In a large saucepan, bring chicken broth and milk to a rolling boil over medium-high heat. Slowly whisk in the instant polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring constantly with a wooden spoon, for 5-7 minutes until polenta is thick and creamy. Stir in 30g butter, grated Parmesan cheese, salt, and black pepper. Keep warm, covered.
Roast asparagus: Preheat oven to 200°C. On a baking sheet, toss asparagus spears with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 8-10 minutes, or until tender-crisp and slightly charred. Set aside.

Cook chicken: Pat chicken breasts dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper. Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Place chicken breasts in the hot skillet. Sear for 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Internal temperature should reach 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside to rest. If desired, add diced shallot to the same skillet, cook for 1 minute. Deglaze with white wine, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom. Reduce liquid slightly.

Wilt spinach: In the same skillet (or a separate pan), melt remaining 15g butter over medium heat. Add minced garlic and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add baby spinach. Cook for 1-2 minutes, stirring occasionally, until just wilted. Season with salt.

Plate the dish: Spoon a generous portion of creamy polenta onto the center of each white porcelain dinner plate. Place one pan-seared chicken breast on top of the polenta. Arrange roasted asparagus spears neatly beside the chicken. Place a delicate cluster of wilted spinach next to the asparagus. Garnish with freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley before serving immediately.
notes: For extra flavor, deglaze the pan after searing chicken with a splash of white wine or chicken broth to create a light pan sauce.
If the polenta thickens too much while waiting, stir in a splash of hot chicken broth or milk to loosen it to your desired consistency.
traditional_techniques: Mantecare (for polenta, refers to the process of stirring in butter and cheese to create a creamy, emulsified texture)

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Cacciatore with Rustic Tomatoes and Mushrooms
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Chicken Cacciatore is presented on a clean, wide-rimmed white porcelain dinner plate, showcasing a rustic yet refined appeal. A bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh, its skin deeply golden and slightly crisped, rests as the centerpiece. It is generously coated in a rich, rustic tomato sauce, vibrant with shades of deep red and hints of orange. Quartered cremini mushrooms, softened and earthy brown, are nestled around and atop the chicken, alongside tender pieces of diced red bell pepper and softened onion. The sauce has a moderate viscosity, clinging to the chicken and vegetables, with visible specks of herbs. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a fresh contrast. The arrangement is natural and flowing, allowing moderate negative space on the plate. The plate is set on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, even light illuminates the dish, highlighting its comforting textures and colors against a soft, blurred restaurant-style background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Serve over creamy polenta or pasta (e.g., tagliatelle, pappardelle).
Offer grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese on the side.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion, red bell pepper, and quartered mushrooms to the pot. Sauté until vegetables soften, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer and cook until wine reduces by half, about 3-4 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken stock, rosemary, thyme, and bay leaf. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pot. Nestle them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 35-45 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C).
Remove bay leaf. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper as needed.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.
notes: Browning the chicken thoroughly adds depth of flavor.
The sauce thickens naturally as it simmers. If too thin, remove chicken and reduce sauce over medium-high heat.

recipes.recipe_name: Potato Pavé with Seared Beef, Roasted Tomato, and Charred Corn Puree
recipes.visual_description: A refined, minimalist presentation on a pristine white bone china plate. Two precise, golden-brown Potato Pavé blocks are anchored on one side, showcasing their crisp edges and layered interior. Adjacent, two small, perfectly seared beef tenderloin cubes gleam, revealing a tender, medium-rare interior. Scattered around these core elements are vibrant halves of roasted cherry tomatoes, some red, some yellow, their skins slightly blistered. A delicate swirl or small quenelle of pale yellow Charred Corn & Mushroom Puree provides a silky counterpoint. A few irregular, translucent Cayenne-Infused Rice Crisps are artfully placed for height and a subtle textural contrast. Dots or a fine drizzle of the creamy Cayenne-Infused Mayonnaise Emulsion complete the composition, integrating the flavors visually. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing the meticulous placement and luxurious quality. The plate rests on a premium light grey marble surface, accompanied by a precisely folded white linen napkin and minimalist flatware, all under dramatic, focused lighting creating soft shadows.
instructions: For the Potato Pavé: Peel potatoes. Slice very thinly (1-2 mm) using a mandoline. Layer slices tightly in a small, parchment-lined baking dish (approx. 15x10 cm). Brush each layer with melted butter. Season with salt and pepper. Pour stock over. Cover with parchment, then foil. Place a weight on top. Bake at 160°C for 90 minutes. Remove weight and foil. Cool completely. Refrigerate overnight with weight. Cut into 8 precise rectangular blocks (approx. 5x3 cm).

For the Seared Beef Tenderloin: Pat beef dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15 ml olive oil in a heavy pan over high heat. Sear beef tenderloin whole for 2-3 minutes per side until deeply browned. Meat internal temperature must reach 75°C. Rest beef for 5 minutes. Cut into 8 small, precise 2-3 cm cubes.

For the Roasted Cherry Tomatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15 ml olive oil, 2 thinly sliced garlic cloves, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking sheet. Roast for 10-12 minutes until just beginning to burst.

For the Charred Corn & Mushroom Puree: Heat a dry pan over high heat. Add corn kernels; char deeply for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally. Set aside. In the same pan, add a drizzle of olive oil. Sauté finely diced shallot and 100g finely chopped mushrooms until softened and browned. Add 1 minced garlic clove and cook for 1 minute. Combine charred corn, mushroom mixture, and 50 ml stock in a blender. Blend until exceptionally smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for silkiness. Season with salt and pepper.

For the Cayenne-Infused Rice Crisp: Spread cooked jasmine rice very thinly (1 mm) onto a parchment-lined baking sheet. Bake at 100°C for 60-90 minutes until completely dry and brittle. Increase oven temperature to 180°C. Bake for 5-10 minutes more until puffed and crisp. Alternatively, deep-fry dry rice until puffed. Season with a pinch of cayenne pepper and salt. Break into irregular, delicate shards.

For the Mayonnaise Emulsion: Roast one garlic clove until very soft. Squeeze out pulp. In a small bowl, whisk mayonnaise with roasted garlic pulp, 15 ml lemon juice, and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Season with salt. Adjust consistency with a few drops of water if too thick.

To Plate: Gently pan-fry potato pavé blocks in a little oil until golden and crisp on all sides. Place two potato pavé blocks slightly offset on one side of each plate. Arrange two beef cubes next to the potato. Artfully scatter a few roasted tomato halves around. Place a small quenelle or swirl of Charred Corn & Mushroom Puree on the plate. Drizzle or dot the Cayenne-Infused Mayonnaise Emulsion around the elements. Garnish with 1-2 delicate Cayenne-Infused Rice Crisps for height and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Turkey Ragu with Creamy Polenta
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion is presented in a wide, shallow white porcelain bowl. A creamy, golden yellow bed of soft polenta forms the base. Mounded centrally is a rich, deep red turkey ragu, showcasing tender ground turkey pieces and finely diced soffritto vegetables. Vibrant, blistered halved roasted cherry tomatoes are scattered, adding bright red pops and sweetness. The dish is garnished with fresh, torn basil leaves for green and aroma, plus a light dusting of finely grated Parmesan. Textures contrast: smooth polenta against hearty ragu and soft, juicy tomatoes. The setting is a simple wooden table, with a folded linen napkin and classic Italian-style flatware beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's inviting colors and textures for an authentic Italian casual dining presentation.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to scoop up the rich sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve the cherry tomatoes. Toss with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast for 15-20 minutes until slightly blistered.
Heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced onion, carrot, and celery (soffritto). Cook for 8-10 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic to the pot. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add ground turkey to the pot. Break it up with a spoon. Cook until browned, ensuring no pink remains (75°C internal temperature). Drain any excess fat.
If using, pour in red wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Let simmer for 2-3 minutes until mostly reduced.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken stock. Season with salt and pepper. Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat to low. Cover and cook for at least 30 minutes, or up to 1 hour, stirring occasionally.
While ragu simmers, prepare polenta. Bring 1 litre of water (or chicken stock) to a boil in a separate saucepan. Season with salt.
Gradually whisk in the polenta, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 5-7 minutes, or until polenta is creamy and thickened.
Remove polenta from heat. Stir in butter and 60g grated Parmesan cheese until melted and smooth.
Taste and adjust seasoning for both ragu and polenta.

To serve, spoon a generous portion of creamy polenta onto each plate. Top with a ladleful of turkey ragu. Garnish with roasted cherry tomatoes and fresh torn basil leaves. Sprinkle with extra grated Parmesan cheese.
notes: The ragu can be prepared a day in advance; its flavors deepen overnight. Reheat gently before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Italian Sausage and Bell Pepper Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, modest portion of Hearty Italian Sausage and Bell Pepper Pasta sits in a simple, deep ceramic bowl. The pasta, likely rigatoni or penne, is generously coated in a rich, rustic red tomato sauce. Chunks of browned, crumbled Italian sausage are visible throughout, interspersed with softened slices of vibrant red and yellow bell peppers and diced onion. A sprinkle of bright green, freshly chopped parsley and a dusting of grated Pecorino Romano cheese sit atop the pasta. The dish is presented on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. A casual, slightly rumpled cloth napkin and a simple fork are placed beside the bowl. Natural, warm light illuminates the scene, creating a comforting, inviting atmosphere typical of a family kitchen. The overall presentation is homely and unpretentious, emphasizing the dish's comforting, satisfying nature.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping in the sauce.
A simple green salad with vinaigrette makes a good accompaniment.

ingredients.name: grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese (for serving)

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium-high heat.
Add Italian sausage, breaking it up with a spoon. Cook until browned and cooked through, about 8-10 minutes. Drain excess fat. Remove sausage from pot and set aside.
Add diced onion and sliced bell peppers to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked sausage to the pot. Stir well. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes, allowing flavors to meld.
While sauce simmers, cook pasta according to package directions in salted boiling water until al dente. Drain pasta, reserving 125 ml of pasta water.
Add drained pasta to the sauce. Stir to combine. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water a little at a time until desired consistency.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and grated Pecorino Romano or Parmesan cheese.
notes: Adjust spice level by choosing sweet or hot Italian sausage.
Reserved pasta water helps bind the sauce to the pasta.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Mushroom & Chicken Ravioli
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented in a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic bowl of natural cream. Three to four plump, irregularly shaped ravioli, revealing the light brown filling through pale yellow pasta, are arranged organically. They rest in a shallow pool of clear, golden Parmesan broth, their forms distinct. Diced chicken and finely chopped fermented mushrooms provide subtle texture. A delicate olive oil drizzle glistens. Small, vibrant green parsley leaves are placed naturally. The bowl sits on a light, reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin is casually placed. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, highlighting natural colors. The background is clean and minimalist, with a hint of natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve as a light first course in a multi-course meal
Accompanied by a glass of dry white wine
instructions: Prepare lacto-fermented mushrooms at least 5 days in advance: Slice fresh mushrooms. Place in a clean jar with 2% brine (20g salt per 1L water). Ensure mushrooms are submerged. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days until slightly tangy. Store in refrigerator.
Make pasta dough: Combine flour and eggs on a clean surface. Knead until smooth and elastic, about 10 minutes. Wrap in plastic wrap. Rest for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Prepare chicken: Poach chicken breast in lightly salted water until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken. Cool. Dice chicken into small cubes (5mm).
Prepare ravioli filling: Finely chop fermented mushrooms. In a bowl, combine diced chicken, chopped fermented mushrooms, ricotta cheese, 10g grated Parmesan, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Mix well.

Make Parmesan broth: Clean fresh mushrooms. Reserve caps for another use. Use mushroom stems. In a pot, combine mushroom stems, Parmesan rind, quartered onion, chopped carrot, chopped celery, and 1.5 L water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 30 minutes. Strain broth. Discard solids. Season broth with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Assemble ravioli: Roll pasta dough thinly using a pasta machine or rolling pin. Place small mounds of filling (about 5g) at regular intervals on one half of the pasta sheet. Moisten edges with water. Fold the other half of the pasta sheet over. Press firmly around filling to seal. Cut into desired shapes (squares or rounds) using a knife or cutter. Ensure no air pockets.
Cook ravioli: Bring a large pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Carefully add ravioli. Cook for 3-4 minutes, or until al dente and floating. Do not overcrowd the pot.

Plate the dish: Place 3-4 cooked ravioli in a shallow ceramic bowl. Ladle warm Parmesan broth around the ravioli. Drizzle with olive oil. Garnish with a few small fresh parsley leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: The fermentation time for mushrooms can vary based on temperature. Taste to determine desired tanginess.
Fresh pasta can be made ahead and refrigerated for up to 24 hours, or frozen for longer storage.
This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using mushroom stems and Parmesan rind for the broth.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Polenta with Spicy Tomato & Dark Chocolate Ragù
recipes.visual_description: A single individual serving of creamy, golden polenta is elegantly plated on a round white porcelain dinner plate, occupying the center. The polenta, cooked to a fluid, soft consistency, forms a smooth, slightly mounded base, not a rigid ring. A rich, deep red tomato and dark chocolate ragù is generously spooned over the polenta, its vibrant color contrasting beautifully with the polenta's warmth. The ragù is thick with finely diced onion, minced garlic, and small pieces of red chili, showcasing a rustic yet refined texture. Scattered across the ragù are fresh, bright green torn basil leaves, adding a pop of color and freshness. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table surface, with a clean white cotton napkin folded neatly beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the steam rising gently from the hot food and the subtle sheen of the sauce. The background is a soft, blurred restaurant-style setting, maintaining a casual yet professional atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread for dipping.
Offer a side of simple green salad with a vinaigrette.

ingredients.name: Fresh basil
ingredients.quantity: A small bunch, torn, for garnish

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add diced red onion. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and minced red chilies. Cook for 2 minutes until fragrant, do not brown garlic.
Pour in crushed tomatoes and 200ml vegetable broth. Bring to a simmer. Season with salt and black pepper.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 20 minutes, stirring occasionally, allowing flavors to meld.

Stir in the finely chopped dark chocolate until it is fully melted and incorporated into the sauce. Continue to simmer gently for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the sauce to thicken slightly. Taste and adjust seasoning.
While the ragù simmers, bring 1.3 litres of vegetable broth to a boil in a separate heavy-bottomed pot.
Slowly whisk in the polenta, ensuring no lumps form.

Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently with a wooden spoon, for 25-30 minutes, or until the polenta is creamy and tender. It should pull away from the sides of the pot. If it becomes too thick, add a little more hot broth. Season with salt.
Ladle a generous portion of creamy polenta onto each plate. Create a slight well in the center.
Spoon a substantial amount of the hot tomato and dark chocolate ragù over the polenta.
Garnish with fresh torn basil leaves. Serve immediately.
notes: For extra richness in the polenta, a knob of plant-based butter or a drizzle of good quality olive oil can be stirred in at the end.
The heat level of the ragù can be adjusted by varying the amount and type of chilies used.
