Candied Lemon Peel: Wash lemons. Remove zest in wide strips, avoiding white pith. Cut zest into thin julienne. Blanch zest in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain. Repeat blanching twice more to reduce bitterness. In a small saucepan, combine 50g maple syrup and 100ml water. Bring to a simmer. Add blanched zest. Simmer gently until translucent, about 15-20 minutes. Remove zest with a slotted spoon. Place on parchment paper to dry completely. Reserve syrup.

Lemon Verbena Infusion: Gently heat 50ml of the reserved candied lemon syrup with 10 fresh lemon verbena leaves. Do not boil. Remove from heat. Let steep for 15 minutes. Strain out leaves. Chill infusion.

Lemon Sablés: Preheat oven to 160°C. Cream cold butter and powdered sugar until just combined. Add flour. Mix until a dough forms. Roll dough very thin (2mm) between two sheets of parchment paper. Cut 6-9 small (3-4 cm diameter) circles. Place on a baking sheet. Bake for 8-10 minutes until light golden. Cool completely on a wire rack.

Mousse Assembly: Zest remaining lemon. Juice one lemon. In a saucepan, combine 50g maple syrup, lemon juice, lemon zest, and vanilla bean paste. Sprinkle agar-agar powder over. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, whisking constantly for 1 minute to dissolve agar. Remove from heat. Let cool to lukewarm.

Fold the lukewarm agar mixture into the chilled cultured cream until just combined. Gently whip the mixture briefly until light and airy, being careful not to overmix. Spoon or pipe mousse onto cooled lemon sablés. Chill for at least 2 hours to set.

Final Plating: Arrange set mousses on an elegant serving platter. Garnish each with a few pieces of candied lemon peel and a small fresh lemon verbena leaf. Lightly drizzle with the chilled lemon verbena infusion.
notes: This recipe utilizes the entire lemon for minimal waste: juice and zest for the mousse, and peel for candying.
Fermentation of the cream adds a subtle tangy note, enhancing flavor complexity and digestibility.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Roasted Chicken with Lemon and Herbs
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mediterranean Roasted Chicken is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two golden-brown, crispy-skinned chicken thighs are the centerpiece, nestled among vibrant roasted vegetables. Small new potatoes, halved and roasted to a tender, slightly crisp exterior, are scattered around. Burst cherry tomatoes add pops of bright red. Red onion wedges, caramelized at the edges, and whole smashed garlic cloves are interspersed. Fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs are casually placed, contributing deep green color and aromatic appeal. Thin lemon slices, slightly charred, rest atop the chicken. The dish exhibits natural textures and rich, warm colors. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware, under soft, natural lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a large baking tray with parchment paper.
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Halve small new potatoes. Quarter red onion into wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
Slice one lemon into thin rounds. Juice the second lemon.
On the baking tray, combine chicken, potatoes, red onion, garlic, cherry tomatoes, and Kalamata olives.
Drizzle with olive oil. Add fresh rosemary and thyme sprigs. Toss to coat evenly.
Arrange ingredients in a single layer. Distribute lemon slices over the chicken and vegetables.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden and crispy, and internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Stir vegetables halfway through roasting for even browning.
Remove from oven. Drizzle with fresh lemon juice. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken Supreme, Artichoke Purée, Crispy Skin, Chive Oil
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken supreme medallion, approximately 5 cm in diameter and 2 cm thick, rests slightly off-center on a pristine, large round bone china plate with a subtle matte finish. The chicken displays a deep golden-brown, crispy skin, contrasting with its tender, pale interior visible from a clean, precise cut. Beside the chicken, a flowing, organic swirl of velvety smooth, pale green artichoke purée creates an elegant arc. A few shards of crisp, golden chicken skin are artfully placed on top of the chicken for textural contrast. A delicate drizzle of vibrant green chive oil adds a pop of color and aromatic sheen, tracing a natural line across the purée and plate. The composition utilizes abundant negative space, emphasizing the dish's minimalist elegance. The plate sits on a grey veined Carrara marble surface. A precisely folded white linen napkin and a single modern, silver fork are positioned to the side. Dramatic, professional lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing depth.
instructions: Pat chicken supreme dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.

Carefully remove skin from two chicken supremes. Place skin between two sheets of parchment paper. Place another baking sheet on top. Bake at 180°C until golden and very crisp, about 15-20 minutes. Break into shards.

Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add 15ml grapeseed oil. Place chicken supremes skin-side down. Sear 6-8 minutes until skin is deep golden and crispy. Flip chicken. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add 20g butter to the pan. Baste chicken with butter for 8-10 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Rest chicken 5 minutes before slicing into medallions.

In a saucepan, combine artichoke hearts and chicken stock. Simmer 5-7 minutes until tender. Drain most stock, reserving a small amount. Transfer artichokes to a high-speed blender. Add 30g butter and heavy cream. Blend until very smooth, adding reserved stock as needed for desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate smoothness. Keep warm.

Blanch chives in boiling water for 30 seconds. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Squeeze dry. Blend chives with 15ml grapeseed oil until bright green and smooth. Strain through a coffee filter or cheesecloth for clear oil.

Spoon a flowing, organic swirl of artichoke purée onto each plate. Slice each rested chicken supreme into two thick medallions. Place one medallion gently onto the purée. Arrange a few crispy chicken skin shards on top of the chicken. Drizzle chive oil artistically around the purée and chicken. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Buckwheat Kasha
recipes.special_requests: just make a dish with buckwheat
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Chicken and Mushroom Buckwheat Kasha is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Tender, golden-brown chicken thigh chunks are nestled into a rustic mound of fluffy, earthy buckwheat kasha. Sliced cremini mushrooms, sautéed to a deep brown, are interspersed throughout the kasha, adding visual depth and texture. The dish is garnished with several vibrant fresh dill sprigs and a generous dollop of creamy white sour cream positioned to the side. The overall color palette is warm and natural, with rich browns, golden hues, and fresh green accents. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface with natural, even lighting from above. A white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are neatly placed beside the plate. The composition is balanced and inviting, with appropriate negative space, showcasing the entire dish as the focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of pickled vegetables, such as pickled cucumbers or cabbage.
Offer rye bread alongside the dish.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Cut chicken into 3-4 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.
Dice onion and carrot. Slice mushrooms. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Add butter to the pot. Add diced onion, carrot, and sliced mushrooms. Sauté until vegetables soften, about 7-8 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in buckwheat groats. Toast for 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a boil. Return seared chicken to the pot.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes, or until buckwheat is tender and liquid is absorbed. Stir occasionally.
Remove from heat. Let rest, covered, for 5 minutes.
Stir in chopped fresh dill. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Serve hot with a dollop of sour cream.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast with Buckwheat-Fig Crumble, Parsnip Puree, and Port Reduction
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of an ultra-sophisticated, minimalist dish is presented on a round, off-white bone china plate with a subtle, delicate pattern. A smooth, creamy parsnip puree forms an organic, flowing sweep across one side of the plate. Resting beside the puree is a perfectly pan-seared duck breast, its skin a deep, crispy golden-brown with a distinct crosshatch pattern, contrasting with the tender, medium-rare pink interior visible from the side. Scattered precisely over and around the duck breast and puree is a textural buckwheat-fig crumble, showcasing earthy brown buckwheat groats interspersed with dark, glossy pieces of finely diced fig. A rich, dark port reduction is artfully drizzled in a sinuous line across the plate, adding a deep, reflective sheen. A single, small fresh thyme sprig is placed as a delicate, verdant accent. The composition emphasizes abundant negative space, highlighting each element's precise execution and vibrant, yet refined, colors. The plate rests on a polished dark wooden table, subtly reflecting the dramatic, professional lighting that casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's architectural precision. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a sharp triangle, sits to the side, completing the luxurious Michelin-starred setting.
instructions: Prepare Parsnip Puree: Peel and chop parsnips into 2cm pieces. Place in a saucepan, cover with cold salted water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain thoroughly. Transfer parsnips to a blender. Add 50g butter, heavy cream, salt, and pepper. Blend until silky smooth. Keep warm.

Prepare Port Reduction: Finely mince shallot and garlic. In a small saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil over medium heat. Sauté shallot and garlic until fragrant, about 2 minutes. Deglaze with port wine. Bring to a simmer. Reduce port by half. Add duck stock. Continue to simmer until the sauce coats the back of a spoon, about 10-15 minutes. Strain the reduction through a fine-mesh sieve into a clean saucepan. Whisk in 20g cold butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare Buckwheat-Fig Crumble: Rinse buckwheat groats. Toast groats in a dry skillet over medium heat until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Transfer to a saucepan. Add 200ml water and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer until tender but still slightly al dente, about 15 minutes. Drain any excess water. Finely dice dried figs. In a small skillet, melt 10g butter. Add diced figs and 1 thyme sprig. Sauté for 2 minutes until softened. Combine cooked buckwheat and sautéed figs. Season lightly. Keep warm.

Prepare Duck Breast: Score the duck skin in a crosshatch pattern, being careful not to cut into the flesh. Season duck breasts generously with salt and pepper on both sides. Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, heavy-bottomed pan. Turn heat to medium-low. Slowly render the fat until the skin is crispy and golden brown, about 8-10 minutes. Pour off excess fat as it accumulates. Flip duck breasts. Sear flesh side for 3-4 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 55-60°C). Remove from pan. Rest duck breasts on a cutting board for 5 minutes.

Plate Dish: Spoon a generous quenelle or sweep of parsnip puree onto the center of each plate. Place one whole pan-seared duck breast next to the puree. Sprinkle buckwheat-fig crumble artfully over and around the duck breast. Drizzle port reduction elegantly around the dish. Garnish each plate with a small, fresh thyme sprig.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Risotto
recipes.visual_description: Serve the risotto on a flat white porcelain dinner plate. The consistency is fluid and spreads naturally across the plate, appearing free-flowing rather than molded. The rice grains are distinct, coated in a glossy, creamy sauce. Large 3cm chunks of golden-brown seared chicken thighs are distributed throughout the rice. Sliced cremini and shiitake mushrooms show deep caramelization and earthy brown tones. The dish features a pale golden hue. Finely minced flat-leaf parsley provides a vibrant green contrast. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese covers the surface. The arrangement is organic. Beside the plate sits a heavy silver spoon and a folded white cotton napkin on a light oak table. Natural side lighting highlights the creamy texture.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while the consistency remains fluid
Accompany with a crisp dry white wine such as Pinot Grigio
Provide extra grated Parmesan at the table
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks.
Dice onion into 5mm pieces.
Mince garlic cloves.
Slice mushrooms into 5mm thick pieces.
Heat 20ml olive oil in a wide pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned and internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add mushrooms to the same pan. Sauté until moisture evaporates and edges brown.
Remove mushrooms and set aside.
Melt 20g butter in the pan. Add onion and garlic.
Cook until softened but not browned.
Add rice. Stir 2 minutes to toast the grains until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until liquid is fully absorbed.
Add 200ml warm stock. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Repeat stock additions one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, until rice is tender but firm.
Return chicken and mushrooms to the pan.
Remove from heat.
Vigorously stir in remaining 30g butter and Parmesan cheese to create a creamy emulsion.
Season with salt and pepper. Fold in chopped parsley.
notes: Keep the chicken stock at a low simmer in a separate pot to maintain cooking temperature.
Stirring constantly is essential to release rice starches for a creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches the safety temperature of 75°C during the initial searing phase.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tomato & White Bean Crostini
recipes.visual_description: A series of 8-10 elegantly presented bite-sized canapés arranged on a light, reclaimed wood serving board. Each canapé features a crisp, rustic whole-grain cracker base, topped with a generous, artfully dolloped quenelle of creamy, pale beige white bean and fresh basil mousse. Nestled atop the mousse is a vibrant, ruby-red fermented cherry tomato half, glistening slightly. Delicate, thinly sliced, translucent quick-pickled red onion slivers are carefully placed beside the tomato, adding a subtle purple hue. A single, fresh, small basil leaf provides a final pop of deep green color and natural aroma. The arrangement emphasizes natural ingredient colors and textures – the crunchy cracker, smooth mousse, tender tomato, and crisp onion. Negative space is abundant, allowing each piece to stand out. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural light, with a clean, minimalist background, possibly hinting at natural elements like a blurred plant. The overall aesthetic is clean, uncluttered, and focuses on the pure beauty and sustainable nature of the ingredients.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Prepare fermented tomatoes: Wash cherry tomatoes. Halve them. Place in a clean jar. Sprinkle with 5 g fine sea salt. Cover loosely with a lid or fermentation airlock. Allow to ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days. Check daily for bubbling. Taste for desired tanginess. Refrigerate once fermented.

Prepare pickled red onion: Thinly slice the red onion into rings. In a small saucepan, combine white wine vinegar, sugar, and water. Bring to a simmer. Stir until sugar dissolves. Pour hot liquid over onion slices in a heatproof jar. Let cool. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes. Store in the refrigerator.

Make white bean and basil mousse: Combine drained cannellini beans, 20 g fresh basil leaves, peeled garlic clove, and 30 ml extra virgin olive oil in a food processor. Process until very smooth and creamy. Season with salt and pepper to taste. Adjust consistency with a tablespoon of water if needed. Refrigerate until ready to use.

Assemble canapés: Arrange crackers on a serving platter. Spoon or pipe a dollop of white bean and basil mousse onto each cracker. Top each with one fermented cherry tomato half. Place a few pickled red onion slivers next to the tomato. Garnish each canapé with a small fresh basil leaf. Drizzle lightly with remaining 30 ml extra virgin olive oil before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Parmesan Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pan-Seared Chicken with Parmesan Risotto is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The creamy, fluid Parmesan risotto forms an organic base, spreading naturally across the plate's center. A whole, unsliced pan-seared chicken breast, with a golden-brown, lightly crisp exterior, rests atop the risotto. A light drizzle of the glistening rosemary-garlic pan sauce coats the chicken and the surrounding risotto. A few fresh, vibrant green rosemary leaves are scattered on the chicken, alongside a light dusting of finely grated Parmigiano Reggiano. The overall color palette is warm, with golden chicken, creamy pale yellow risotto, and dark green herb accents. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A neatly folded cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish without harsh shadows. The background is minimal, ensuring focus on the food while evoking a casual, professional dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce and risotto.
Pair with a glass of dry white wine, such as Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C.
Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken breasts for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-15 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from oven, rest on a cutting board.
While chicken bakes, start risotto. In a separate large saucepan, melt 30 g butter with remaining 15 ml olive oil over medium heat.
Add chopped shallot. Sauté until softened, about 3 minutes.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until absorbed.
Add hot chicken broth, one ladle at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each addition to be mostly absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 20-25 minutes.
Risotto is done when creamy and al dente. Remove from heat. Stir in 100 g Parmigiano Reggiano and remaining 30 g butter. Season with salt and pepper. Cover to keep warm.
For the sauce, return the chicken skillet to medium heat. Add remaining 2 minced garlic cloves and rosemary sprigs. Sauté for 1 minute.
Add any resting juices from the chicken. Stir briefly. Remove rosemary sprigs.

Plate risotto onto individual plates. Place one whole pan-seared chicken breast on top of the risotto. Spoon the rosemary-garlic pan sauce over the chicken and risotto. Garnish with fresh rosemary leaves and extra grated Parmigiano Reggiano.
traditional_techniques: Mantecatura (finishing risotto with butter and cheese)

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef with Quick Fermented Bell Pepper Salsa
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared beef medallion is presented on a minimalist, handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The beef is cooked to a rich brown crust, showcasing its natural texture. Adjacent to the beef, a vibrant mound of quick fermented bell pepper salsa bursts with color from finely diced red and yellow bell peppers, and tomatoes, creating a fresh, inviting contrast. A delicate dusting of pale red dehydrated tomato powder lightly graces the plate, offering a subtle, refined accent. The composition is clean and uncrowded, allowing ample negative space to highlight each ingredient's inherent beauty. The plate rests on a light bamboo table surface, reflecting a natural, eco-conscious aesthetic. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue is subtly placed to the side. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, enhancing the organic textures and colors of the food. A hint of green foliage from a simple plant in the background adds a touch of life without distracting from the dish.
instructions: Prepare Quick Fermented Bell Pepper Salsa: Finely dice red and yellow bell peppers. Finely dice 3 tomatoes. Finely dice red onion. Mince garlic. In a bowl, combine diced vegetables, garlic, and 5g sea salt. Mix well. Cover loosely. Let sit at room temperature for 1-2 hours to macerate and develop flavor. Stir occasionally.
Prepare Dehydrated Tomato Powder: Save skins and ends from the diced tomatoes. Dehydrate in an oven at 70°C (158°F) until brittle. Grind into a fine powder. Store in an airtight container.
Prepare Beef: Pat beef medallions dry with a clean cloth. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper.

Sear Beef: Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Once hot, place beef medallions in the pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) for well-done. Remove beef from pan. Let rest on a cutting board for 5 minutes.
Finish Salsa: Stir fresh cilantro or parsley into the quick fermented bell pepper salsa.

Plate Dish: Place one beef medallion on a handcrafted ceramic plate. Spoon a generous portion of the quick fermented bell pepper salsa next to the beef. Sprinkle a pinch of dehydrated tomato powder over the salsa and plate for visual interest. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Tomato-Bean Ragout
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken is centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. Two whole, golden-brown chicken thighs, cooked to tender perfection, are nestled atop a generous bed of vibrant red tomato and cannellini bean ragout. The ragout, chunky with diced tomatoes and whole white beans, shows a rich, glossy texture. A sprinkle of fresh, bright green chopped parsley provides a contrasting pop of color and freshness over the chicken and ragout. The overall presentation is clean and organized, with moderate negative space on the plate. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a folded natural cotton napkin positioned beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its inviting colors and textures against a subtle, casual restaurant background.

ingredients.name: Canned cannellini beans, drained and rinsed

instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same pan. Cook 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and thyme. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Deglaze with white wine, if using. Scrape up browned bits from the pan. Cook 2 minutes until reduced.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Add drained cannellini beans. Simmer 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until sauce thickens slightly.
Stir in butter until melted and incorporated. Taste and adjust seasoning as needed.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the ragout.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Tomatoes and Oregano
recipes.visual_description: A single, succulent braised chicken thigh, its skin a rich golden-brown, rests on a pristine white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken is nestled in a vibrant, deep red tomato sauce. The sauce is thick with visible chunks of diced tomato and tender, soft pieces of diced onion. Specks of finely minced garlic and dried oregano are integrated throughout the sauce. Fresh green oregano leaves are scattered lightly over the chicken and sauce as a final garnish, adding a pop of color. The composition is balanced and inviting, with moderate negative space around the elements. The plate sits on a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin and classic silver fork and knife are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and rich colors, set against a subtly blurred modern bistro background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce.
Serve alongside polenta or pasta.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large braising pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear for another 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pan.
Add diced onion to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in red wine, if using. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in crushed tomatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a simmer.
Return chicken thighs to the pan, nestling them into the sauce. Ensure chicken is partially submerged.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pan.
Simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and is very tender.
Remove lid for the last 10 minutes if sauce needs to thicken.
Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Sweet & Savory Chicken Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Sweet & Savory Chicken Fruit Salad is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a subtly uneven rim, resting on a well-used, warm-toned wooden dining table. The salad is a vibrant mix of colors: tender, golden-brown glazed chicken cubes are interspersed with bright red cherry tomato halves, sunny yellow pineapple cubes, cool green cucumber cubes, and creamy white cannellini beans. Thinly sliced crimson red onion adds a delicate pop of color. Each ingredient maintains its distinct shape and texture. The glazed chicken pieces are slightly glossy, contrasting with the juicy, soft fruits and firm beans. A scattering of fresh, bright green chopped mint leaves provides a final aromatic and visual accent. The arrangement is natural and casual, with ingredients piled comfortably, as if scooped directly from a family serving bowl. A simple fork with a wooden handle rests beside the bowl on a casually placed linen napkin. Warm, inviting light from a nearby kitchen window illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh, wholesome appeal. The background is softly blurred, showing hints of a lived-in kitchen atmosphere, suggesting a relaxed, comforting meal.
instructions: Pat chicken cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Cook until golden and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove from heat.
In a small bowl, whisk together honey, lime juice, rice vinegar, soy sauce, grated ginger, and red pepper flakes (if using).
Add cooked chicken back to the pan. Pour half of the glaze over the chicken. Toss to coat. Cook for 1-2 minutes until glaze slightly thickens. Remove from heat. Let cool slightly.
Place rinsed cannellini beans in a small saucepan with 50ml water and 1 teaspoon of honey. Simmer gently for 3-4 minutes until warmed through and slightly sweetened. Drain excess liquid. Let cool.
In a large bowl, combine halved cherry tomatoes, diced pineapple, diced cucumber, and thinly sliced red onion. Add the cooled glazed chicken and sweetened cannellini beans.
Pour the remaining glaze over the salad. Add chopped fresh mint. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Poulet à la Moutarde Crème
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared chicken breast, cooked to a golden-brown exterior, rests centered on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The chicken is presented as a whole piece, never fanned. A rich, creamy, pale yellow Dijon mustard sauce is generously spooned over the chicken and pooled elegantly around its base. A few vibrant green fresh tarragon leaves are artfully scattered over the sauce and chicken for garnish. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table surface. A silver fork and knife are placed neatly beside the plate on a crisp white folded cotton napkin. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a refined yet approachable bistro ambiance.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with roasted new potatoes or steamed haricots verts (green beans).
Pair with a dry white wine like Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add minced shallots to the same skillet. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Deglaze skillet with white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom. Simmer 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and Dijon mustard. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes, reducing sauce slightly.
Stir in heavy cream and chopped tarragon. Simmer 2 minutes until sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken to skillet. Spoon sauce over chicken. Heat through for 1 minute.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Chorizo Paella
recipes.visual_description: An individual portion of Chicken and Chorizo Paella is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The rice, vibrant golden-yellow from saffron, forms a cohesive base with visible, distinct grains. Interspersed are tender, browned 3 cm chicken chunks and rich red 1 cm chorizo rounds. Diced red bell pepper and finely diced onion pieces add color and texture. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled generously over the top, and a bright yellow lemon wedge rests at the plate's edge. The presentation is organized but natural. The background features a rustic wooden table, with simple, elegant flatware and a small ceramic bowl for discarded lemon rind, all under soft, natural lighting, creating an authentic Spanish bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, offering extra lemon wedges for squeezing.
Traditionally enjoyed communally from a large paella pan, but individual portions are common in restaurant settings.
Pair with a crisp Spanish white wine or sangria.

ingredients.name: Saffron threads
ingredients.quantity: 0.5 g, steeped in 60 ml hot water

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large paella pan or wide, shallow pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken chunks until browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add chorizo to the pan. Cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered. Remove chorizo. Set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pan. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Stir in minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5 minutes until sauce thickens.
Add rice to the pan. Stir to coat rice in the tomato mixture. Cook for 2 minutes.
Return chicken to the pan. Pour in hot chicken stock and saffron water. Stir gently once.
Bring to a simmer. Distribute ingredients evenly. Do not stir further.
Cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, or until most liquid is absorbed and rice is al dente.
Reduce heat to low. Continue cooking for 5-7 minutes, listening for a crackling sound to form the socarrat.
Remove from heat. Arrange cooked chorizo on top of the paella.
Cover pan with foil or a lid. Let rest for 5-10 minutes.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and lemon wedges before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Corn & Rice Patties with Pickled Radish
recipes.visual_description: The dish presents two golden-brown, delicately crisp corn and rice patties, each approximately 5 cm in diameter, resting on a pristine, matte cream-colored ceramic plate. The patties exhibit a subtly uneven, natural texture from the visible corn kernels and rice grains. Adjacent to the patties, a small, artfully arranged pile of thinly sliced pickled radishes, displaying vibrant shades of fuchsia and translucent pink, adds a pop of color and a contrasting texture. The radishes are cut into perfect rounds. A single, fresh dill sprig and a few small, deep green radish greens are placed sparingly, adding a touch of natural verdancy. The composition embraces ample white space, highlighting the purity of each ingredient. The plate sits on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige tone. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the ingredients' inherent beauty with a clean, unfussy aesthetic.

ingredients.name: Lacto-fermented vegetable brine (e.g., from sauerkraut, kimchi, or pickles)

instructions: Prepare Quick Pickled Radish:
Wash radishes. Thinly slice into rounds using a mandoline or sharp knife.
In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, water, sugar, and salt. Heat gently until sugar and salt dissolve. Do not boil.
Place sliced radishes in a heatproof jar or bowl. Pour warm pickling liquid over radishes.
Let cool to room temperature. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
Prepare Fermented Corn & Rice Patties:
Cut kernels from corn cobs.
In a food processor, combine 200 g of corn kernels, lacto-fermented vegetable brine, salt, and pepper. Process until a coarse paste forms, leaving some texture.
In a large bowl, combine the corn paste, remaining 100 g whole corn kernels, cooked rice, flour, and egg. Mix well until just combined. Do not overmix.
Form mixture into 8 small patties, about 5 cm in diameter and 1.5 cm thick.
Cook Patties:
Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Carefully place patties in the hot pan. Cook for 3-4 minutes per side, until golden brown and cooked through.
Transfer cooked patties to a wire rack to drain excess oil.
Plate and Serve:
On each plate, place two patties.
Arrange a small, neat pile of pickled radish slices next to the patties.
Garnish with a fresh dill sprig and a few washed radish greens.
Serve immediately.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing radish greens and lacto-fermented brine, and encourages the use of seasonal, local ingredients.
Day-old cooked rice works best for the patties, further promoting zero-waste.

recipes.recipe_name: Thai Yellow Curry Noodle Soup
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Thai Yellow Curry Noodle Soup in a deep white porcelain bowl. Golden egg noodles are submerged in a rich, creamy, turmeric-yellow broth, creating a warm, inviting hue. Two halves of a soft-boiled egg, with a bright orange, jammy yolk, are positioned neatly on top. The broth's surface shows subtle flecks of red curry oil and tiny pieces of aromatic lemongrass and ginger. Garnishes are precisely placed: a sprinkle of vibrant green chopped cilantro and delicate, translucent slices of red onion. The overall composition is clean and professional, with moderate negative space. The bowl sits on a simple wooden table surface beside a folded cotton napkin. A pair of dark wooden chopsticks rests across the rim of the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the soup's texture and color. A lime wedge is placed on the side.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lime wedges for fresh acidity.
Offer small dish of chili oil on the side.
Accompany with a side of pickled mustard greens.
Serve in traditional deep ceramic noodle bowls.
Use chopsticks and a ceramic spoon.
instructions: Prepare eggs: Boil water. Gently lower eggs into boiling water. Cook 6-7 minutes. Transfer to ice bath. Peel eggs. Halve each egg.
Cook noodles: Boil egg noodles per package. Drain. Rinse with cold water. Set aside.

Sauté aromatics: Heat oil in large pot over medium heat. Add yellow curry paste. Bruise lemongrass stalks, slice thinly. Peel ginger, slice thinly. Peel turmeric, grate. Add lemongrass, ginger, and turmeric to pot. Sauté 3-4 minutes until fragrant.
Build broth: Stir in miso paste until dissolved. Pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth. Bring to gentle simmer. Stir occasionally.
Season broth: Add brown sugar and soy sauce. Simmer 10-15 minutes. Squeeze juice from 1 lime into broth. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Assemble: Divide noodles among 4 deep serving bowls. Ladle hot curry broth over noodles.
Garnish: Place 2 egg halves on top of each bowl. Chop cilantro. Thinly slice red onion. Garnish bowls with cilantro and red onion. Serve with remaining lime, cut into wedges.
traditional_techniques: Tempering curry paste with oil to release aromatics
Balancing sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavors

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Tomato and Cucumber Chickpea Salad
recipes.visual_description: A generous individual portion of Tomato and Cucumber Chickpea Salad is presented on a simple, round ceramic plate. The salad is casually mounded, showcasing its vibrant colors and varied textures. Bright red diced tomatoes (1.5 cm cubes) and fresh green diced cucumbers (1.5 cm cubes) are interspersed with creamy white chickpeas. Thinly sliced red onion half-moons add a subtle purple hue. Fresh green chopped parsley is sprinkled throughout. The ingredients are lightly coated in a clear, golden-green olive oil and red wine vinegar dressing, which glistens subtly. The arrangement is natural and unpretentious, reflecting a homely meal. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table under warm, natural kitchen lighting, creating a cozy atmosphere. A simple fork and a casually placed linen napkin complete the scene.
instructions: Dice tomatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Dice cucumber into 1.5 cm cubes.
Thinly slice red onion into half-moons.
Rinse and drain chickpeas thoroughly.
Chop fresh parsley.
Combine diced tomatoes, diced cucumber, sliced red onion, chickpeas, and chopped parsley in a large mixing bowl.
In a separate small bowl, whisk together olive oil, red wine vinegar, dried oregano, salt, and black pepper to make the dressing.
Pour the dressing over the salad ingredients.
Toss gently to ensure all ingredients are evenly coated.
Serve immediately or chill for 15 minutes for flavors to meld.

recipes.recipe_name: Broccoli and Chicken Salad
recipes.visual_description: A hearty, homestyle Broccoli and Chicken Salad is presented in an everyday, slightly imperfect ceramic serving bowl on a well-used wooden kitchen table. The salad features small, vibrant green broccoli florets, evenly coated in a creamy, off-white dressing. Shredded or diced cooked chicken pieces are generously mixed throughout. Bright red dried cranberries and chopped pecans add pops of color and textural contrast, alongside finely diced red onion pieces. Ingredients are casually arranged, overlapping naturally, showcasing diverse components. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed cloth napkin. Warm kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, evoking a comfortable, lived-in family dining atmosphere with minimal background clutter, focusing on the wholesome, unpretentious dish.

ingredients.name: Cooked chicken breast, shredded or diced

instructions: Steam or blanch small broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 3-4 minutes. Immediately plunge into ice water. Drain well and pat dry. Chill thoroughly.
If chicken is not pre-cooked, poach or bake chicken breast until internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Cool completely. Shred or dice the chicken into small pieces.
In a large bowl, combine the chilled broccoli, shredded chicken, dried cranberries, chopped pecans, and finely diced red onion.
In a small bowl, whisk together mayonnaise, apple cider vinegar, maple syrup, Dijon mustard, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Pour the dressing over the salad mixture. Toss gently until all ingredients are evenly coated.
Serve immediately or chill for at least 30 minutes for flavors to meld.
notes: This salad is best served chilled.
Adjust sweetness of dressing to personal preference.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Chicken and Autumn Vegetable Bowl
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, inviting individual portion of Roasted Chicken and Autumn Vegetable Bowl is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate, centrally placed on a simple wooden table. A golden-brown, crispy-skinned roasted chicken thigh, whole and un-sliced, is the focal point, resting beside a mound of fluffy brown rice. Surrounding them are substantial, caramelized chunks of butternut squash, tender carrot rounds, and softened red onion wedges, all showing slight charring. The vegetables exhibit warm orange, deep red, and golden hues. Fresh rosemary sprigs and lemon wedges are carefully positioned, adding green and brightness. The plate features balanced negative space. A crisp white cotton napkin and traditional flatware are placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting creates soft shadows, enhancing textures in this modern bistro setting.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Rinse brown rice. Combine rice and 500ml chicken broth in a saucepan. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer 40-45 minutes until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender.
Cut butternut squash into 2.5 cm cubes. Peel carrots and cut into 2.5 cm thick rounds. Cut red onion into 2.5 cm wedges. Smash garlic cloves.
In a large bowl, combine squash, carrots, onion, and garlic. Drizzle with 30ml olive oil. Season with salt, pepper, and chopped rosemary and thyme. Toss to coat.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until skin is golden and crispy. Flip chicken.
Add seasoned vegetables around chicken in the skillet. Transfer skillet to preheated oven.
Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C and vegetables are tender and lightly caramelized.
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest 5 minutes.
To serve, place a bed of brown rice in each bowl. Arrange roasted chicken thigh and vegetables over rice. Garnish with fresh lemon wedges.
notes: The chicken skin becomes wonderfully crisp, and the vegetables soften and sweeten during roasting.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Chicken & Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of creamy Italian Chicken & Broccoli Risotto is presented in a shallow, rustic ceramic bowl on a well-worn wooden kitchen table. The risotto has a fluid, natural consistency, its pale orange hue infused with tomato. Tender, golden-brown chicken breast cubes, approximately 2 cm, are nestled throughout and on top. Bright green broccoli florets, cooked tender-crisp, are visible, some mixed in, some artfully placed on the surface. A generous sprinkle of freshly grated Parmesan cheese melts gently over the top. The scene is bathed in warm, natural kitchen light. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl on a casually placed linen napkin. The background is minimal, suggesting a cozy, lived-in family kitchen.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately while hot.
Offer with crusty bread for dipping.
instructions: Dice chicken breasts into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic. Cut broccoli into small florets.

Heat olive oil in a large, deep pan or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add diced chicken. Cook until golden brown and cooked through, reaching an internal temperature of 75°C. Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Add chopped onion to the same pan. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes (this is the start of the soffritto). Add minced garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the rice kernels.
Pour in white wine, if using. Stir until liquid is absorbed.
Add crushed tomatoes and a ladleful of warm chicken broth. Stir constantly until broth is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each addition to be absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
During the last 5 minutes of cooking, add the broccoli florets to the risotto. Stir until broccoli is tender-crisp.

When rice is al dente and risotto is creamy and fluid, remove from heat. Stir in cooked chicken cubes, butter, and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1 minute to achieve a creamy consistency (mantecatura).
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.
notes: Risotto requires constant stirring and gradual addition of broth for the best creamy texture.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Butternut Squash Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Chicken and Butternut Squash Risotto is elegantly presented in a shallow, wide white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale orange hue from the squash, flows naturally, showcasing its fluid consistency. Golden-brown, seared chicken chunks (2-3 cm) are nestled amongst the rice. Vibrant orange butternut squash cubes (1.5 cm) are visible, alongside bright red halved cherry tomatoes. Specks of fresh basil add green. The texture is rich and velvety, with tender chicken and al dente rice. A light drizzle of extra virgin olive oil glistens, with scattered small fresh basil leaves and fine grated Parmesan. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table, accompanied by a polished fork, spoon, and folded cotton napkin, under soft, natural lighting, reflecting a modern Italian bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with extra grated Parmesan cheese.
A side of crusty bread for 'scarpetta' (mopping up sauce).
A simple green salad.
instructions: Dice chicken thighs into 2-3 cm chunks. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken from pot and set aside. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.

Add another 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add finely diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and butternut squash (1.5 cm cubes). Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring, until squash begins to soften slightly.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of rice grains are translucent.
Pour in white wine (if using). Stir until fully absorbed.

Add a ladle of warm chicken broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed. Continue adding broth, one ladle at a time, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. Stir frequently.
After about 10 minutes of adding broth, return seared chicken to the pot. Add dried oregano. Continue adding broth and stirring.
Cook for approximately 18-20 minutes total, or until rice is al dente and creamy. Risotto should be fluid. Stir in halved cherry tomatoes for the last 3-4 minutes.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan cheese until melted and incorporated. Add chopped fresh basil. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately.
notes: Use good quality chicken broth for best flavor.
Risotto requires constant attention and stirring.

recipes.recipe_name: Rustic Baked Chicken with Roasted Garlic Tomatoes and Broccoli
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of a hearty, comforting meal presented on a round, rustic ceramic plate. Two golden-brown, baked chicken thighs are positioned centrally. Around the chicken, a cluster of vibrant red cherry tomatoes, some slightly burst, intermingle with tender, golden-roasted garlic cloves. Alongside, bright green broccoli florets, steamed to a tender-crisp texture, add a fresh contrast. A generous scoop of fluffy white long-grain rice, subtly mixed with grated Parmesan cheese, sits beside the other components. The dish is casually arranged, with ingredients touching and overlapping naturally. A scattering of fresh green chopped parsley garnishes the chicken and vegetables. The scene is set on a well-used wooden dining table, with warm, natural kitchen lighting. A simple fork and knife rest beside the plate, with a casually folded cloth napkin nearby, evoking a relaxed, family dining atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot as a family dinner.
Pair with a simple green salad.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Pat chicken thighs dry. Season chicken with salt, pepper, and dried oregano.
In a large baking dish, combine halved cherry tomatoes and half of the minced garlic. Drizzle with 15ml olive oil. Toss to coat.
Place seasoned chicken thighs on top of the tomatoes and garlic in the baking dish.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C.
While chicken bakes, cook rice. Rinse rice under cold water until clear.
In a medium saucepan, combine rice, chicken broth, remaining minced garlic, and a pinch of salt. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 15-18 minutes, or until liquid is absorbed and rice is tender. Do not lift lid during cooking.
Remove from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff with a fork. Stir in grated Parmesan cheese.
Steam broccoli florets until tender-crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Alternatively, toss broccoli with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper, and roast alongside chicken for the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Serve one chicken thigh per plate. Arrange roasted tomatoes, garlic, and broccoli next to chicken. Serve with a generous portion of Parmesan rice.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A thick, golden-brown seared pork chop rests prominently on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. The chop exhibits a beautifully caramelized crust, indicating a perfect sear, and appears juicy. A rich, velvety cream sauce, studded with tender, earthy brown mushroom slices and flecks of fresh parsley, is elegantly spooned over and around the pork. Beside the chop, a neat bundle of vibrant green, tender-crisp roasted asparagus spears adds a pop of color and freshness. The plate is positioned on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by classic silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin, evoking a modern bistro setting. Natural, soft light illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and inviting presentation. The entire plate is visible, showcasing a balanced and professional single serving.
instructions: Pat pork chops dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat.
Sear pork chops 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer chops to a plate. Keep warm.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to skillet. Add sliced cremini mushrooms. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add finely diced shallots and minced garlic. Sauté 2 minutes until fragrant.
Pour in dry white wine. Scrape up browned bits from bottom of skillet. Reduce by half, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and fresh thyme sprigs. Bring to a simmer. Cook 5 minutes until slightly reduced.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer 3-5 minutes until sauce thickens to desired consistency. Season with salt and pepper.
Return pork chops to skillet with sauce. Spoon sauce over chops. Cook 2-3 minutes or until heated through.
Meanwhile, toss asparagus with a drizzle of olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast in a preheated 200°C oven for 8-10 minutes until tender-crisp.
Remove thyme sprigs from sauce. Garnish sauce with fresh chopped parsley. Serve pork chops immediately with mushroom cream sauce and roasted asparagus.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb and Chicken Harira
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Lamb and Chicken Harira is presented in a deep, rustic, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. The rich, reddish-brown broth is thick, showcasing tender, diced lamb and chicken cubes, visible whole brown lentils, and plump beige chickpeas. Finely diced onion and celery are discernible within the hearty soup. A vibrant sprinkle of fresh, chopped parsley and cilantro garnishes the top, adding a pop of green. A small, bright yellow lemon wedge rests on the bowl's rim or casually beside it. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table. Nearby, a few pitted dates and a piece of traditional Moroccan chebakia are casually arranged on a small, simple ceramic plate, alongside a plain, textured cloth napkin. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft kitchen lighting, creating a comforting, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with lemon wedges
Serve with dates
Serve with chebakia (Moroccan honey cookies)
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add diced lamb and chicken. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove meat from pot.
Add diced onion and celery to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in turmeric, ginger, cinnamon, black pepper, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return seared meat to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes and tomato paste. Stir well.
Add rinsed lentils, drained chickpeas, and 1.5 litres of water or stock. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 60 minutes, or until lamb is tender and chicken reaches 75°C internal temperature. Stir occasionally.
In a small bowl, whisk together flour and 60ml cold water until smooth. This is the 'tadwira'.
Slowly pour the tadwira into the simmering soup while stirring continuously. Cook for 5-10 minutes, stirring, until soup thickens slightly.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley and cilantro. Season with salt to taste.
Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Individual Chicken and Potato Gratin
recipes.visual_description: A single individual Chicken and Potato Gratin, presented as a small starter portion on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The gratin is served directly in its small, round, oven-safe ramekin, showcasing its golden-brown, bubbling top crust with hints of melted Gruyere cheese. Visible beneath the crust are creamy, thinly sliced potato rounds (approximately 1-2 mm thick), tender, seared chicken cubes (1.5 cm pieces), and deep amber caramelized onion slices. The dish exhibits a rich, savory aroma. A fresh sprig of green thyme rests delicately on the side of the ramekin or plate, providing a contrasting color and fresh element. The plate is positioned on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, characteristic of a modern bistro setting. Natural, even lighting highlights the textures and colors of the dish. A folded cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The background is clean and slightly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere. The entire plate is visible, with moderate negative space surrounding the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside a small, simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer with a slice of crusty baguette.

ingredients.name: Potatoes (starchy, e.g., Russet)
ingredients.quantity: 300 g, peeled and thinly sliced (1-2 mm thick)

ingredients.name: Fresh thyme
ingredients.quantity: 2-3 sprigs, leaves picked (plus extra for garnish)

instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Grease four individual gratin dishes or ramekins (approx. 100-120 ml capacity).

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Season chicken cubes with salt and pepper. Sear chicken for 3-4 minutes until browned on all sides. Do not cook through. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.
Add butter to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add sliced onion. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized and soft.
Add minced garlic to the pan with onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in heavy cream and chicken stock. Add picked thyme leaves. Bring to a gentle simmer. Season sauce with salt and pepper. Remove from heat.

Arrange a layer of thinly sliced potatoes in the bottom of each prepared ramekin. Top with a layer of seared chicken cubes and caramelized onions. Repeat layers until ramekins are full, ending with a potato layer.
Pour the cream mixture evenly over the potatoes and chicken in each ramekin. Ensure liquid covers most of the potatoes.
Sprinkle grated Gruyere cheese over the top of each gratin (if using).
Bake for 25-35 minutes, or until potatoes are tender and the top is golden brown and bubbling. Insert a meat thermometer into the thickest part of a chicken piece; it should read 75°C.
Let gratins rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh thyme sprigs.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Slicing potatoes very thinly ensures even cooking and a creamy texture.
Caramelizing onions slowly develops deep, sweet flavors essential to the dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Beef and Mushroom Pie with Cheesy Garlic Potato Topping
recipes.visual_description: A robust, individual portion of a layered beef and mushroom pie is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate, centered on a simple wooden table. The top layer of cheesy garlic mashed potato is golden-brown with visible peaks and valleys, showing a slightly crispy texture. Beneath, the rich, dark brown beef and mushroom filling is visible at the edges, showcasing tender, irregular chunks of beef and quartered cremini mushrooms. A subtle, creamy layer of white rice forms the base. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of bright green chopped fresh parsley, providing a vibrant color contrast. The overall composition is professional and inviting, with moderate negative space. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish’s hearty textures and warm, earthy colors. A folded cotton napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate, completing a casual dining aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a fresh green salad with a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread for dipping into the rich sauce.
instructions: Cut beef chuck into 3cm cubes. Season beef with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef cubes until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Dice onion, carrots, and celery. Add diced vegetables to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened.
Mince 2 garlic cloves. Add minced garlic and tomato paste to the pot. Cook for 1 minute.
Deglaze with red wine, scraping up any browned bits. Cook until wine mostly evaporates.
Stir in flour. Cook for 1 minute.
Return beef to the pot. Add beef broth, thyme sprigs, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer. Cover and braise in a preheated 160°C oven for 2 hours, or until beef is tender.
Quarter cremini mushrooms. After 2 hours, add mushrooms to the beef mixture. Continue braising for another 30 minutes, uncovered, until mushrooms are tender and sauce thickens slightly.
Cook Arborio rice according to package instructions. Fluff with a fork.
Peel and cut Russet potatoes into 2cm chunks. Boil potatoes in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Mince remaining 2 garlic cloves. Return potatoes to the pot. Add milk, butter, minced garlic, salt, and pepper. Mash until smooth and creamy. Stir in grated cheddar cheese until melted and combined.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Spread cooked rice evenly in the bottom of a large oven-safe baking dish (approx. 20x30cm).
Spoon the beef and mushroom mixture over the rice layer.
Carefully spread the cheesy garlic mashed potato topping over the beef mixture, creating a rustic, even layer.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the potato topping is golden brown and bubbly. If desired, broil for the last 2-3 minutes for extra crispness.
Chop fresh parsley. Garnish the baked pie with fresh parsley before serving.
notes: Ensure beef is very tender before adding mushrooms for the final braising period.
The rice layer absorbs some of the beef juices, adding another layer of flavor and texture to this hearty dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Spring Vegetable Risotto with Toasted Almonds
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of vibrant Spring Vegetable Risotto is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl, positioned on a simple light wooden table. The risotto is creamy and free-flowing, showcasing a rich, golden hue with visible bursts of bright yellow corn kernels, tender green peas, and small diced orange carrots. Interspersed among the grains are roughly chopped, slightly wilted spinach leaves, adding a deeper green contrast. A generous sprinkling of golden-brown toasted almond slivers crowns the dish, providing a textural counterpoint. A subtle drizzle of glistening extra virgin olive oil enhances its sheen. The overall presentation is natural and organic, emphasizing the dish's fresh ingredients and inviting texture, with appropriate negative space around the food. A simple set of standard silver flatware and a neatly folded white cotton napkin rest beside the bowl, completing the modern bistro setting under even, natural lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto should be enjoyed fresh and creamy.
Offer additional grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
instructions: Warm vegetable broth in a saucepan. Keep it simmering.
Toast sliced almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden. Set aside.
Peel and small dice carrots. Roughly chop spinach. Mince shallot and garlic.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add minced shallot. Cook until translucent, about 3 minutes.
Add minced garlic and diced carrots. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add Arborio rice. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until grains are slightly translucent at the edges.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladle of warm broth to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is absorbed.
Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. This takes about 18-20 minutes.
When rice is almost al dente (creamy outside, slight bite in the center), add corn and green peas. Stir for 2 minutes.
Stir in spinach. Cook until spinach just wilts.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter, grated Parmesan, lemon zest, and a squeeze of lemon juice. This is 'mantecare'.
Stir vigorously until risotto is creamy and flowing. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle risotto immediately into warm bowls. Drizzle with remaining 30 ml olive oil. Garnish with toasted almonds.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Roasted Carrots, Corn, and Toasted Almonds
recipes.visual_description: A pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and perfectly cooked, sits prominently on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The chicken, presented whole, has a tender, juicy appearance. Alongside, vibrant orange carrot batons are artfully arranged, showing a slight caramelization from roasting. A colorful medley of bright yellow corn kernels and vivid green peas is spooned beside the chicken, glistening with a light pan sauce. A bed of subtly wilted, deep green spinach provides a soft contrast beneath the chicken. Toasted slivered almonds are scattered over the dish, adding a delicate crunch and visual texture. Fresh chopped parsley provides a final touch of bright green garnish. The plate is well-proportioned with appropriate negative space, showcasing a single, refined individual portion. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table surface, with standard flatware (fork and knife) and a folded cotton napkin placed beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh ingredients and professional preparation. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere without distraction.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Cut carrots into 5cm batons. Toss carrots with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast on a baking sheet for 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized.
Heat a dry pan over medium heat. Add slivered almonds. Toast for 3-5 minutes, stirring frequently, until golden brown. Remove and set aside.

Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat 15ml olive oil in a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Sear chicken breasts for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown. Transfer skillet to preheated oven. Bake for 10-12 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet. Rest on a cutting board.

While chicken rests, add remaining 15ml olive oil to the same skillet over medium heat. Add shallot and minced garlic. Sauté for 2 minutes until fragrant. Add chicken stock and lemon zest. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 3-5 minutes, scraping up any browned bits, until sauce slightly reduces. Stir in lemon juice.
In a separate pot, bring water to a boil. Blanch corn kernels and green peas for 2 minutes. Drain well. Add blanched corn and peas to the skillet with the sauce. Toss to coat and heat through.
In the same pot used for blanching, wilt spinach with a splash of water or remaining olive oil for 1-2 minutes. Drain excess liquid.

To plate, place a bed of wilted spinach on each clean white porcelain dinner plate. Arrange one pan-seared chicken breast on top. Place roasted carrot batons alongside. Spoon the corn and pea medley next to the chicken. Drizzle with pan sauce. Sprinkle toasted slivered almonds and fresh chopped parsley over the dish. Serve immediately with a lemon wedge.

recipes.recipe_name: Green Pea and Yogurt Kofta Curry with Cherry Chutney
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, white ceramic plate, hinting at a modern bistro setting. A single portion features 3-4 golden-brown, spherical green pea and yogurt koftas, nestled in a vibrant, creamy orange-red yogurt curry. The curry has a smooth, rich texture, with visible specks of green coriander. A small, separate ramekin beside the main plate holds the deep ruby-red cherry chutney, its chunky texture visible with softened cherry pieces and finely diced onion. The koftas are whole, perfectly round. The plate is moderately spaced, allowing the dish to breathe. Fresh green coriander sprigs are scattered over the curry. A simple cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. The scene is bathed in soft, natural, even lighting. Traditional Indian flatware is placed alongside the plate, suggesting authentic dining.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with fresh naan bread for dipping.
Accompanied by steamed basmati rice.
Offer a side of cooling raita.
instructions: For the Green Pea & Yogurt Kofta:
Blanch green peas in boiling water for 2 minutes. Drain and cool.
Mash peas coarsely. Do not make a paste.
In a bowl, combine mashed peas, hung yogurt, crumbled paneer, gram flour, chopped green chili, grated ginger, cumin powder, coriander powder, and salt. Mix well to form a dough.
Divide mixture into 12 equal portions. Shape into smooth, round koftas.
Heat oil in a deep pan to 170°C.
Gently deep fry koftas in batches until golden brown and cooked through. Drain on paper towels.
For the Yogurt Curry:
Heat oil in a large pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onions. Sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and slit green chilies. Sauté for 1 minute until aromatic.
Reduce heat to low. Add turmeric, coriander, cumin, and red chili powders. Stir for 30 seconds.
Remove pan from heat. Gradually whisk in the plain yogurt to prevent curdling.
Return pan to low heat. Cook, stirring constantly, until the curry comes to a gentle simmer and oil separates. This may take 5-7 minutes.
Add water and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Just before serving, gently add the fried koftas to the simmering curry. Simmer for 2-3 minutes to absorb flavors.
Stir in garam masala. Garnish with fresh coriander.
For the Cherry Chutney:
In a small saucepan, combine pitted cherries, diced red onion, apple cider vinegar, sugar, mustard seeds, red chili flakes, and salt.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat.
Cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until cherries break down and mixture thickens to a chutney consistency.
Remove from heat. Let cool.
notes: Ensure yogurt for koftas is thick (hung curd) to help bind.
Whisk yogurt well for curry before adding to heat to prevent curdling.
Add koftas to curry just before serving to maintain their texture.
traditional_techniques: Slow cooking yogurt curry to prevent curdling

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Pea Risotto with Charred Cherries
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of creamy Fermented Pea Risotto is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The risotto forms a fluid, organic mound, its pale green hue showcasing the embedded whole peas and their vibrant color. Charred cherries, deep red with slightly darkened edges, are clustered naturally on top. A clean, subtle swirl of plain white yogurt contrasts with the risotto. Fresh mint leaves are sparsely scattered for a touch of natural green. The plate rests on a light reclaimed wood surface. An undyed linen napkin is subtly placed. Soft, natural light illuminates the dish. The background is minimalist, with a hint of blurred natural elements.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately as a main course.
Accompanied by a simple side salad with foraged greens.
Pair with a glass of natural, biodynamic wine.

ingredients.name: Green Peas (fresh or frozen, 200g for fermenting, 200g fresh)

instructions: Prepare Fermented Peas: Blend 200g green peas with 50g plain yogurt and a pinch of salt. Transfer to a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 24-48 hours until tangy. Refrigerate.
Prepare Pea Pod Stock: If using fresh peas in pods, simmer clean pea pods with water for 30 minutes. Strain liquid. Use this as vegetable broth. If using frozen peas, use regular vegetable broth.
Char Cherries: Heat a dry pan over medium-high heat. Add pitted cherries. Cook until slightly softened and charred in spots, about 5-7 minutes. Set aside.
Sauté Aromatics: Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Toast Rice: Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes until rice edges are translucent.
Deglaze: Add a splash of warm vegetable broth. Stir until absorbed.

Cook Risotto: Gradually add remaining warm vegetable broth, one ladle at a time. Stir constantly. Wait for liquid to be almost absorbed before adding the next ladle. Continue for 15-18 minutes until rice is al dente and creamy.
Add Peas and Flavor: Stir in the remaining 200g fresh or frozen green peas. Cook until tender. Stir in the fermented pea-yogurt mixture. Stir in nutritional yeast.
Finish Risotto: Remove pot from heat. Stir in half of the remaining plain yogurt, fresh lemon juice, and lemon zest. Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Risotto should be creamy and fluid.

Plate: Ladle risotto onto shallow, individual plates. Create a small well in the center of the risotto. Spoon charred cherries into the well. Swirl the remaining plain yogurt around the risotto. Garnish with fresh mint leaves.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing pea pods for a flavorful vegetable stock.
Adjust fermentation time for the peas based on desired tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Sourdough Flatbread with Avocado-Tahini Crema and Preserved Sun-dried Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Fermented Sourdough Flatbread is presented on a large, flat, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. The substantial, golden-brown flatbread, with its naturally irregular, slightly puffed surface, occupies the center, perhaps torn organically into two or three pieces. A generous, smooth swoosh of pale green avocado-tahini crema is artfully spread across a section of the bread or placed delicately to its side, showcasing its creamy texture. Vibrant, deep red chopped sun-dried tomatoes are scattered thoughtfully over the crema and bread, providing bursts of rich color. A few translucent, thinly sliced radish rounds are strategically placed for a subtle pop of white and pink. A delicate drizzle of golden white wine reduction glistens across the dish. The plating is minimalistic, emphasizing natural forms and textures, with ample negative space. The setting features a light, textured bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, natural light illuminating the dish from the side. The background is clean and unobtrusive, perhaps with a subtle hint of a green plant.
instructions: Prepare sourdough flatbread dough: In a large bowl, combine sourdough starter, warm water, bread flour, and salt. Mix until shaggy. Cover and let rest 30 minutes.
Add 15ml olive oil to dough. Knead gently for 2 minutes. Cover and ferment at room temperature for 4-6 hours, or until doubled. Alternatively, cold ferment in refrigerator for 12-24 hours.
Punch down dough gently. Divide into 4 equal portions. Roll each portion into a thin oval or round flatbread. Brush lightly with olive oil.
Preheat oven to 220°C (425°F) with a baking stone or inverted baking sheet inside. Carefully transfer flatbreads to hot stone/sheet.
Bake 8-12 minutes, or until golden brown and puffed. Remove and cool slightly.
Make avocado-tahini crema: In a food processor, combine avocados, tahini, lemon juice, 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Blend until smooth and creamy. Add a tablespoon of water if too thick.
Prepare white wine reduction: In a small saucepan, bring white wine to a simmer over medium heat. Reduce until thickened to a light syrup consistency, about 5-7 minutes. Cool slightly.
Assemble: Spread a generous amount of avocado-tahini crema onto each warm flatbread. Scatter chopped sun-dried tomatoes over the crema.
Arrange thin slices of radish on top. Drizzle with white wine reduction. Garnish with fresh parsley or chives.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Pork Belly with Ginger and Steamed Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Braised Pork Belly with Ginger and Steamed Rice is presented in a clean, white ceramic bowl, resting on a simple wooden table. Three to four succulent, dark mahogany braised pork belly chunks, approximately 4-5 cm cubes, are nestled on one side of the bowl. The pork glistens with a rich, glossy, reduced sauce, showcasing its tender texture. Beside the pork, a pristine mound of fluffy white steamed jasmine rice provides a clean contrast. The dish is vibrant with color: bright green chopped scallions are scattered generously over the pork, complemented by delicate julienned ginger strips. A pair of dark chopsticks rests beside the bowl on a simple chopstick rest. The composition is balanced and inviting, with natural, even lighting highlighting the food's appeal against a subtly blurred, restaurant-style background, suggesting a casual yet refined dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve in individual ceramic bowls with a small ceramic spoon for the sauce.
Offer chopsticks as the primary utensil.
Accompany with a small side dish of quick-pickled cucumber or daikon for a refreshing contrast.

ingredients.name: Pork Belly
ingredients.quantity: 1 kg, skin on, cut into 4-5 cm cubes

ingredients.name: Fresh Ginger
ingredients.quantity: 100 g, 70g sliced thickly, 30g julienned for garnish

instructions: Place pork belly cubes in a large pot. Cover with cold water. Bring to a boil. Skim off impurities. Boil for 5 minutes. Drain pork. Rinse well with warm water. Set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add pork belly cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove excess fat if desired.
Add thick ginger slices and smashed garlic to the pot. Stir-fry for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in Shaoxing wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and water or broth. Add rock sugar, star anise, and cinnamon stick.
Bring liquid to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until pork is fork-tender. Stir occasionally.

While pork braises, rinse jasmine rice thoroughly under cold water. Combine rice and 450 ml water in a rice cooker or saucepan. Cook according to rice cooker instructions or until water is absorbed and rice is fluffy.
Once pork is tender, remove lid from pot. Increase heat to medium-high. Reduce sauce until thickened and glossy, stirring frequently. Remove star anise and cinnamon stick.
Taste and adjust seasoning if needed.
Spoon steamed jasmine rice into individual serving bowls. Arrange 3-4 pieces of braised pork belly beside the rice. Drizzle generously with the reduced sauce.
Garnish pork with chopped green onions and julienned fresh ginger. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure pork belly is blanched thoroughly to remove impurities for a cleaner braising liquid.
The internal temperature of pork should reach 63°C (145°F) for doneness, but braising to tenderness will exceed this.

recipes.recipe_name: Salsa de Lentejas y Elote con Chipotle
