Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until the edges of the grains are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.

Add one ladleful of hot vegetable broth to the rice. Stir continuously until the broth is almost completely absorbed. Continue adding broth one ladleful at a time, allowing each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. Stir constantly. This process takes about 18-20 minutes. The rice should be creamy and al dente.

Remove the pot from heat. Stir in the sautéed apple cubes, remaining 20 g butter, and 60 g vegetarian Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously until the risotto is creamy and well combined. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately in warm bowls. Garnish each serving with reserved caramelized onions and a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Tofu Steaks with Fermented Cherry-Chili Chutney and Parsnip-Potato Puree
recipes.visual_description: A single, sustainably portioned dish is presented on a matte, natural-toned ceramic plate. A thick, rectangular smoked tofu steak, pan-seared to a golden-brown crust, rests centrally. Beside it, a generous, smooth quenelle of creamy parsnip-potato puree, its light beige color contrasting with the plate. A vibrant dollop of rich, dark red fermented cherry-chili chutney is spooned next to the tofu, showcasing small pieces of cherry and chili flecks. The dish is garnished sparingly with fresh, finely chopped chives, providing a subtle pop of green. The overall presentation is clean and minimalistic, with ample negative space. The plate is set on a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by a simple undyed linen napkin. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, enhancing textures and colors, creating an eco-conscious and inviting feel.

ingredients.name: Red Chilies, deseeded and finely chopped

instructions: Prepare the Fermented Cherry-Chili Chutney: Combine 150g pitted cherries, 1 chopped red chili, 15ml apple cider vinegar, and a pinch of salt in a clean jar. Cover loosely. Ferment at room temperature for 3-5 days, burping daily, until tangy. (Alternatively, for quick chutney: skip fermentation and use all fresh cherries, add all vinegar and maple syrup directly to the pan).
Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Slice tofu into four thick rectangular steaks.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Sear tofu steaks for 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and crispy. Set aside.
For the Parsnip-Potato Puree: Place chopped parsnips and potatoes in a pot. Cover with water. Bring to a boil. Cook until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well.
Return cooked parsnips and potatoes to the pot. Add 200ml vegetable broth, 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Mash until smooth and creamy. Keep warm.
For the Cherry-Chili Chutney: In the same pan, add remaining 15ml olive oil. Sauté diced onion, minced garlic, and grated ginger for 3-4 minutes until fragrant.

Add remaining 50g fresh pitted cherries (if using quick method, add all 200g now), remaining chopped red chili, fermented cherry-chili mixture (if using), 35ml apple cider vinegar, 15ml maple syrup, and smoked paprika. Stir well.
Bring to a simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chutney thickens and cherries break down. Season with salt and pepper to taste.

To serve: Spoon a generous portion of parsnip-potato puree onto each plate. Place a seared tofu steak on top or beside the puree. Spoon a dollop of the cherry-chili chutney next to the tofu. Garnish with fresh chopped chives or parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Dry-Aged Ribeye with Black Garlic Purée, Braised Baby Leeks, and Beef Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A single, impeccably seared dry-aged beef ribeye, cooked to a perfect medium-rare with a deep, caramelized crust, rests as the focal point. Adjacent to it, a smooth, glossy swipe of dark, almost charcoal-grey black garlic purée adds an organic curve. Two slender, vibrant green braised baby leek halves are precisely positioned, offering a subtle color contrast. A delicate scattering of whole, dark fermented black beans provides tiny, intriguing textural accents. A shallow, crystal-clear pool of amber beef consommé encircles the elements, reflecting light. The plating is minimalist, with abundant negative space on a pristine white bone china plate. The scene is set on a polished grey veined marble surface, with a crisply folded white linen napkin. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting the dish's architectural precision and premium ingredients.
instructions: Prepare Beef Consommé: Combine beef stock, diced carrot, celery, and onion in a pot. Bring to a simmer. Whisk egg whites until frothy. Gently fold egg whites into simmering stock. Continue to simmer, without stirring, for 20 minutes. A raft will form. Carefully ladle clear consommé through a fine-mesh sieve lined with cheesecloth. Season lightly with salt. Keep warm.

Make Black Garlic Purée: In a small saucepan, combine black garlic cloves, 10g butter, and 50ml beef stock. Simmer gently for 5 minutes until softened. Transfer to a high-speed blender. Blend until perfectly smooth. Season with salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Keep warm.

Braise Baby Leeks: Trim and clean baby leeks. Halve them lengthwise if large. In a shallow pan, melt 20g butter. Add leeks and sauté briefly. Pour in vegetable stock. Bring to a simmer. Cover and braise gently for 10-15 minutes until tender. Season with salt. Keep warm.

Cook Beef Ribeye: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat beef steaks dry. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper. Heat olive oil in a heavy-bottomed, oven-safe pan over high heat until shimmering. Carefully place steaks in the hot pan. Sear for 3 minutes per side until a deep brown crust forms. Add remaining butter to the pan. Baste steaks for 1 minute. Transfer pan to preheated oven. Roast for 6-8 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 54-57°C). Adjust time for desired doneness. Remove from oven. Rest steaks on a wire rack for 10 minutes.

Plate the Dish: Place a rested ribeye steak as the central anchor on each plate. Create a precise swipe or dollop of black garlic purée beside the steak. Arrange two braised baby leek halves artfully alongside. Scatter a few whole fermented black beans around the plate for textural and umami contrast. Gently pour a small amount of warm beef consommé around the base of the plated elements, creating a delicate pool. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Panang-Glazed Duck Breast with Rhubarb-Almond Puree and Tapioca Crisp
recipes.visual_description: The dish embodies sophisticated minimalism on a pristine white bone china plate, featuring abundant negative space. Three thick, succulent slices of pan-seared duck breast, with perfectly rendered, golden-crisp skin and a glistening, deep reddish-brown Panang glaze, are positioned off-center. The duck reveals a rosy pink interior. An organic sweep of vibrant, pale pink rhubarb-almond puree provides soft textural contrast. A delicate, translucent tapioca crisp, with an irregular edge, stands elegantly upright, adding architectural height. A small, perfectly formed quenelle of ethereal whipped cream cheese rests near the puree. Microgreens or chili threads offer a precise color accent. The composition sits on polished white Carrara marble, illuminated by dramatic, directional lighting. A pristine white linen napkin and minimalist silver flatware complete the luxurious setting.
instructions: Prepare Duck: Score duck breast skin in a crosshatch pattern. Do not cut into meat. Season skin with salt and pepper.

Render Duck Fat: Place duck breasts skin-side down in a cold, heavy-bottomed pan. Heat pan over medium-low heat. Cook slowly for 12-15 minutes until skin is golden brown and crisp, and fat is rendered. Pour off excess fat periodically.

Sear & Finish Duck: Flip duck breasts meat-side down. Sear for 2 minutes. Transfer pan to preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Roast for 6-8 minutes for medium-rare (internal temperature 54-57°C). Rest duck breasts on a cutting board for 5 minutes before slicing.

Make Rhubarb-Almond Puree: Chop rhubarb into 2cm pieces. In a small saucepan, combine rhubarb, sugar, and 15ml water. Cook over medium heat until rhubarb softens, about 8-10 minutes. Stir in blanched almonds. Transfer mixture to a blender. Blend until very smooth. Season with a pinch of salt. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultra-smoothness. Keep warm.

Prepare Panang Glaze: In a small saucepan, combine Panang curry paste, chicken stock, and coconut milk. Bring to a simmer over medium heat, stirring constantly. Reduce heat to low and simmer for 5-7 minutes until slightly thickened. Stir in lime juice and butter. Season with salt to taste. Keep warm.

Form Tapioca Crisps: In a small bowl, whisk tapioca starch with 100ml water until smooth. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Pour 1 tablespoon of mixture onto the hot pan, spreading thinly with the back of a spoon to create an irregular shape. Cook until edges crisp and center is translucent, about 2-3 minutes. Carefully lift with a spatula and transfer to a wire rack to cool and harden. Repeat for remaining mixture.
Whip Cream Cheese: In a small bowl, whisk cream cheese until smooth and light. Season with a tiny pinch of salt.

Plate Dish (per serving): Slice each duck breast crosswise into 2-3 thick pieces. Arrange duck pieces off-center on a pristine white plate. Create an organic 'swoosh' or irregular shape of rhubarb-almond puree beside the duck. Drizzle Panang glaze artfully over and around the duck. Place one tapioca crisp upright or leaning against the duck. Add a small quenelle or dot of whipped cream cheese near the puree. Garnish minimally with microgreens or chili threads.

recipes.recipe_name: Spanish Braised Chicken with Saffron Potatoes and White Beans
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Spanish Braised Chicken with Saffron Potatoes and White Beans is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. Two whole, tender, golden-brown boneless chicken thighs are placed centrally, nestled amongst rich, rust-red sauce. Surrounding the chicken are irregular 3cm chunks of tender, pale yellow Yukon Gold potatoes and creamy white cannellini beans. Diced red bell pepper and softened onion pieces are visible within the thick, aromatic sauce, which has a slight sheen. The dish is generously sprinkled with vibrant green, freshly chopped flat-leaf parsley. The overall presentation is inviting and rustic, yet refined, with ample negative space on the plate. The plate rests on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface, accompanied by a folded cream-colored cotton napkin and traditional silver flatware. Natural, soft, even light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's vibrant colors and textures against a subtly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread (e.g., pan de pueblo) for dipping into the sauce.
A simple green salad with a vinaigrette can accompany the meal.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs until golden brown on all sides, about 3-4 minutes per side. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add diced onion and red bell pepper to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and smoked paprika. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant, stirring constantly.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, chicken broth, bloomed saffron, and bay leaf. Bring to a simmer.
Add potato chunks to the pot. Return seared chicken thighs to the pot. Ensure chicken is mostly submerged.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through (internal temperature 75°C) and potatoes are tender.
Stir in rinsed cannellini beans. Cook for another 5 minutes to heat through.
Remove bay leaf. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve hot, garnished generously with fresh chopped parsley.
notes: For deeper flavor, allow the dish to rest for 10-15 minutes after cooking.
This dish can be made ahead; flavors often improve the next day.

recipes.recipe_name: One-Pot Chicken and Rice Pilaf
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of One-Pot Chicken and Rice Pilaf rests centrally on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate with natural imperfections. The dish features a golden-brown, seared chicken thigh, its skin slightly crisped, positioned atop a bed of fluffy, light brown long-grain rice. The rice is naturally mounded, interwoven with small, soft orange diced carrots and translucent diced onions, adding subtle color. A scattering of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley provides a natural garnish, contrasting with the warm tones of the chicken and rice. The chicken thigh is presented whole, showing its rustic, home-cooked appeal. The plate sits on a well-used wooden dining table, illuminated by warm, inviting kitchen light. A simple cloth napkin and a standard fork and knife are casually placed beside the plate, completing the homely family kitchen scene.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken thighs, skin-side down, until golden brown and crispy, about 6-8 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes.
Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion and diced carrot to the pot. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic and dried thyme. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in rice until coated with oil and aromatics, about 1 minute.
Pour in chicken broth. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a boil.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up, nestling them into the rice.
Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot tightly. Simmer for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Do not lift the lid during cooking.
Remove pot from heat. Let stand, covered, for 10 minutes.
Check internal temperature of chicken; it should be 75°C (167°F).
Fluff rice gently with a fork. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Panang Rhubarb & Tapioca Comfort Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion of Panang Rhubarb & Tapioca Comfort Soup is presented in an everyday ceramic bowl, possibly with minor chips or imperfections. The bowl is generously filled with the creamy, warm orange-hued soup. Small, softened pieces of diced rhubarb are visible, along with translucent, chewy small pearl tapioca adding a unique texture. A creamy white swirl of melted cream cheese is subtly visible on top, blending into the curry. A scattering of golden-brown toasted almond slivers provides a textural contrast and crunch. A few fresh green cilantro leaves are casually placed on the surface. The bowl rests on a well-used, light wooden dining table, perhaps with faint rings or scratches, next to a slightly crumpled cloth napkin or a paper towel. In the background, hints of a lived-in kitchen environment with soft, warm lighting from an overhead fixture suggest a cozy, familial meal.
instructions: Heat cooking oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add panang curry paste to the pot. Sauté for 1 minute, stirring constantly, until fragrant.
Add small diced rhubarb to the pot. Cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring, until slightly softened.
Pour in coconut milk and vegetable broth. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer.
Stir in the small pearl tapioca. Continue to simmer for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tapioca pearls are translucent and the soup has slightly thickened.
Remove the pot from heat. Add the softened cream cheese. Stir vigorously until the cream cheese is fully melted and incorporated, creating a smooth, creamy soup.
Season the soup with salt to taste. Squeeze in the juice from half a lime for brightness.
Ladle the hot soup into individual serving bowls.
Garnish each bowl with toasted almond slivers and a few fresh cilantro or basil leaves.

recipes.recipe_name: Quick-Pickled Corn and Black Bean Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant Quick-Pickled Corn and Black Bean Salad is presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in an earthy cream tone. The plate is set on a light bamboo table surface, reflecting a minimalist, natural aesthetic. The salad features a colorful medley of textures: bright yellow corn kernels, dark black beans, small diced red and green bell peppers, and creamy small diced avocado. Thinly sliced, translucent purple quick-pickled red onion ribbons are artfully interspersed. Freshly chopped green cilantro leaves are sprinkled throughout. The ingredients are loosely arranged, allowing ample white space on the plate, highlighting the natural beauty of each component. The dressing lightly coats the salad, adding a subtle sheen. The background is clean and uncluttered, with soft natural light illuminating the dish. A simple, undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually placed beside the plate. The overall presentation is ingredient-focused, emphasizing sustainability and the pure, unfussy beauty of fresh produce.
instructions: Cut corn kernels from cobs. Reserve cobs for stock. In a saucepan, combine 250 ml water, 125 ml apple cider vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, and 1 tsp salt. Bring to a boil. Add corn kernels. Simmer 1 minute. Remove from heat. Let cool completely in liquid.
Thinly slice red onion. In a small bowl, combine 125 ml water, 60 ml apple cider vinegar, 0.5 tbsp sugar, and 0.5 tsp salt. Stir until dissolved. Add sliced onion. Let sit at least 20 minutes.

In a large bowl, combine drained quick-pickled corn, drained quick-pickled red onion, rinsed black beans, small diced red bell pepper, small diced green bell pepper, and small diced avocado. Add chopped cilantro.
In a small jar, combine olive oil, lime juice, 30 ml quick-pickling liquid, 0.5 tsp salt, and 0.25 tsp black pepper. Shake well to emulsify.
Pour dressing over salad. Toss gently to combine. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Corn and Black Bean Fermented Salad
recipes.visual_description: The 'Corn and Black Bean Fermented Salad' is presented on an unglazed, light-colored ceramic plate, showcasing a clean, minimalist aesthetic. Golden fermented corn kernels are artfully scattered among dark, plump black beans. Vibrant red cubes of bell pepper and halved cherry tomatoes add bright pops of color. Creamy, pale green diced avocado provides a soft contrast. Thinly sliced, translucent pink pickled red onion pieces are strategically placed, along with finely chopped fresh green cilantro. All components are distinct yet harmoniously arranged, with a light drizzle of lime-cilantro dressing glistening over the ingredients. The plate sits on a reclaimed wood table, complemented by an undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the dish, highlighting its natural textures and colors. The background is kept clean and minimalist, with a subtle hint of green foliage from a blurred potted plant, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.
instructions: Prepare pickled red onion: Combine thinly sliced red onion, white vinegar, water, sugar, and 3 g salt in a small jar. Stir to dissolve sugar. Let sit for at least 30 minutes, or refrigerate for longer preservation.
Drain and rinse cooked black beans.
In a large mixing bowl, combine fermented corn kernels, drained black beans, diced red bell pepper, halved cherry tomatoes, and diced avocado.
Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together lime juice, extra virgin olive oil, and chopped cilantro. Season with black pepper.
Drain pickled red onion, reserving a few slices for garnish.
Add drained pickled red onion to the salad bowl.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine all ingredients evenly.
Divide salad among four plates. Garnish with reserved pickled red onion slices and additional fresh cilantro if desired. Serve immediately.
notes: For fermented corn kernels, you can use store-bought lacto-fermented corn, or ferment your own corn at home with salt and water for 5-7 days.
This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by using pickled red onion for preservation and utilizing all parts of fresh herbs.

recipes.recipe_name: Spicy Tom Yum Chicken and Corn Sauté
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of Spicy Tom Yum Chicken and Corn Sauté rests in a rustic, earth-toned ceramic bowl. Seared chicken chunks, about 3cm each, are interspersed with vibrant yellow corn kernels and glossy, red-orange sauce. The chicken pieces show a slight golden-brown crust from searing. Green onion slices, both the tender white and vibrant green parts, are scattered throughout, adding fresh color and texture. The dish has a natural, slightly loose arrangement, typical of home cooking, with components touching and overlapping. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, with a simple, off-white cloth napkin casually placed beside it. Warm, cozy kitchen lighting illuminates the scene, creating an inviting, lived-in atmosphere. A small, white ceramic bowl of fluffy steamed jasmine rice and a pair of simple chopsticks are placed beside the main dish, completing the homely setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately with steamed jasmine rice.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3cm chunks. Set aside.
Mince garlic cloves. Finely chop chipotle chiles. Slice green onions diagonally into 2.5cm pieces, separating white and green parts.
Heat vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Cook, stirring occasionally, until browned on all sides and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Add minced garlic and chopped chipotle to the skillet. Sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in tom yum paste, corn kernels, and water or chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet. Stir to coat.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, and granulated sugar. Stir well to combine all flavors.
Stir in the white parts of the green onions. Cook for 1 minute.
Remove from heat. Stir in the green parts of the green onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust the amount of chipotle chile to your preferred spice level.
This dish balances spicy, sour, sweet, and savory flavors, characteristic of Thai cuisine.

recipes.recipe_name: Rosemary Lemon Roast Chicken and Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of golden-brown roasted chicken thigh rests centrally on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The skin is crisp, showing rich caramelization. Around the chicken, rustic potato wedges, roasted until tender with slightly crispy edges, are artfully scattered. Smashed garlic cloves, soft red onion wedges, and vibrant green sprigs of fresh rosemary and thyme are interspersed among the potatoes, adding color and texture. Thin, caramelized lemon slices are tucked alongside the chicken and potatoes. The arrangement is natural and flowing, with moderate negative space. The entire plate is visible, set on a simple wooden table with a folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and inviting textures, reflecting a casual yet refined Mediterranean dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread for dipping in the pan juices.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with a lemon vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Pat chicken thighs dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Wash potatoes. Cut smaller potatoes in half, larger ones into wedges. Place in a large roasting pan.
Add red onion wedges, smashed garlic cloves, rosemary, and thyme sprigs to the pan with potatoes.
Drizzle vegetables and herbs with 30 ml olive oil. Season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.
Arrange chicken thighs, skin-side up, among the potatoes and vegetables in the pan. Drizzle chicken with remaining 30 ml olive oil.
Tuck lemon slices around the chicken and potatoes.
Roast for 45-55 minutes, or until chicken skin is golden brown and crispy, and potatoes are tender. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Remove from oven. Let chicken rest in the pan for 5 minutes.
Serve hot.
notes: Adjust roasting time based on the size of your potatoes and chicken pieces.
For extra crispiness, you can broil the chicken for the last 5 minutes, watching carefully to prevent burning.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken and Mushroom Arancini
recipes.visual_description: The dish features three perfectly golden-brown arancini, each about 6 cm in diameter, arranged artfully on a clean, round white porcelain plate. The arancini have a crisp, textured exterior from the fried breadcrumbs, showing subtle hints of their golden hue. A slight scattering of finely chopped fresh parsley or a few small, vibrant basil leaves adorns the plate, adding a pop of green against the warm tones of the arancini. A modest dollop or a thin swirl of a bright red, smooth marinara sauce is placed elegantly beside the arancini, offering a contrasting color and a hint of accompanying flavor without overwhelming the dish. The plate sits on a simple, light-colored wooden table surface. A neatly folded white cotton napkin is placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the arancini's texture. The background is a gently blurred, casual restaurant setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with a simple marinara sauce on the side for dipping.
Traditionally enjoyed as a street food or appetizer in Sicily.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into small cubes, approximately 0.5 cm. Finely dice cremini mushrooms and onion. Mince garlic.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a large pan. Add diced chicken. Cook until browned. Season with salt and pepper. Remove chicken from pan.
Add remaining 15ml olive oil and butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute.
Add finely diced mushrooms to the pan. Cook until softened and their liquid evaporates.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes until rice grains are translucent.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed by the rice.
Add warm chicken stock, 150ml at a time. Stir continuously. Wait for each addition of liquid to be absorbed before adding more. Continue until rice is al dente, about 18-20 minutes.
Stir in the cooked chicken, grated Parmesan cheese, and chopped fresh parsley. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Spread the finished risotto evenly onto a baking sheet. Let it cool completely in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours, or until firm.

Take a spoonful of cooled risotto. Flatten it in your palm. Place a small cube of mozzarella cheese in the center. Enclose the mozzarella with risotto, forming a compact ball, about 5-6 cm in diameter. Repeat for all risotto.
Set up three shallow dishes: one with plain flour, one with beaten eggs, and one with Panko breadcrumbs.
Roll each arancini ball first in flour, then in beaten egg, then coat thoroughly with breadcrumbs, ensuring full coverage.
Heat vegetable oil in a deep pot to 175°C. Fry arancini in batches for 3-4 minutes per batch, until golden brown and crispy. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove arancini with a slotted spoon. Place on paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Cooling the risotto thoroughly is crucial for forming firm arancini balls.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Corn & Pickled Beet Sustainable Salad
recipes.visual_description: A vibrant, naturally composed salad rests on a handcrafted, matte ceramic plate in an earthy beige. The minimalistic arrangement allows each ingredient's distinct beauty to shine. Golden fermented corn kernels and bright fresh corn kernels are scattered with deep red diced pickled beets, crisp green cucumber cubes, and thin slices of pale pink radishes. Cooked chickpeas add a creamy texture. Fresh green parsley and mint leaves provide vibrant accents. The dressing lightly coats the components, adding a subtle sheen. The plate sits on a light, natural wood surface beside an undyed linen napkin. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene, emphasizing the pure colors and textures of the seasonal, plant-forward ingredients. A small plant in a simple pot is visible in the clean, minimalist background, reinforcing the sustainable theme. The presentation is unfussy, celebrating natural beauty.
instructions: Remove all kernels from corn cobs. Place cobs in a small saucepan. Add 500ml water. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 20 minutes. Strain broth and let cool. Reserve 100ml for dressing.
Dice fresh corn kernels, pickled beets, and cucumber into small cubes. Thinly slice radishes. Chop parsley and mint.
In a small bowl, whisk together cooled corn cob broth, apple cider vinegar, olive oil, Dijon mustard, salt, and pepper until emulsified.
In a large bowl, combine fermented corn kernels, fresh corn kernels, diced pickled beets, diced cucumber, sliced radishes, cooked chickpeas, chopped parsley, and chopped mint.
Pour dressing over the salad ingredients. Gently toss to combine. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, ferment corn kernels for 3-5 days at room temperature. For quick pickling beets, slice thinly and marinate in vinegar, sugar, and salt for at least 30 minutes.

recipes.recipe_name: Clear Cherry & Aged Cheese Consommé
recipes.visual_description: A clear, golden-hued consommé fills a simple, handcrafted ceramic bowl. At the bottom, a few deep red, plump fermented cherry halves are visible. Delicate, transparent shavings of aged cheese float on the surface, some melting slightly into the warm liquid. A scattering of bright green dill sprigs or finely chopped chives provides a pop of natural color and fresh aroma. The bowl rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface, emphasizing natural textures. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige hue sits beside it. Soft, natural light illuminates the scene from the side, highlighting the pure ingredients and clean lines. The presentation is minimalistic, showcasing the inherent beauty of each element with ample white space around the bowl.

ingredients.name: Vegetable scraps (carrot peels, onion skins, celery ends, mushroom stems, leek greens)
Aged hard cheese (e.g., Pecorino, vegetarian Parmesan), finely shaved
Fresh dill or chives, finely chopped

instructions: Prepare Fermented Cherries (at least 5-7 days in advance): Wash cherries. Pit them. Reserve pits for broth. Combine pitted cherries, 15g salt, and 250ml filtered water in a clean jar. Ensure cherries are submerged. Seal jar with an airlock lid or burp daily. Ferment at room temperature for 5-7 days, or until desired tanginess. Refrigerate when done.

Make Vegetable & Cherry Pit Broth: Combine vegetable scraps, cherry pits, cherry stems, bay leaf, peppercorns, and cheese rind (if using) in a large pot. Add 2 litres cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer. Cook for 45-60 minutes. Do not boil vigorously. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids. Season broth with salt to taste. Keep warm.
Assemble Soup: Ladle warm, clear broth into individual serving bowls. Add a few fermented cherries to each bowl. Garnish with finely shaved aged cheese. Sprinkle with fresh dill or chopped chives.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing cherry pits and stems, along with vegetable scraps, to create a flavorful broth. Lacto-fermentation extends the shelf life of cherries and adds complex savory notes, reducing food spoilage. Choose locally sourced, seasonal ingredients whenever possible to minimize environmental impact.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo Chipotle con Maíz y Cebolla Verde
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of hearty Chipotle Chicken with Corn and Green Onion is presented in a deep, rustic terracotta bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. Tender, braised chicken thigh pieces, rich and dark with chipotle sauce, are nestled amongst vibrant yellow corn kernels. The chicken is cooked until fall-apart tender, maintaining its whole shape. Bright green slices of fresh green onion and chopped cilantro are generously scattered over the top, adding a fresh contrast. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to the ingredients. A stack of warm, soft corn tortillas sits beside the bowl, with a small bowl of salsa roja and a simple fork nearby. Warm, inviting kitchen light illuminates the scene, highlighting the dish's comforting appeal and natural textures.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas for scooping the sauce and chicken.
Accompany with a side of Mexican red rice or white rice.
Offer a side of crema or crumbled cotija cheese.
Serve with pickled red onions or sliced jalapeños for added tang.
instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken thighs. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken. Set aside.
Add diced white onion to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and minced chipotle chiles. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tom yum paste. Cook 30 seconds.
Return chicken to pot. Add chicken broth and adobo sauce. Bring to a simmer.
Reduce heat to low. Cover pot. Simmer 30 minutes.
Add corn kernels. Continue simmering, uncovered, 10-15 minutes. Cook until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Stir in sliced green onion, fresh lime juice, and chopped cilantro. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.
notes: The tom yum paste adds a subtle, complex layer of acidity and spice, complementing the smoky chipotle without overpowering the Mexican profile.
Adjust chipotle quantity for desired spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy chicken and mushroom pasta rests in a round, off-white ceramic bowl on a well-used wooden dining table. The golden-brown, 2 cm seared chicken cubes are nestled amongst the al dente pasta strands, which are thoroughly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Sliced, earthy brown mushrooms are interspersed throughout, adding depth. A scattering of fresh, vibrant green chopped parsley provides a pop of color on top. The dish is presented casually, as if just served from the stove, with the pasta naturally piled. The lighting is warm and natural, suggesting a cozy family kitchen setting. A simple fork rests beside the bowl on a plain cloth napkin, emphasizing the homely, unpretentious comfort of the meal.
instructions: Boil a large pot of salted water. Add pasta. Cook according to package directions until al dente. Drain pasta. Reserve 120ml pasta water.
Pat chicken breast cut into 2 cm cubes dry. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from pan. Set aside.

Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the same pan. Add diced onion. Sauté until softened, about 3-4 minutes. Add sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are browned and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Stir in heavy cream and grated Parmesan cheese. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes.
Add cooked chicken back to the pan with the sauce. Add drained pasta. Toss to coat everything evenly. If sauce is too thick, add reserved pasta water, a little at a time, until desired consistency.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley and extra grated Parmesan.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Kohlrabi Steaks with Herbed Lentils
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of roasted kohlrabi steaks with herbed lentils is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Two to three golden-brown, thick-cut kohlrabi rounds, roasted until tender with slightly caramelized edges, are arranged neatly over a bed of earthy green Puy lentils. The lentils are plump and distinct, not mushy. A vibrant, verdant herb puree, glossy from olive oil, is artfully drizzled over the kohlrabi and around the plate, creating striking color contrast. The dish features a balanced composition with moderate negative space. The textures are varied: tender kohlrabi, firm lentils, and smooth puree. The setting is a modern bistro with a simple wooden table, a folded cotton napkin beside the plate, and soft, natural overhead lighting, creating an inviting, casual restaurant ambiance.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Peel kohlrabi. Slice each bulb into 1.5 cm thick rounds.
Toss kohlrabi slices with 2 tablespoons olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast kohlrabi for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway, until tender and lightly caramelized.
Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat.
Sauté shallots until translucent, about 3 minutes. Add garlic and cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add lentils and vegetable broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low.
Simmer, covered, for 20-25 minutes, or until lentils are tender but still hold their shape. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a small pot of water to a boil. Prepare an ice bath. Blanch parsley and mint in boiling water for 30 seconds.
Immediately transfer to ice bath to cool. Drain well. Squeeze out excess water.
Combine blanched herbs, chives, 4 tablespoons olive oil, juice of half a lemon, and a pinch of salt in a blender. Blend until very smooth. Adjust seasoning as needed.
Spoon a generous portion of warm lentils onto each plate. Arrange 2-3 roasted kohlrabi steaks over the lentils.
Drizzle herb puree generously over the kohlrabi and around the plate. Serve immediately.
notes: For best flavor, select firm, fresh kohlrabi. Smaller bulbs are often more tender.

recipes.recipe_name: Caramelized Kohlrabi and Onion Tart with Goat Cheese
recipes.visual_description: A golden-brown, rustic tart occupies the center of a clean white porcelain dinner plate. The puff pastry crust is visibly flaky and puffed, its edges brushed to a rich, glossy sheen. Within the raised border, a generous layer of deep amber caramelized onions forms the base, their soft texture hinted at. Neatly arranged atop the onions are thin, translucent rounds of blanched kohlrabi, their pale green edges offering a subtle color contrast. Scattered over the kohlrabi are creamy white crumbles of goat cheese, some slightly melted and browned at the edges, alongside vibrant green flecks of fresh thyme. The tart is presented as a single, generous wedge, showcasing the layers. The plate sits on a simple wooden table. A folded cotton napkin and standard flatware rest beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the tart's textures and warm colors.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve warm, perhaps with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C. Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add sliced onions. Cook slowly for 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply caramelized.
Add sugar and balsamic vinegar to onions. Cook 5 more minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Blanch kohlrabi slices: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil. Add kohlrabi slices. Cook 2-3 minutes until slightly tender-crisp. Drain immediately and plunge into ice water. Drain well and pat dry.
Unroll puff pastry onto the prepared baking sheet. Score a 2 cm border around the pastry edge, do not cut through.
Spread caramelized onions evenly within the scored border.
Arrange blanched kohlrabi slices neatly over the onions.
Crumble goat cheese over the kohlrabi and onions. Sprinkle with fresh thyme.
In a small bowl, whisk egg yolk with water. Brush the scored pastry border with egg wash.
Bake 25-30 minutes, or until pastry is golden brown and puffed.
Let tart cool slightly before slicing and serving.
notes: Kohlrabi can be slightly bitter; blanching mellows its flavor and ensures even cooking.
Caramelizing onions slowly is key for deep flavor.

recipes.recipe_name: Slow-Cooked Pork Ragu with Pappardelle and Tomato Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A pristine white, shallow porcelain dinner plate forms the canvas. On one side, a generous mound of vibrant red tomato risotto is carefully shaped, its creamy texture visible. Adjacent to the risotto, a nest of broad, golden-hued pappardelle is artfully arranged. The rich, dark red pork ragu, with its tender, shredded pork chunks, is draped generously over the pappardelle, allowing some noodles to peek through. The ragu features small, tender diced onions and hints of garlic, creating a rustic yet refined appearance. The dish presents a striking contrast of deep reds from the ragu and risotto against the lighter golden pappardelle. The pork chunks are a warm brown, showing their slow-cooked tenderness. Textures range from the soft, yielding risotto and tender pasta to the succulent, shredded pork. A few fresh, vibrant green basil leaves are artfully scattered over the risotto and ragu, providing a pop of color and freshness. A light dusting of finely grated Parmesan cheese graces both components. Pork is cut into 3-4 cm cubes before cooking and then shredded into irregular, tender chunks. Onions for both ragu and risotto are finely diced. Garlic is minced. The plate rests on a simple, textured wooden table surface. A neatly folded, crisp white cotton napkin is placed to the left of the plate. Standard polished silver flatware (fork and knife) is positioned to the right and left, respectively. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro ambiance with warm, natural, even lighting casting subtle shadows that define the dish's contours. The scene is uncluttered, allowing the food to be the undisputed focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to sop up extra sauce.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Pair with a robust red wine like Chianti or Sangiovese.
instructions: Pat pork cubes dry. Season pork with salt and pepper.
Heat 30 ml olive oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat.
Sear pork in batches until browned on all sides. Remove pork from pot.
Add large diced onion to the pot. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add 4 minced garlic cloves. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste. Cook 2 minutes, stirring.
Deglaze with red wine. Scrape up browned bits. Reduce wine by half.
Return pork to the pot. Add crushed tomatoes, 500 ml broth, rosemary, and bay leaf.
Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 2.5-3 hours, until pork is fork-tender.
Remove rosemary and bay leaf. Shred pork with two forks directly in the sauce. Adjust seasoning.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a separate pot over medium heat.
Add small diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add 2 minced garlic cloves. Cook 1 minute.
Add Arborio rice. Toast 2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Pour in tomato puree. Stir until absorbed.
Begin adding warm broth, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously.
Wait until liquid is almost absorbed before adding the next ladle.
Continue adding broth and stirring for 18-20 minutes, until rice is creamy and al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in butter and grated Parmesan. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a rolling boil.
Add pappardelle. Cook according to package directions until al dente.
Drain pasta, reserving some pasta water.
Add drained pappardelle to the ragu. Toss to coat. Add a splash of pasta water if needed for consistency.

recipes.recipe_name: Pollo e Funghi Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of creamy Pollo e Funghi Risotto is presented in a clean, shallow white porcelain bowl. The risotto is fluid and free-flowing, not stiff or mounded, showcasing its characteristic creaminess. Scattered throughout are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks, approximately 2 cm cubes, and tender, earthy sliced cremini mushrooms. Finely diced onion pieces are integrated into the rice. The color palette is warm, with the pale golden risotto contrasting with the rich brown chicken and mushrooms. A vibrant sprinkle of roughly chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley provides a pop of green on top. The bowl sits on a simple light wooden table surface, with a folded white cotton napkin beside it. Natural, soft, even lighting illuminates the dish, creating subtle shadows and highlighting the texture. A small, simple fork rests on the napkin, and a traditional small Parmigiano-Reggiano grater is subtly placed in the background, maintaining an authentic Italian bistro feel without clutter.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately after preparation, as risotto is best enjoyed hot and creamy.
Offer additional grated Parmigiano-Reggiano at the table for guests to add to their liking.
instructions: Heat chicken stock in a saucepan. Keep it at a gentle simmer.
Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.
Slice mushrooms. Dice onion finely. Mince garlic.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Cook to internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil and 15 g butter to the pot. Add diced onion. Sauté until translucent, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook until mushrooms are softened and liquid has evaporated, about 7-8 minutes.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir constantly for 2 minutes until edges of grains become translucent (toasting).
Pour in white wine. Stir until completely absorbed.
Add one ladleful of hot chicken stock to the rice. Stir continuously until liquid is almost absorbed.
Continue adding stock one ladleful at a time, stirring constantly. Wait for each addition to be nearly absorbed before adding the next. This process takes about 20-25 minutes.
The risotto should be creamy and the rice al dente.
Remove from heat. Stir in remaining 45 g butter and grated Parmigiano-Reggiano (mantecare).
Fold in seared chicken cubes and most of the chopped fresh parsley.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Beer-Braised Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Beer-Braised Chicken with Roasted Potatoes and Tomatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, seared bone-in, skin-on chicken thigh rests as the centerpiece. Around the chicken, rustic, golden-brown roasted potato chunks are scattered alongside vibrant, burst cherry tomatoes. A rich, amber-hued sauce, reduced from the braising liquid, is generously spooned over the chicken and vegetables, pooling slightly on the plate. The dish is topped with a generous sprinkle of finely grated Parmesan cheese, adding a pale, textured contrast, and a scattering of fresh, bright green chopped parsley for a pop of color and freshness. The arrangement is natural and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate is set on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded white cotton napkin and standard silver flatware are placed beside the plate. The scene is illuminated by natural, even lighting, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere typical of a modern bistro.
instructions: Preheat oven to 180°C. Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Lightly dredge chicken in flour, shaking off excess.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe Dutch oven or heavy-bottomed pot over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down for 5-7 minutes until deeply golden brown and crispy. Flip and sear for 2-3 minutes on the other side. Remove chicken from pot and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add sliced onions to the pot. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and translucent. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in beer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 2 minutes.
Add chicken stock, thyme sprigs, and rosemary sprig to the pot. Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in liquid.
Cut potatoes into 3-4 cm rustic chunks or wedges. Halve cherry tomatoes. Arrange potatoes and cherry tomatoes around the chicken in the pot.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer on the stovetop. Cover the pot tightly with a lid.
Transfer the Dutch oven to the preheated oven. Braise for 45-60 minutes, or until chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F) and is fork-tender. Potatoes should also be tender.

Remove pot from oven. Remove chicken and vegetables to a platter. Discard herb sprigs. Place pot back on stovetop over medium-high heat. Reduce braising liquid by simmering for 5-10 minutes until slightly thickened to a sauce consistency.
Adjust seasoning of the sauce with salt and pepper. Ladle sauce over chicken and vegetables. Garnish with grated Parmesan cheese and fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous portion of creamy Chicken and Broccoli Risotto is presented in a clean, white porcelain bowl. The risotto, a pale, creamy yellow, flows naturally within the bowl. Diced, golden-seared chicken pieces (2 cm cubes) are visibly integrated, alongside vibrant green, tender-crisp broccoli florets and flecks of deep amber caramelized onion. A small, elegant swirl of bright white lemon-herb mayonnaise rests on top, providing a contrasting color and texture. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of finely chopped fresh parsley and a dusting of grated Parmesan. The setting is a modern bistro, with the bowl placed on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a fork and a crisp cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting. The background is subtly blurred, maintaining focus on the dish while suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Dice chicken breast into 2 cm cubes. Season with salt and pepper.

Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken cubes until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pot; set aside.
Finely dice the onion. Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the pot. Add diced onion and cook over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes until deeply caramelized and soft. Stir occasionally.
Mince garlic. Add minced garlic to the pot with onions. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pot. Stir for 2 minutes to toast rice kernels.
Pour in white wine. Stir until wine is fully absorbed.
Heat chicken broth in a separate saucepan; keep it simmering.
Begin adding hot broth to the rice, one ladleful at a time. Stir continuously. Wait until each ladleful is almost fully absorbed before adding the next. This process takes 20-25 minutes.
While risotto cooks, steam or blanch broccoli florets until tender-crisp. Drain well.
When risotto is creamy and rice is al dente, stir in cooked chicken and broccoli florets.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in butter and half of the Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes until creamy and fluid. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Finely chop fresh parsley. Grate lemon zest. In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise with half of the chopped parsley and lemon zest. Mix well.
Serve risotto immediately in shallow bowls. Garnish each serving with a small dollop or swirl of lemon-herb mayonnaise, remaining Parmesan cheese, and a sprinkle of fresh parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Orecchiette with Soppressata, Artichoke and Bel Paese
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, showcasing a generous individual portion of Orecchiette pasta. The pasta is coated in a rich, creamy sauce, with vibrant elements thoughtfully integrated. Diced soppressata, approximately 1 cm cubes, are scattered throughout, offering pops of deep red and a savory texture. Tender artichoke hearts, quartered, add soft green hues, complementing the intense red, thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes. Melted, golden Bel Paese cheese creates a luxurious, glossy finish, subtly binding the ingredients. A sprinkle of golden, coarse breadcrumbs provides a contrasting crunch. Fresh, finely chopped parsley garnishes the top, adding a bright green accent. The overall composition is organic and inviting, with moderate negative space. The plate rests on a simple wooden surface, accompanied by a silver fork and a crisp white linen napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine like Pinot Grigio or Sauvignon Blanc.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook orecchiette according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta water. Drain pasta.

While pasta cooks, prepare breadcrumbs. Pulse stale bread in a food processor until coarse crumbs form. Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a small pan over medium heat. Add breadcrumbs and toast until golden and crisp. Set aside.
Dice soppressata into 1 cm cubes. Drain artichoke hearts and quarter them. Drain sun-dried tomatoes and thinly slice.

Heat remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet or pan over medium heat. Add diced soppressata. Cook until slightly crispy and fat is rendered, about 3-4 minutes. Remove soppressata with a slotted spoon and set aside, leaving rendered fat in the pan.
Add minced garlic and finely diced shallot to the pan. Sauté until fragrant and softened, about 2 minutes.
Pour in dry white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce wine by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in heavy cream, quartered artichoke hearts, and sliced sun-dried tomatoes. Bring to a gentle simmer.

Add cooked orecchiette to the skillet with the sauce. Add grated or diced Bel Paese cheese. Toss well to combine, allowing cheese to melt and create a creamy sauce. Add reserved pasta water gradually, 50 ml at a time, until desired sauce consistency is reached. The sauce should be fluid and coat the pasta well.
Stir in cooked soppressata and red pepper flakes, if using. Season with salt and black pepper to taste.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with toasted breadcrumbs and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Always reserve pasta water before draining; it is crucial for adjusting sauce consistency.
Adjust red pepper flakes to your preferred level of spice.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Chicken and Spinach Rigatoni
recipes.visual_description: The dish is presented in a classic white porcelain pasta bowl, showcasing a single generous serving. Al dente rigatoni pasta is evenly coated in a rich, pale cream sauce. Tender, golden-brown chicken breast chunks, approximately 2-3 cm in size, are interspersed throughout the pasta, offering a pleasing contrast. Vibrant dark green wilted spinach leaves are visible, adding a fresh pop of color, alongside ruby-red, roughly chopped sun-dried tomato pieces. The dish is lightly garnished with fresh green parsley leaves and a delicate dusting of grated Parmigiano Reggiano. The overall presentation is clean and inviting, with moderate negative space. The bowl rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by a silver fork and spoon, and a neatly folded cotton napkin beside it. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors, creating an approachable bistro atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up the sauce.
Accompany with a simple green salad dressed with vinaigrette.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2-3 cm chunks. Season chicken generously with salt and pepper.
Heat 15 ml olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken chunks.
Sear chicken 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Cook until internal temperature reaches 75°C. Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Roughly chop sun-dried tomatoes.
Add remaining 15 ml olive oil to the same skillet. Add diced onion. Sauté 3-4 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and chopped sun-dried tomatoes. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in white wine. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet. Reduce wine by half, about 2-3 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth and heavy cream. Bring sauce to a gentle simmer.
Meanwhile, cook rigatoni pasta according to package directions until al dente. Reserve 120 ml pasta cooking water before draining.
Add fresh spinach to the simmering sauce. Stir until spinach wilts, about 1-2 minutes.
Return cooked chicken to the skillet with the sauce. Add drained rigatoni pasta. Toss to combine.
Add half of the grated Parmigiano Reggiano. Add reserved pasta water as needed to achieve desired sauce consistency. Toss well.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. Garnish each portion with remaining Parmigiano Reggiano and fresh chopped parsley.
notes: Ensure pasta is cooked al dente for optimal texture.
Do not overcook the chicken to keep it tender and juicy.

recipes.recipe_name: Hungarian Beef Goulash (Marha Pörkölt)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Hungarian Beef Goulash (Marha Pörkölt) is presented in a clean, white porcelain deep bowl on a simple wooden table. The rich, deep red-brown stew fills the bowl, showcasing tender, dark beef chunks (approximately 4cm cubes) and softened, vibrant red bell pepper pieces (approximately 2cm dice), interspersed with creamy diced potatoes. The sauce is thick and glossy, clinging to the ingredients, with a subtle sheen from the rendered beef fat and paprika. A small mound of freshly chopped green parsley is sprinkled on top, providing a fresh color contrast. A small dollop of creamy white sour cream (tejföl) is placed delicately on the side of the goulash. Beside the bowl, a small stack of soft, traditional Hungarian nokedli (egg noodles or dumplings) is neatly arranged, ready to accompany the stew. A simple white cotton napkin is folded beside the plate. The scene is bathed in natural, even lighting, creating a warm and inviting atmosphere, with a blurred, casual restaurant background that keeps the focus on the dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with nokedli (Hungarian egg dumplings)
Serve with crusty bread for dipping
Offer a side of pickled vegetables (e.g., pickled cucumbers, cabbage)
Garnish with a dollop of sour cream (tejföl)
instructions: Pat beef cubes dry with paper towels. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat vegetable oil in a large heavy-bottomed pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear beef in batches until browned on all sides. Remove beef and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until softened and translucent, about 8-10 minutes. Do not brown.
Remove pot from heat. Stir in sweet paprika, caraway seeds, dried oregano, and minced garlic. Stir for 1 minute until fragrant. This 'blooms' the spices.
Return pot to medium heat. Add diced bell peppers and crushed tomatoes. Stir well. Cook for 5 minutes, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom.
Return seared beef to the pot. Pour in beef stock. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 1.5 hours, stirring occasionally.

Add diced potatoes to the pot. Stir well. Continue to simmer, covered, for another 45-60 minutes, or until beef is fork-tender and potatoes are cooked through. Ensure beef reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F).
Uncover the pot for the last 15 minutes of cooking if the sauce is too thin. Adjust seasoning with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh chopped parsley and a dollop of sour cream if desired.
traditional_techniques: Paprika blooming (sautéing paprika in fat to enhance flavor and color)

recipes.recipe_name: Crema Catalana Espuma, Roasted Plum, Cinnamon Marshmallow
recipes.visual_description: A refined dessert presented on a pristine, matte white bone china plate. An ethereal, airy mound of light beige Crema Catalana espuma, dispensed organically, occupies one side of the plate, its delicate texture visible. Adjacent, a rich, deep ruby-red roasted plum compote is artfully spooned, its rustic texture contrasting with the smooth espuma. Small, pearl-like dots of torched cinnamon marshmallow are strategically placed, their golden-brown tips hinting at a delicate crunch. A single, vibrant green mint leaf is precisely positioned for a fresh color accent. The composition is minimalist, with abundant negative space. The plate rests on a cool, grey-veined Carrara marble surface. Soft, directional lighting creates subtle shadows, emphasizing textures and forms. The scene is clean, highlighting a luxurious, sophisticated Spanish dining experience.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a small glass of chilled Moscatel de Valencia.
Offer a strong espresso or café con leche alongside.

ingredients.name: Fresh plums (pitted, cut into small wedges)

instructions: Soak gelatin sheets for Crema Catalana in cold water.
Heat milk with lemon peel, orange peel, and cinnamon stick until simmering. Remove from heat. Steep 15 minutes. Strain milk; discard solids.
Whisk egg yolks, 100g sugar, and cornstarch in a bowl until pale. Gradually whisk in warm strained milk.
Return mixture to saucepan. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until thickened to a custard. Do not boil.
Remove from heat. Stir in squeezed gelatin until dissolved. Strain custard into a bowl. Cover surface with plastic wrap. Chill completely, at least 4 hours.
Once chilled, whisk custard until smooth. Transfer to a siphon bottle. Charge with 1 N2O cartridge. Shake well. Keep chilled.
Preheat oven to 180°C.
Toss plum wedges with 30g sugar, 15ml lemon juice, 30ml water, and a pinch of cinnamon powder. Spread on a baking sheet.
Roast plums 20-25 minutes, until tender and slightly caramelized. Cool. Mash lightly with a fork for a rustic compote, or blend for a smooth gel.
Soak gelatin sheets for marshmallow in cold water.
In a small saucepan, combine 150g sugar and 50ml water. Heat over medium-high heat until syrup reaches 118°C.
While syrup cooks, whip egg whites to soft peaks.
With mixer running, slowly pour hot syrup into egg whites in a thin stream. Continue whipping until meringue is stiff and glossy.
Gently fold in squeezed gelatin and 2g cinnamon powder. Transfer marshmallow mixture to a piping bag.
Dispense Crema Catalana Espuma onto each dessert plate, creating an organic mound.
Spoon roasted plum compote artistically next to the espuma.
Pipe small, delicate dots or swirls of cinnamon marshmallow onto the plate. Gently torch the marshmallow for a toasted effect, if desired.
Garnish with a small mint leaf and a tiny piece of edible gold leaf. Serve immediately.
notes: For best espuma texture, ensure custard is thoroughly chilled before siphoning.
Adjust sweetness of plum compote based on plum ripeness.

recipes.recipe_name: Summer Rose Fruit Salad
recipes.visual_description: A modest, individual serving of Summer Rose Fruit Salad is presented in a well-loved, everyday ceramic bowl, resting on a sturdy, well-used wooden kitchen table. The bowl is generously filled with a vibrant medley of fresh, seasonal fruits: plump strawberry halves, soft peach slices, creamy banana rounds, and juicy pineapple chunks. The fruit is naturally arranged, with some pieces overlapping, showcasing their varied textures and bright, natural colors. A light, glistening rose-infused syrup coats the fruit, adding a subtle sheen and enhancing its fresh appearance. The scene is illuminated by warm, natural light, characteristic of a cozy, lived-in kitchen. The background is minimal and unobtrusive, emphasizing the homely comfort and unpretentious beauty of the dish, ready for a casual family meal.
instructions: Wash strawberries. Hull and cut into halves or quarters, depending on size.
Wash peaches. Peel, pit, and slice into bite-sized pieces.
Peel bananas. Slice into 1 cm thick rounds.
Peel and core pineapple. Cut into 2 cm chunks.
In a small saucepan, combine sugar and water. Heat over medium heat. Stir until sugar dissolves completely.
Remove from heat. Stir in rose water. Let the syrup cool completely.
In a large mixing bowl, combine strawberries, peaches, banana rounds, and pineapple chunks.
Drizzle lemon juice over the fruit. Gently toss to coat.
Pour the cooled rose syrup over the fruit. Gently toss again to ensure all fruit is coated.
Cover the bowl. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Hearty Peanut Tofu Udon Stir-Fry
recipes.visual_description: A generous single portion of Peanut Tofu Udon Stir-Fry fills a deep, rustic ceramic bowl. Thick, chewy udon noodles are lightly coated in a rich, glossy peanut-ginger sauce, forming a soft mound. Cubes of pan-fried firm tofu, golden-brown and slightly crisp on the edges, are nestled throughout the noodles. Vibrant green broccoli florets and thinly sliced red bell pepper are evenly distributed, adding color and tender-crisp texture. The dish is generously garnished with a sprinkle of coarsely chopped roasted peanuts, adding a satisfying crunch, and thinly sliced bright green spring onions for freshness. The bowl sits on a warm, well-used wooden dining table, alongside a pair of simple wooden chopsticks. Natural, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the comforting meal, creating an inviting, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks in a deep ceramic bowl
Offer a side of chili garlic sauce for extra heat
Serve with a small dish of pickled ginger
instructions: Press tofu block for 15 minutes to remove excess water. Cut pressed tofu into 2cm cubes.
Cook udon noodles according to package directions. Drain and rinse with cold water to prevent sticking. Set aside.
For the sauce, combine soy sauce, peanut butter, rice vinegar, sesame oil, maple syrup, and water/broth in a bowl. Whisk until smooth.
Peel and finely mince ginger and garlic.
Cut red bell pepper into thin slices. Cut broccoli florets into bite-sized pieces.

Heat vegetable oil in a large wok or pan over medium-high heat. Add tofu cubes. Cook, turning occasionally, until golden brown and crispy on all sides, about 8-10 minutes. Remove tofu from pan and set aside.
Add minced ginger and garlic to the same pan. Stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add bell pepper slices and broccoli florets to the pan. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until tender-crisp.
Return cooked tofu to the pan. Add the prepared peanut sauce. Stir well to coat all ingredients.
Add cooked udon noodles to the pan. Toss gently to combine and heat through, ensuring noodles are fully coated in sauce.
Coarsely chop roasted peanuts. Thinly slice green onions.
Serve immediately, garnished with chopped peanuts and sliced green onions.
notes: Adjust peanut butter and maple syrup to taste for desired sweetness and creaminess.
For a spicier kick, add a pinch of red chili flakes to the sauce.

recipes.recipe_name: Chicken Marsala
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared chicken breast is centrally placed on a round white porcelain plate. The chicken, a golden-brown whole piece, is partially covered with a rich, glossy Marsala mushroom sauce. Thinly sliced, tender cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots are visible within the deep brown sauce. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley garnishes the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The dish exhibits a clean, organized, yet organic plating style with moderate negative space. The setting is a modern bistro, featuring a simple wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the plate. Standard polished flatware (fork and knife) are arranged next to the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a warm, inviting atmosphere with a softly blurred restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve alongside creamy polenta or a simple pasta like fettuccine or linguine.
Offer a side of steamed green beans or asparagus.
Crusty Italian bread is ideal for soaking up the Marsala sauce.
instructions: Place each chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap. Pound to an even 1.5 cm thickness. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Dredge each chicken breast lightly in flour, shaking off excess.
Slice mushrooms thinly. Finely dice shallots. Mince garlic.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add chicken. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side until golden brown. Internal temperature should reach 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from skillet and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the skillet. Add sliced mushrooms and diced shallots. Sauté for 5-7 minutes until softened and browned. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour Marsala wine into the skillet. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan. Reduce liquid by half, about 3-5 minutes.
Stir in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Cook for 5 minutes until sauce slightly thickens. Stir in heavy cream, if using.
Return chicken breasts to the skillet. Simmer in the sauce for 2-3 minutes, ensuring chicken is fully heated through. Chop fresh parsley.
Remove skillet from heat. Stir in half of the chopped parsley. Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately, garnished with remaining fresh parsley.
notes: Pounding the chicken ensures even cooking and tenderness.
Ensure Marsala wine is dry, not sweet, for a savory dish.

recipes.recipe_name: Grilled Octopus with Lemon-Parsley Dressing and Roasted Potatoes
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of grilled octopus and roasted potatoes is presented on a clean, round white porcelain plate, centrally positioned on a rustic wooden table. The octopus, cut into thick, irregular chunks, displays a beautiful char on its exterior, ranging from deep purple to rich brown, contrasting with its tender, opaque interior. The roasted small potatoes, halved or quartered, are golden-brown with slightly crisped skins and a fluffy texture, arranged organically beside the octopus. A generous drizzle of vibrant green lemon-parsley dressing coats the octopus and potatoes, adding a fresh, glossy sheen and flecks of finely chopped parsley. A fresh lemon wedge sits on the plate's edge. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple cotton napkin folded beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's textures and colors. The background is subtly blurred, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere, allowing the food to be the undisputed focal point.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty artisanal bread to soak up the dressing.
Pair with a crisp, dry white wine.
Offer a simple green salad as a light accompaniment.
instructions: Clean octopus thoroughly. Remove beak and eyes. Place whole octopus in a large pot.

Add 3 minced garlic cloves, 2 bay leaves, and white wine to the pot with the octopus. Add enough water to cover the octopus by 2-3 cm. Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Simmer gently for 60-90 minutes, or until octopus is very tender when pierced with a fork. Drain and let cool slightly. Reserve 50 ml of cooking liquid.

Preheat oven to 200°C (390°F). Wash and halve small potatoes. Toss potatoes with 50 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet. Roast for 30-40 minutes, or until golden brown and tender. Turn halfway through.
While potatoes roast, prepare the lemon-parsley dressing. Finely chop remaining 3 garlic cloves. Finely chop the large bunch of parsley. Zest both lemons. Juice one and a half lemons (about 60 ml).

In a small bowl, combine chopped garlic, chopped parsley, lemon zest, and lemon juice. Whisk in 100 ml extra virgin olive oil. Add the reserved 50 ml octopus cooking liquid. Season with salt and pepper. Mix well.
Once octopus is cool enough to handle, cut tentacles into large, irregular chunks, about 5-7 cm long. Leave smaller pieces whole. Discard the head if desired.

Heat a grill pan or outdoor grill to medium-high heat. Lightly brush octopus chunks with a small amount of olive oil. Grill octopus for 2-4 minutes per side, until slightly charred and crispy. Do not overcook.
Arrange roasted potato halves on a white porcelain plate. Place grilled octopus chunks artfully over and around the potatoes. Drizzle generously with the lemon-parsley dressing. Serve immediately.
notes: For best results, use fresh octopus. If using frozen, thaw completely before cooking.
The octopus can be braised ahead of time and refrigerated until ready to grill.

recipes.recipe_name: Jasmine Advocaat Blueberry Cake
recipes.visual_description: A generous, thick slice of golden-brown jasmine tea infused loaf cake rests on a simple, off-white ceramic dessert plate. The cake has a slightly domed, cracked top and a tender, moist crumb. A thick, pale yellow advocaat glaze, subtly infused with blueberry schnapps, generously coats the top of the slice, with some drips gently pooling at the base. Scattered across the glaze are plump, deep blue fresh blueberries, some whole, some slightly burst, adding a pop of color and natural texture. The plate is placed on a well-used, light-colored wooden kitchen table, showing natural grain. In the background, the rest of the loaf cake sits on a plain wooden cutting board. A casually folded, simple linen tea towel and a small glass of milk complete the cozy, homely scene. Warm, soft kitchen lighting illuminates the dessert, emphasizing its comforting appearance.

ingredients.name: Jasmine tea, strongly brewed and cooled

instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Line a 20x10 cm loaf pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time. Mix well after each addition.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking powder, and salt.
Gradually add dry ingredients to wet ingredients. Mix until just combined.
Stir in cooled jasmine tea. Mix until smooth.
Pour batter into the prepared loaf pan. Smooth the top.
Bake for 45-55 minutes. A wooden skewer inserted into the center should come out clean.
Let cake cool in the pan for 10 minutes. Then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
For the glaze, whisk together powdered sugar, advocaat, and blueberry schnapps in a bowl until smooth.
Once cake is completely cool, pour the glaze over the top. Let it drip down the sides.
Arrange fresh blueberries on top of the glaze. Let glaze set for 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.recipe_name: Mediterranean Seared Octopus
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of pan-seared octopus is elegantly presented on a round, clean white porcelain dinner plate. The octopus, cooked until tender then seared, displays a beautiful golden-brown char on its exterior, contrasting with its pale, tender interior visible where tentacles are cut into thick chunks or left as whole, curled pieces. A light, glossy drizzle of lemon-garlic-parsley vinaigrette pools subtly around the octopus, reflecting the natural light. Fresh, vibrant green parsley leaves are scattered sparingly over and around the octopus, providing a burst of color and freshness. A bright yellow lemon wedge sits beside the main elements, ready to be squeezed. The plate rests on a simple, light-toned wooden table surface. A neatly folded cream-colored cotton napkin and classic silver flatware are positioned beside the plate. The background is softly blurred, hinting at a modern bistro atmosphere with natural, even lighting that highlights the dish's textures and colors.
instructions: Clean octopus thoroughly. Remove beak and eyes if present. Rinse well.
Place octopus in a large pot. Add 4 whole garlic cloves, bay leaves, quartered onion or shallot, white wine, and enough water to just cover the octopus.
Bring liquid to a gentle simmer over medium heat. Reduce heat to low. Cover the pot.
Simmer octopus for 45-60 minutes, or until very tender when pierced with a fork. Cooking time varies by size.
Remove pot from heat. Let octopus cool completely in its cooking liquid. This ensures tenderness.
Once cool, remove octopus from liquid. Discard aromatics and liquid. Pat octopus dry with paper towels.
Cut octopus into thick, irregular chunks or leave smaller tentacles whole.
Finely chop remaining 4 garlic cloves and a generous amount of fresh parsley.
Heat 50 ml olive oil in a large non-stick pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat.
Add octopus pieces to the hot pan. Sear for 3-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and slightly crispy.
Reduce heat to low. Add chopped garlic to the pan. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Remove pan from heat. Squeeze juice from 1 lemon over the octopus. Add remaining 50 ml olive oil and chopped parsley.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Toss gently to combine.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges.

recipes.recipe_name: Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Mexican Chicken and Rice Skillet is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features a natural mound of vibrant reddish-orange rice, cooked with diced tomatoes and spices. Visible amongst the fluffy rice are golden-brown, seared chicken chunks (3-4 cm). Bright yellow corn kernels are interspersed throughout, adding pops of color and texture. A generous sprinkle of fresh, chopped green cilantro garnishes the top. A bright green lime wedge rests beside the main dish. The plating is organized but not overly arranged, with moderate negative space. The setting is a simple wooden table surface, with a folded cotton napkin and standard flatware beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, creating a professional yet approachable restaurant-style atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with warm corn tortillas on the side for scooping.
Offer a small bowl of salsa verde or pico de gallo as an optional accompaniment.
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season with salt and pepper. Cut into 3-4 cm chunks.
Heat olive oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks to the hot skillet. Sear until golden brown on all sides. Do not overcrowd. Cook in batches if necessary. Remove chicken from skillet. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic, ground cumin, smoked paprika, and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in undrained diced tomatoes and rice. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring to coat the rice.
Return seared chicken to the skillet. Pour in chicken broth. Bring mixture to a simmer.

Reduce heat to low. Cover the skillet tightly. Cook for 20-25 minutes, or until rice is tender and most liquid is absorbed. Check chicken internal temperature with a thermometer; it must reach 75°C (167°F).
Stir in frozen corn kernels. Cook for 3-5 minutes more, uncovered, until corn is heated through and any remaining liquid is absorbed.
Remove skillet from heat. Let stand, covered, for 5 minutes. Fluff rice gently with a fork.
Serve hot. Garnish each portion with fresh chopped cilantro and a lime wedge.
notes: For best results, use a heavy-bottomed skillet to ensure even cooking.
