instructions: Dice chicken into 2 cm cubes.
Peel and dice potatoes into 1.5 cm cubes.
Peel and dice carrots into 1 cm cubes.
Finely chop onion. Mince garlic.
Heat olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add chopped onion and diced carrots. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add diced chicken to pot. Brown on all sides, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Stir in diced potatoes and chicken broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low. Simmer 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
In a small bowl, whisk mayonnaise with 125 ml hot broth from the pot until smooth.
Slowly stir mayonnaise mixture into the soup. Do not boil after adding mayonnaise.
Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste. Serve hot.

recipes.recipe_name: Banana Peanut Butter Celebration Cake
recipes.visual_description: A generous slice of Banana Peanut Butter Celebration Cake sits on a simple, everyday ceramic plate. The cake slice reveals two moist, golden-brown cake layers separated by a thick, creamy layer of pale tan peanut butter frosting. The cake crumb appears tender and speckled with mashed banana. The rich, creamy frosting is spread generously over the top and sides of the slice, showing natural swirls and peaks from the spatula. A few finely chopped peanuts are casually sprinkled on top of the frosting for added texture. In the background, the whole, fully frosted cake rests on a modest cake stand or directly on a well-used wooden dining table. The scene is illuminated by warm, soft lighting, typical of a family kitchen. A casually placed cloth napkin and a simple fork complete the homely, comforting presentation. The overall impression is one of a beloved homemade dessert, inviting and unpretentious.
instructions: Preheat oven to 175°C. Grease and flour two 15 cm round cake pans. Line bottoms with parchment paper.
In a medium bowl, mash ripe bananas with a fork until mostly smooth. Set aside.
In a separate bowl, whisk together flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside.
In a large bowl, cream softened butter and granulated sugar with an electric mixer until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Stir in vanilla extract.
Gradually add dry ingredients to the wet ingredients, alternating with milk. Begin and end with dry ingredients. Mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Fold in mashed bananas.
Divide batter evenly between prepared cake pans.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until a wooden skewer inserted into the center comes out clean.
Cool cakes in pans on a wire rack for 10 minutes. Invert cakes onto the wire rack to cool completely.
Prepare the Frosting: In a large bowl, beat softened butter and creamy peanut butter together until smooth.
Gradually add sifted icing sugar, mixing until well combined.
Add milk or cream, 15ml at a time, until frosting reaches desired creamy consistency. Beat in vanilla extract.
Assemble the Cake: Once cakes are completely cool, place one cake layer on a serving plate. Spread about one-third of the frosting evenly over the top.
Place the second cake layer on top. Spread remaining frosting over the top and sides of the cake.
For a simple decoration, use an offset spatula to create swirls or peaks in the frosting. Optionally, sprinkle with a few chopped peanuts.

recipes.recipe_name: West African Chicken Peanut Stew with Caramelized Banana
recipes.visual_description: The dish is a vibrant, hearty West African Chicken Peanut Stew, presented in a clean white porcelain bowl. At the center, rich, deep reddish-brown stew with tender chunks of chicken (cut into 4cm pieces) is spooned over a bed of fluffy white basmati rice. The stew's surface glistens with the slight oil from the peanut butter, and hints of tender, wilted spinach leaves are visible throughout. Alongside, golden-brown caramelized banana slices (cut into 1.5cm thick rounds) are carefully arranged, offering a contrasting sweet-savory note and textural interest. A sprinkle of fresh chopped cilantro adds a pop of green. The overall presentation is inviting and rustic yet refined. The plate sits on a simple wooden surface with a cotton napkin beside it, under natural, even lighting, evoking a modern bistro setting. A simple metal fork rests beside the bowl.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of fufu or ugali if preferred over rice.
Offer a small dish of piri-piri sauce or a similar hot chili sauce on the side for those who prefer more heat.
Enjoy with a refreshing non-alcoholic beverage like bissap (hibiscus drink).
instructions: Heat 15ml vegetable oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Season chicken cubes with salt and pepper. Sear chicken until golden brown on all sides. Remove chicken and set aside.
Add remaining 15ml vegetable oil to the pot. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion. Cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in paprika, cumin, and cayenne pepper. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in canned diced tomatoes and chicken stock. Bring to a simmer.
Whisk in peanut butter until smooth and fully incorporated.

Return seared chicken to the pot. Ensure chicken is submerged. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 30-40 minutes, or until chicken is tender and cooked through (internal temperature 75°C). Stir occasionally to prevent sticking.
While stew simmers, heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add banana rounds in a single layer. Cook for 2-3 minutes per side until golden brown and slightly caramelized. Set aside.
Stir fresh spinach into the stew during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Cook until wilted.
Taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper.
Serve the stew hot over cooked basmati rice. Arrange caramelized banana slices alongside each portion. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro.
notes: For best results, use natural, unsweetened peanut butter.
Adjust cayenne pepper according to desired spice level.
Ensure bananas are firm ripe; overripe bananas will become mushy.
traditional_techniques: Groundnut (peanut) as a thickening agent and flavor base

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Sardine, Morel Polenta, Strawberry-Radish Gastrique
recipes.visual_description: A single individual portion is presented on an expansive, pristine white bone china plate with a subtle, elegant rim. The setting is a luxurious white Carrara marble surface, softly lit with professional, dramatic lighting casting gentle shadows. A crisp white linen napkin, folded into a precise triangle, rests beside the plate. A pool of creamy, pale yellow morel-infused polenta forms the organic base, its smooth texture contrasting with the rougher surface of the plate. Two perfectly pan-seared sardine fillets, boasting golden-brown, crisp skin and tender, flaky flesh, are carefully placed slightly offset on the polenta. A vibrant, deep red strawberry-radish gastrique is artfully drizzled in an organic, flowing pattern around and partially over the sardine, creating a striking color contrast. A few ultra-thin, translucent slices of pink and white radish are meticulously arranged, providing a delicate pop of color and texture. A single, delicate sprig of fresh dill or chervil is precisely placed for a subtle green accent. Abundant negative space surrounds the dish, emphasizing its minimalist elegance and the architectural precision of its components. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful composition.
instructions: Clean morel mushrooms. Roughly chop half the morels. Leave remaining whole.
Heat 15ml olive oil in a saucepan. Sauté chopped morels until fragrant, about 3 minutes. Add chicken stock. Simmer for 10 minutes to infuse. Strain stock, reserving morels. Keep stock hot.

In a heavy-bottomed pot, bring infused stock to a simmer. Slowly whisk in polenta. Reduce heat to low. Cook, stirring frequently, for 30-40 minutes until creamy and smooth. Stir in 60g butter. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Finely dice shallots and mince garlic.
In a small saucepan, heat 5ml olive oil. Sauté shallots and garlic until softened, about 2 minutes. Add white wine vinegar. Reduce by half.

Add sliced strawberries, sugar, and vegetable stock. Simmer gently for 10-15 minutes until strawberries are soft and liquid reduces to a syrupy consistency. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Discard solids. Season gastrique with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Thinly slice radishes using a mandoline or sharp knife.
Pat sardine fillets very dry with paper towels. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

Heat 10ml olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Place sardine fillets skin-side down. Sear for 2-3 minutes until skin is crisp and golden. Flip and cook for 30 seconds on the flesh side. Remove from pan.
In the same pan, add remaining 20g butter and reserved whole morels. Sauté morels for 2-3 minutes until tender. Season lightly.

To plate, spoon a generous quenelle of morel-infused polenta onto the center of each plate. Arrange 2-3 sardine fillets artfully on the polenta. Drizzle gastrique around and over the sardines. Arrange a few thinly sliced radishes around the dish. Garnish with a small sprig of fresh dill or chervil.

recipes.recipe_name: Baked Spinach and Ricotta Stuffed Shells
recipes.visual_description: A comforting single serving of Baked Spinach and Ricotta Stuffed Shells is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with natural imperfections. The bowl sits on a well-used wooden dining table, hinting at a lived-in family kitchen. Six to eight generously stuffed, plump pasta shells, slightly golden brown from baking, are nestled together. Each shell is bursting with a creamy, green-flecked ricotta and chopped spinach filling, peeking out from the openings. A rich, vibrant red marinara sauce pools around the shells, with patches of bubbling, melted mozzarella cheese creating a golden crust. A few fresh basil leaves are scattered over the top for a touch of green. A simple, silver fork rests casually beside the bowl. The lighting is warm and inviting, casting soft shadows and highlighting the comforting textures of the dish, evoking a cozy, homely atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 190°C. Lightly grease a 20x20 cm baking dish.
Cook pasta shells according to package directions until al dente. Drain well. Rinse with cold water to prevent sticking.
Heat olive oil in a pan over medium heat. Add minced garlic. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add fresh spinach to the pan. Cook until wilted. Squeeze out excess water from spinach. Roughly chop the spinach.
In a medium bowl, combine ricotta cheese, chopped spinach, grated Parmesan, egg, nutmeg, salt, and pepper. Mix well until combined.
Spread a thin layer of marinara sauce (about 100g) on the bottom of the prepared baking dish.
Carefully stuff each cooked pasta shell with the ricotta-spinach mixture.
Arrange the stuffed shells in a single layer in the baking dish. They can touch or slightly overlap.
Pour the remaining marinara sauce evenly over the stuffed shells.
Sprinkle shredded mozzarella cheese generously over the sauce and shells.
Bake for 20-25 minutes, or until the sauce is bubbling and the cheese is melted and golden brown.
Remove from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes before serving. Garnish with fresh chopped basil.

recipes.recipe_name: Swiss Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Swiss Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Rice is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate on a light wooden table. The creamy rice, cooked to a fluid consistency, forms a natural mound, showcasing vibrant green peas and earthy brown sliced mushrooms. Thick, golden-brown pan-seared chicken medallions, cooked to perfection, are artfully placed on top of the rice. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped parsley, adding a pop of green. The colors are rich and natural: golden chicken, creamy white rice, bright green peas, and deep brown mushrooms. The texture contrast is evident between the seared chicken and the tender, luscious rice. A simple silver fork and knife rest beside the plate on a folded white cotton napkin. The setting is a modern bistro, with natural, even lighting highlighting the dish's inviting appeal. The background is clean and uncluttered, emphasizing the food.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a simple green salad dressed with a light vinaigrette.
Offer crusty bread on the side for soaking up the creamy sauce.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.

Sear chicken breasts 4-5 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through to an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan. Rest on a cutting board. Slice into thick medallions.
Add butter to the same pan. Reduce heat to medium. Add diced onion. Sauté 3 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until mushrooms are browned and tender.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir 1 minute to coat grains.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until wine is fully absorbed.
Add one ladle of hot chicken broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed. Repeat this process, adding broth ladle by ladle, until rice is creamy and al dente (about 18-20 minutes).
Stir in frozen green peas. Cook 2 minutes.
Remove pan from heat. Stir in grated Gruyère cheese and heavy cream until melted and combined. Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Ladle creamy rice onto individual plates. Arrange seared chicken medallions on top of the rice.
Garnish generously with fresh chopped parsley. Serve immediately.
notes: Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Stirring the rice constantly is key to achieving a creamy texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Roasted Lobster Tail, Smoked Eggplant Puree, Jamón Ibérico Crisp
recipes.visual_description: A single roasted lobster tail, halved lengthwise, presents its vibrant, opaque flesh, nestled beside a rich, dark smoked eggplant puree. The puree is artfully swiped or dolloped, creating an organic, flowing shape. A delicate, golden saffron-shellfish nage pools around the components, catching the light. Thin, irregular shards of crispy Jamón Ibérico stand upright, adding height and textural contrast. The plate, a pristine white bone china, provides abundant negative space, emphasizing the dish's minimalist elegance. A few vibrant green microgreens or chervil sprigs are precisely placed for a final touch of freshness and color. The scene is set on a premium grey veined marble surface, with dramatic professional lighting creating soft shadows, highlighting the dish as the sole focus.
instructions: Blanch lobsters in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath. Twist off tails and claws. Split tails lengthwise. Remove meat. Crack claws and knuckles; reserve meat for nage.
Pierce eggplants. Grill or char eggplants over high heat until skin is blackened and flesh is very soft. Scoop out flesh. Discard skin.
Blend smoked eggplant flesh with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper until very smooth. Keep warm.
Lay Jamón Ibérico slices on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper. Bake at 160°C until very crisp, about 8-10 minutes. Cool. Break into shards.

In a saucepan, heat 15ml olive oil. Sauté finely minced shallots and garlic until fragrant. Add reserved lobster claw and knuckle meat. Deglaze with white wine. Reduce by half. Add fish stock and saffron threads. Simmer gently for 15 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Return liquid to pan. Whisk in butter until emulsified. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.
Preheat oven to 200°C. Drizzle lobster tails with a little olive oil, salt, and pepper. Roast flesh-side up for 6-8 minutes, or until cooked through and opaque. Squeeze fresh lemon juice over.

Spoon a generous dollop of smoked eggplant puree onto each plate. Place a roasted lobster tail alongside the puree. Drizzle saffron-shellfish nage around the lobster and puree. Garnish with Jamón Ibérico crisps and a few sprigs of chervil or microgreens.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented White Bean & Chipotle Spread
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion of the Fermented White Bean & Chipotle Spread is elegantly presented on a small, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural off-white tone. A thin, golden-brown slice of toasted sourdough bread serves as the base. The creamy, pale beige spread is generously applied to the bread, showcasing its smooth, thick texture. On top, a few translucent, pinkish-purple rings of thinly sliced pickled shallots are carefully placed, adding a vibrant pop of color and crisp texture. A light scattering of finely chopped bright green chives or flat-leaf parsley provides a fresh, aromatic garnish. The composition emphasizes clean lines and natural forms, with ample negative space on the plate. The setting features a light, textured reclaimed wood surface, an undyed linen napkin in natural beige, and soft, diffused natural lighting. The background is minimalist, allowing the dish to be the sole focal point.

ingredients.name: Reserved bean cooking liquid or water

instructions: Prepare pickled shallots. Thinly slice shallots into rings. Combine apple cider vinegar, 50ml water, sugar, 2g salt, and peppercorns in a small saucepan. Bring to a boil. Pour hot brine over sliced shallots in a heatproof jar. Let cool completely. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.

Prepare fermented white beans. If using dry beans, cook until tender; reserve cooking liquid. Drain canned beans, rinse, reserve liquid. Lightly mash cooked beans in a clean glass jar. Add 5g salt and 100ml reserved bean liquid or water. Mix well. Cover jar loosely with a lid or cloth. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 1-2 days. Beans should develop a slight tangy aroma. Stir daily.

Make chipotle bean spread. Transfer fermented beans to a food processor. Add chipotle in adobo, garlic clove, nutritional yeast, and lemon juice. Process until very creamy and smooth. Add more bean liquid or water, 15ml at a time, if needed for desired consistency. Taste and adjust salt.
Toast sourdough bread slices until golden and crisp.
Finely chop fresh parsley or chives.

Assemble dish. Spread a generous amount of fermented white bean and chipotle spread onto each toasted sourdough slice. Arrange a few pickled shallot rings artfully on top of the spread. Sprinkle with chopped fresh herbs. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Wagyu Striploin, Broccoli Puree, Banana-Black Garlic Jus
recipes.visual_description: A single, refined serving rests on a large, pristine white bone china plate, showcasing abundant negative space. The plate is set on a cool white Carrara marble surface. A flowing, organic smear of vibrant, silky broccoli stem puree anchors the left. Two thick, perfectly seared Wagyu striploin medallions, with a deep, caramelized crust and medium-rare interior, are artfully arranged to the right. Beside the beef, two small, vivid green broccoli florets, lightly charred, provide textural contrast. A small, glossy pool of deep amber-brown banana-black garlic jus is precisely placed. The composition is asymmetrical, natural, and elegant. A crisp white linen napkin, folded precisely, lies to the left. Dramatic, focused lighting casts soft shadows, highlighting textures and colors against the minimalist background.

ingredients.name: Broccoli
ingredients.quantity: 2 large heads (stems for puree, florets for charring)

instructions: Prepare Broccoli: Separate broccoli heads into florets and stems. Peel the tough outer layer of the stems. Cut stems into 2 cm pieces. Reserve a few small, perfect florets for charring. Blanch remaining florets in salted boiling water for 1 minute. Immediately transfer to ice bath. Drain well.

Make Broccoli Puree: Steam broccoli stem pieces until very tender, about 10-12 minutes. Transfer steamed stems to a high-speed blender. Add 20g butter, a splash of hot water, salt, and pepper. Blend until perfectly smooth and vibrant green. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve for ultimate silkiness. Keep warm.

Prepare Banana-Black Garlic Jus: Finely dice shallots. Slice banana into 1 cm rounds. In a small saucepan, melt 10g butter with 10 ml olive oil over medium heat. Add shallots; cook until translucent. Add banana rounds; cook until lightly caramelized, about 3-4 minutes. Add black garlic cloves. Deglaze with red wine; reduce by half. Add beef stock; bring to a simmer. Reduce by one-third until slightly thickened. Strain the jus through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids to extract all liquid. Season with salt and pepper. If desired, whisk in a tiny pinch of xanthan gum for desired consistency. Keep warm.

Sear Wagyu Striploin: Pat Wagyu striploin portions dry with paper towels. Season generously with sea salt and black pepper on all sides. Heat remaining 20 ml olive oil in a heavy-bottomed pan or cast iron skillet over high heat until shimmering and almost smoking. Carefully place Wagyu portions in the hot pan. Sear for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness, forming a deep, rich crust. Add remaining 20g butter to the pan during the last minute of cooking, basting the beef with melted butter. Remove beef from pan. Rest on a cutting board for 5-7 minutes.

Char Broccoli Florets: While beef rests, heat a small non-stick pan or cast iron skillet over high heat. Add reserved small broccoli florets. Cook without oil, turning occasionally, until florets develop charred edges and are tender-crisp. Season lightly with salt.

Plate Dish: Slice each rested Wagyu striploin portion into 2-3 thick, even medallions. On each plate, create an organic smear of broccoli puree. Arrange 2-3 Wagyu medallions artfully beside the puree. Place 2-3 charred broccoli florets delicately near the beef. Spoon a small pool or drizzle of the banana-black garlic jus beside the elements. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chocolate Raspberry Entremet
recipes.visual_description: A single, exquisite Chocolate Raspberry Entremet commands the center of a pristine white porcelain dessert plate with a delicate gold rim. The entremet, approximately 7 cm in diameter and 4 cm tall, is perfectly cylindrical with sharp, clean edges, coated in a flawless, high-gloss dark chocolate mirror glaze that reflects light like liquid glass. The glaze is a deep, rich brown, almost black, hinting at the intense chocolate within. Atop the entremet, precisely placed, are two vibrant, plump fresh raspberries, their bright red contrasting sharply with the dark glaze. A delicate, almost invisible, wisp of edible gold leaf is strategically placed next to the raspberries, catching the light and adding a touch of luxury without distracting. The plate itself is immaculately clean, with abundant negative space around the entremet, emphasizing its architectural precision and elegant simplicity. The setting is a pristine white marble surface, reflecting the sophisticated ambiance of a haute patisserie shop. Lighting is dramatic, creating subtle shadows that enhance the entremet's form and shine. A precisely folded white linen napkin sits to the side, maintaining the ultra-minimalist background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve chilled with a small espresso.
Serve with a glass of dessert wine.
instructions: Prepare Raspberry Crémeux: Combine raspberry puree, 20g sugar, and 2 egg yolks in a saucepan. Whisk constantly over medium heat until thickened (82°C). Remove from heat. Stir in 2g bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Add 30g cold butter, emulsify with an immersion blender until smooth. Pour into small silicone molds (approx. 4 cm diameter). Freeze completely.

Prepare Chocolate Génoise: Preheat oven to 170°C. Line a 20x20 cm baking tray with parchment paper. Whisk 2 eggs and 60g sugar until pale, thick, and doubled in volume. Sift 40g flour and 20g cocoa powder together. Gently fold dry ingredients into egg mixture in two additions. Pour batter onto prepared tray. Spread evenly. Bake 10-12 minutes, or until a skewer comes out clean. Cool completely. Cut out 4 discs (same size as entremet molds).
Prepare Praline Crunch: In a bowl, combine 50g melted milk chocolate, 50g feuilletine, and 30g hazelnut praline paste. Mix well. Press a thin layer onto the 4 génoise discs. Chill until set.

Prepare Dark Chocolate Mousse: Melt 150g dark chocolate over a bain-marie. Bloom 2g gelatin. Whisk 1 egg yolk and 15g sugar until pale. Heat 50ml milk until simmering. Temper egg yolk mixture with hot milk. Return to saucepan. Cook over low heat, stirring, until thickened (nappe consistency). Stir in bloomed gelatin until dissolved. Pour hot custard over melted chocolate. Emulsify with an immersion blender until smooth. Let cool to 30-35°C. Whip 250ml cold heavy cream to soft peaks. Gently fold whipped cream into chocolate mixture in two additions.

Assemble Entremets: Place 4 individual silicone entremet molds (e.g., 7 cm diameter, 4 cm height) on a tray. Pipe or spoon a layer of chocolate mousse into each mold (one-third full). Gently push a frozen raspberry crémeux insert into the center of the mousse. Cover with more chocolate mousse, filling mold almost to top. Place a génoise disc with praline crunch side down onto the mousse. Gently press. Smooth top. Freeze entremets for at least 6 hours, preferably overnight, until completely solid.

Prepare Mirror Glaze: Bloom 7g gelatin. In a saucepan, combine 75ml water, 150g sugar, and 150g glucose syrup. Bring to a boil (103°C). Remove from heat. Stir in 100ml sweetened condensed milk. Add bloomed gelatin, stir until dissolved. Pour mixture over 150g chopped white chocolate. Emulsify with an immersion blender, avoiding air bubbles. Add red food coloring if desired. Strain glaze through a fine-mesh sieve. Let cool to 32-35°C for glazing.

Glaze and Garnish: Remove frozen entremets from molds. Place on a wire rack set over a tray. Pour warm mirror glaze evenly over each frozen entremet, ensuring full coverage. Let excess drip off. Carefully transfer glazed entremets to individual serving plates. Garnish each with fresh raspberries and edible gold leaf. Allow to thaw in refrigerator for 2-3 hours before serving.
notes: Ensure all ingredients are measured precisely for optimal results.
Achieve precise temperatures for crémeux and glaze for perfect texture and shine.
Use high-quality couverture chocolate for superior flavor and texture.

recipes.recipe_name: Braised Chicken with Mustard and Oregano
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of braised chicken is presented on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A golden-brown, whole chicken thigh with slightly crisp skin sits prominently on one side of the plate. Adjacent to the chicken, a neat scoop of fluffy, light brown rice is placed. A rich, glossy, amber-hued sauce, infused with mustard and oregano, is generously spooned over the chicken, pooling slightly around the base of the rice. Flecks of vibrant green chopped fresh parsley are scattered over the chicken and sauce, adding a pop of color. The plating is balanced and organized, allowing for moderate negative space. The dish rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded cotton napkin. Natural, even lighting illuminates the scene, highlighting the textures and warm colors of the dish in a casual bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with crusty bread to soak up the sauce
Pair with a simple green salad
instructions: Pat chicken thighs dry. Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat olive oil in a large oven-safe pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Sear chicken thighs skin-side down until golden brown and crisp, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and sear other side for 3-4 minutes. Remove chicken from pot. Set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add diced yellow onion to the pot. Cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add minced garlic. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in Dijon mustard and dried oregano. Cook for 1 minute.
Pour in chicken stock. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the bottom of the pot.
Return chicken thighs to the pot, skin-side up. Ensure chicken is partially submerged in liquid.

Cover the pot. Transfer to a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F). Braise for 30 minutes. Uncover. Continue braising for another 15-20 minutes, or until chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C (167°F) and sauce has slightly thickened.
While chicken braises, cook brown rice according to package instructions.
Remove chicken from oven. Let rest for 5 minutes. Stir chopped fresh parsley into the sauce.
Serve chicken thighs with brown rice. Spoon sauce generously over chicken and rice.
notes: Ensure chicken is thoroughly cooked to 75°C (167°F) for food safety.
Adjust mustard quantity to your preferred tanginess.

recipes.recipe_name: Sustainable Fermented Tofu & Miso Soup
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Sustainable Fermented Tofu & Miso Soup is presented in a handcrafted, off-white ceramic bowl. The rich, earthy brown broth forms the base, with tender, whole white beans and vibrant green peas settled naturally within. Cubed, slightly golden tofu pieces, about 2cm, are gently nestled amongst the other ingredients, showcasing their firm texture. Cooked brown rice forms a subtle bed at the bottom of the bowl. The soup is garnished with finely sliced bright green spring onion, adding a fresh, crisp contrast. The composition is clean and minimalistic, allowing each ingredient’s natural beauty to shine. It sits on a light reclaimed wood surface, accompanied by an undyed linen napkin and a simple wooden spoon. Soft natural lighting illuminates the scene, creating a serene, eco-conscious aesthetic.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of quick-pickled daikon or cucumber.
A sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds can enhance the nutty flavor.

ingredients.name: Vegetable Scraps (onion skins, carrot peels, celery ends, mushroom stems)

instructions: Prepare zero-waste broth: Combine vegetable scraps with 2L water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer for 1 hour. Strain broth through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard solids.
Cook beans: Drain soaked white beans. Place in a pot with 500ml fresh water. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat. Simmer until tender, about 1 to 1.5 hours. Drain excess water.
Prepare tofu: Cut firm tofu into 2cm cubes. For a quick ferment, immerse tofu cubes in a light salt brine (1 tsp salt per 250ml water) for at least 30 minutes. Drain well before use.
Sauté aromatics: Mince garlic and ginger. Heat 5ml sesame oil in a large soup pot over medium heat. Add minced garlic and ginger. Sauté for 1 minute until fragrant.
Combine soup base: Pour the strained vegetable broth into the pot with aromatics. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Add beans and peas: Add the cooked white beans and green peas to the simmering broth. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Incorporate miso: In a small bowl, dissolve miso paste with a ladleful of hot broth until smooth. Stir the dissolved miso into the soup. Do not boil the soup after adding miso.
Add tofu: Gently add the brined tofu cubes to the soup. Heat through for 2-3 minutes.
Season soup: Stir in soy sauce and remaining sesame oil. Taste and adjust salt and pepper as needed.
Cook rice: While soup simmers, cook brown rice according to package instructions.
Serve: Ladle hot soup over cooked brown rice in individual bowls. Garnish generously with finely sliced spring onions.
notes: This recipe emphasizes zero-waste by utilizing vegetable scraps for a flavorful broth.
Quick brining or fermenting tofu enhances its flavor depth and texture.
Adjust miso quantity to personal preference for desired savory intensity.

recipes.recipe_name: Creamy Herb Chicken and Root Vegetables
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of Creamy Herb Chicken and Root Vegetables is presented on a simple, round, off-white ceramic plate. A golden-brown, roasted chicken thigh, coated in a creamy herb crust, is the focal point, positioned slightly off-center. Surrounding the chicken are generously portioned, rustic chunks of roasted potatoes, their skins slightly browned and interiors tender. Thick-cut, vibrant orange carrot rounds are interspersed among the potatoes. All ingredients show natural roasting marks and subtle charring at the edges, indicating proper cooking. A few fresh, chopped parsley leaves are scattered over the chicken and vegetables for a pop of green. The components are naturally arranged, touching and slightly overlapping, creating an inviting, home-cooked feel. The plate is placed on a well-used wooden dining table, revealing its natural grain and minor imperfections. Simple, everyday stainless steel cutlery (fork and knife) rests beside the plate. A casually folded linen napkin in a neutral tone is nearby. Warm, soft light, typical of a cozy kitchen, illuminates the scene, enhancing the comforting appeal of the dish. The background is minimal, showing just a hint of a lived-in family kitchen environment.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash and peel potatoes. Cut into 3 cm chunks.
Wash and peel carrots. Cut into 2 cm thick rounds.
In a large bowl, toss potatoes and carrots with olive oil, 5 ml salt, and 2 ml black pepper. Spread vegetables evenly on a large baking tray.
Pat chicken pieces dry with paper towels.
Mince garlic. Chop parsley finely.
In a small bowl, combine mayonnaise, minced garlic, chopped parsley, 2.5 ml salt, and 1 ml black pepper. Mix well.
Spread mayonnaise mixture evenly over each chicken piece.
Place chicken pieces on the baking tray among the vegetables. Ensure chicken skin is facing up.
Bake for 40-50 minutes. Chicken is done when internal temperature reaches 75°C. Vegetables should be tender and lightly browned.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Chipotle-Fermented Soybean Spread with Roasted Beets
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, vegan cream spread type, fermented
recipes.visual_description: A handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone holds the dish. A single, generous dollop of the creamy, light tan fermented soybean spread occupies the center. Around it, roasted beet wedges are artfully yet naturally scattered, showcasing their deep burgundy and earthy tones. The beets are slightly caramelized, revealing varied textures. A sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh dill and a few delicate pieces of finely chopped beet greens are placed atop the spread and beets, providing a subtle color contrast. The overall composition is minimalistic, emphasizing negative space. Each ingredient's natural beauty is highlighted. The plate rests on a light bamboo or reclaimed wood table surface. An undyed linen napkin in a natural beige is subtly folded beside the plate. Soft, diffused natural light illuminates the scene from the side, creating gentle shadows and enhancing textures. The background is clean and uncluttered, with a hint of a leafy green plant or natural stone visible, reinforcing the eco-conscious theme.

ingredients.name: Dried chipotle chiles, rehydrated and deseeded
Fresh dill or chives, finely chopped

instructions: Prepare Fermented Soybean Spread (start 2-3 days ahead): Soak soybeans in cold water overnight (at least 8 hours). Drain.
Cook soaked soybeans in fresh water until very tender (approx. 1-1.5 hours in a pot, or 30 minutes in a pressure cooker). Drain, reserving 50 ml cooking liquid. Cool completely.
Blend cooked soybeans with salt, rehydrated chipotle chiles, apple cider vinegar, and reserved cooking liquid until very smooth and creamy.

Transfer mixture to a clean glass jar. Cover loosely with a cloth or lid. Let ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 2-3 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Stir daily. Refrigerate after fermentation.
Roast Beets: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash beets thoroughly. Trim greens, reserving them. Cut beets into 2 cm wedges.
Toss beet wedges with olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking tray.
Roast for 25-35 minutes, or until tender and slightly caramelized.
Plate the Dish: Place a generous dollop (approx. 60-70 g) of the fermented soybean spread onto the center of each plate.
Arrange roasted beet wedges naturally around the spread.
Garnish with fresh dill or chives and reserved finely chopped beet greens.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Miso Glazed Eggplant (Nasu Dengaku)
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of two lengthwise-cut eggplant halves, flesh-side up, rests on a pristine round white porcelain plate. The eggplant is deeply roasted, boasting a rich, glossy, caramelized miso glaze. Its surface shows a golden-brown hue with darker, bubbly spots where the glaze has intensified, highlighting the visible crisscross scoring. A vibrant sprinkle of thinly sliced green onions and a scattering of toasted white sesame seeds provide a fresh contrast against the dark, inviting glaze. The plate maintains moderate negative space, showcasing the dish elegantly. It is set on a simple light wooden table. Beside the plate, a small, elegant ceramic bowl of fluffy steamed white rice and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks complete the authentic Japanese dining experience. A neatly folded light grey cotton napkin is placed alongside. The scene is illuminated by soft, natural, even lighting, with a minimalist background suggesting a modern bistro with subtle Japanese aesthetics.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Served with steamed white rice
Can be accompanied by a light clear soup (osuimono)
Can be accompanied by pickled vegetables (tsukemono)
instructions: Wash and trim eggplant ends. Cut each eggplant in half lengthwise.
Score the cut eggplant flesh in a crisscross pattern, about 1 cm deep. Do not cut through the skin.
Lightly salt the scored eggplant flesh. Let sit for 15 minutes. Pat dry thoroughly with paper towels.
In a small saucepan, combine miso paste, mirin, sake, sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil, and water.
Whisk ingredients. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until glaze thickens slightly, about 3-5 minutes. Remove from heat.
Heat vegetable oil in a large frying pan over medium-high heat. Add eggplant halves, flesh-side down.
Cook until golden brown and tender, about 5-7 minutes. Flip and cook skin-side down for 3-4 minutes until skin is tender.
Transfer eggplant to a baking sheet, flesh-side up. Preheat broiler.
Generously brush miso glaze over the scored eggplant flesh.
Broil for 3-5 minutes, watching carefully, until glaze is caramelized and bubbly.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and thinly sliced green onions. Serve immediately.
notes: Salting the eggplant helps remove excess moisture, preventing sogginess and improving glaze absorption.
Adjust sugar in glaze to taste.
Watch eggplant closely under broiler to prevent burning due to sugar in glaze.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoked Paprika Potato Salad with Fermented Pepper Relish
recipes.visual_description: The Smoked Paprika Potato Salad is presented on a handcrafted, unglazed ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone, resting on a light, textured bamboo surface. Roasted potato cubes, with their skins on and a light dusting of red paprika, form the base, interspersed with vibrant yellow charred corn kernels, bright red halved cherry tomatoes, and small white cubes of cheese. Minimal diced chicken pieces are subtly integrated, not fanned, amidst the vegetables. The fermented bell pepper and onion relish adds pops of deep red and purple, its slightly translucent texture visible. A light vinaigrette glistens on the ingredients, binding them visually. The plating is clean and minimalist, with ample negative space highlighting the natural beauty and varied textures of each component. A sprinkle of fresh green chopped parsley provides a final touch of color. The setting features an undyed linen napkin in a natural beige and soft, diffused natural lighting from the side, with a hint of green foliage in the clean, blurred background.

ingredients.name: Small new potatoes or waxy potatoes, unpeeled
Mature cheddar or smoked gouda, diced into 1 cm cubes
Boneless, skinless chicken breast, diced into 1.5 cm cubes
Red bell pepper, diced into 1 cm pieces

instructions: Prepare Fermented Relish (3-5 days in advance): In a clean 1-liter jar, combine diced red bell pepper and thinly sliced red onion. Dissolve 10 g salt in 500 ml non-chlorinated water to make a 2% brine. Pour brine over vegetables, ensuring they are fully submerged. Seal jar loosely. Ferment at room temperature (20-24°C) for 3-5 days, or until desired tanginess is achieved. Burp daily. Once fermented, seal tightly and refrigerate.

Roast Potatoes: Preheat oven to 200°C. Wash potatoes thoroughly, do not peel. Cut larger potatoes into 2-3 cm cubes, keeping smaller ones whole. Toss potatoes with 30 ml olive oil, smoked paprika, salt, and pepper on a baking tray. Roast for 25-30 minutes, or until tender and lightly browned.

Char Corn: While potatoes roast, remove husks and silk from corn cobs. Heat a large cast-iron skillet or grill pan over high heat. Add corn cobs and char for 8-10 minutes, rotating frequently, until kernels are tender and lightly blackened in spots. Once cooled, carefully cut kernels from cobs using a sharp knife.

Cook Chicken: Heat a small amount of olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add diced chicken. Season with salt and pepper. Cook for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until chicken is cooked through and reaches an internal temperature of 75°C.

Prepare Dressing: In a small bowl, whisk together 30 ml fermentation liquid, 60 ml olive oil, 15 ml apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, and maple syrup (if using). Season with salt and pepper to taste.

Assemble Salad: In a large bowl, combine roasted potatoes, charred corn kernels, halved cherry tomatoes, diced cheese, and cooked diced chicken. Add 60-80 g of the fermented bell pepper and onion relish. Pour dressing over the salad. Toss gently to combine.
Serve: Transfer salad to individual plates. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley or cilantro.
notes: The fermented relish is a key flavor component and requires advance preparation.
For zero-waste, corn cobs can be simmered in water to make a flavorful vegetable stock.
Adjust the amount of fermented relish based on desired tanginess.
Ensure chicken reaches an internal temperature of 75°C for food safety.

recipes.recipe_name: Fermented Tofu & Chipotle Tartare
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, vegan cream spread type, fermented
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is presented on a round, handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream or beige tone. The plate rests on a light bamboo table surface, showcasing its natural grain. In the center, a generous, organically shaped dollop of the creamy, off-white fermented tofu forms the visual anchor. Its texture is smooth yet subtly rustic. Around the tofu, thinly sliced, vibrant pink pickled radish rounds are artfully scattered, their translucent edges catching the light. Bright green blanched edamame pods are strategically placed, adding pops of contrasting color and rounded forms. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh green chives and a few golden-brown toasted sesame seeds are delicately dusted over the tofu and surrounding elements, providing subtle texture and natural color accents. Negative space on the plate is abundant, emphasizing the clean, ingredient-focused presentation. The background is minimalist, with a hint of natural light and possibly a soft, out-of-focus green plant element. An undyed linen napkin in natural beige is casually draped beside the plate. Soft, natural lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting the natural textures and colors of the ingredients without harsh shadows. The entire plate is visible, showcasing the thoughtful arrangement and the dish's minimalistic beauty.

ingredients.name: Chipotle chile in adobo, finely minced

instructions: Press tofu for 30 minutes to remove excess water. Wrap in a clean cloth. Place heavy object on top.

Combine pressed tofu, miso paste, minced chipotle, adobo sauce, half of lime juice, and 15 ml olive oil in a food processor. Process until smooth and creamy. Season with sea salt. Taste and adjust. Transfer to a bowl. Cover. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes to firm. This allows flavors to meld and develop a fermented-like depth.

For pickled radishes: In a small saucepan, combine rice vinegar, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Heat gently until sugar dissolves. Let cool completely. Add thinly sliced radishes to the cooled pickling liquid. Marinate for at least 20 minutes.
Blanch edamame in boiling salted water for 2-3 minutes. Drain immediately. Rinse with cold water to stop cooking. Pat dry.

To assemble: Place a generous spoonful of the fermented tofu mixture onto each of four white ceramic plates. Use the back of a spoon to create a slight swirl or smear. Arrange a few pickled radish slices and blanched edamame around the tofu. Garnish with chopped fresh chives and a sprinkle of toasted sesame seeds. Drizzle with remaining olive oil and a few drops of fresh lime juice just before serving.
notes: This recipe embraces zero-waste by utilizing full ingredients. Consider composting any vegetable scraps.

recipes.recipe_name: Beef Tartare Bites with Aged Cheddar Tuiles and Chili Oil
recipes.visual_description: A sophisticated sharing platter showcasing 'Beef Tartare Bites with Aged Cheddar Tuiles and Chili Oil'. The composition features four meticulously arranged individual bites on a large, round, modern designer bone china plate with a subtle, pristine white finish, resting on a premium white Carrara marble surface. Each bite presents a delicate, perfectly formed quenelle of deep ruby-red beef tartare, precisely diced into 2mm cubes. Perched atop each tartare is a golden-brown, irregularly shaped, crisp aged cheddar tuile. A scattering of dark, finely crumbled crispy bacon dust encircles the base of the tartare. A single, vibrant red dot of chili oil is artfully placed beside each tartare quenelle, and a tiny sprig of vivid green micro cilantro delicately garnishes the tuile. Abundant negative space surrounds the elements, emphasizing their architectural precision and minimalist elegance. The scene is illuminated by dramatic professional lighting, casting soft, intentional shadows, with an ultra-minimalist background, highlighting the pristine white linen napkin folded into a sharp triangle. The overall presentation is one of luxurious simplicity and refined culinary artistry.
instructions: Prepare bacon crumble: Dice smoked streaky bacon into small pieces. Render bacon slowly in a dry pan until very crispy. Drain on paper towel. Crumble finely once cool.

Make chili oil: Heat neutral oil in a small saucepan to 80°C. Add dried red chili flakes. Let steep off heat for 30 minutes. Strain oil through a fine-mesh sieve. Discard chili solids. Cool completely.

Prepare cheddar tuiles: Grate aged cheddar cheese. Spread thinly in irregular shapes on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Bake at 180°C until golden and crispy (approx. 5-7 minutes). Cool completely on the tray. Break into elegant, irregular shards.
Prepare beef tartare: Pat beef tenderloin dry. Dice beef into very precise 2mm cubes. Ensure consistency. Place diced beef in a chilled bowl.
Finely mince shallot, capers, and cornichons. Add to beef.
Add Dijon mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and extra virgin olive oil to the beef mixture. Season with fine sea salt and freshly ground black pepper. Gently fold to combine. Do not overmix.
Plate immediately: Form small, elegant quenelles or precise mounds of beef tartare onto a sharing platter. Arrange 3-4 portions per platter.
Place an irregular aged cheddar tuile gently on top of each tartare mound. Scatter a small amount of crispy bacon crumble around the base of the tartare.
Dot the platter with a few drops of the vibrant chili oil. Garnish each bite with a single sprig of micro cilantro or a few finely snipped chives.
Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Beef Medallion, Silky Potato-Carrot Puree, Charred Broccoli, Tomato-Mustard Jus, Crispy Rice
recipes.visual_description: A single pan-seared beef tenderloin medallion, perfectly cooked to a rosy medium-rare, rests elegantly on a premium bone china plate. Beside it, a luscious, vibrant orange potato-carrot puree forms a sculptural quenelle. A few charred broccoli florets, their edges kissed with a slight char and bright green, are artfully arranged nearby, adding a pop of verdant color and textural contrast. A small, clear pool of glossy, reddish-amber tomato-garlic-mustard jus gleams on the plate, adding depth and richness. A delicate, translucent crispy rice tuile stands upright, providing an architectural element and subtle texture. The composition is minimalist and precise, with abundant negative space highlighting each component. The plate sits on a grey veined marble surface, accompanied by a pristine white linen napkin folded into a precise triangle and modern, minimalist flatware. Dramatic, professional lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the dish's sophisticated allure.
instructions: Prepare the Tomato-Garlic-Mustard Jus: Preheat oven to 200°C. Halve tomatoes, garlic cloves, and onion. Toss with 15 ml olive oil. Roast 25 minutes until caramelized. Transfer to a saucepan. Add beef stock. Simmer 30 minutes. Strain through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing solids. Return liquid to pan. Stir in Dijon mustard. Reduce until glossy and lightly coats a spoon. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare the Potato-Carrot Puree: Peel and dice potatoes and carrots into small cubes. Boil in salted water until very tender, about 15-20 minutes. Drain well. Pass through a ricer or fine sieve into a clean saucepan. Add butter, heavy cream, and mayonnaise. Whisk vigorously until silky smooth. Season with salt and pepper. Keep warm.

Prepare the Crispy Rice Tuile: In a small bowl, whisk rice flour with water until smooth. Heat a non-stick pan over medium-low heat. Pour a very thin layer of batter to form a 8 cm circle. Cook until edges crisp and center is dry, about 2-3 minutes. Carefully flip and cook 30 seconds more. Transfer to a wire rack to cool and crisp. Repeat for 4 tuiles.

Prepare the Broccoli: Wash broccoli. Cut into small, uniform florets. Blanch in boiling salted water for 2 minutes. Immediately transfer to an ice bath to stop cooking. Drain well. Heat a pan with 15 ml olive oil over medium-high heat. Add broccoli florets. Char lightly for 2-3 minutes until bright green and slightly tender-crisp. Season with salt.

Prepare the Beef Medallions: Pat beef tenderloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper. Heat a heavy-bottomed pan over high heat with a touch of olive oil. Sear beef medallions 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or to desired doneness. Remove from pan. Rest 5 minutes on a cutting board.

Plate the dish: Place a generous quenelle or swoosh of potato-carrot puree slightly off-center on each plate. Arrange one beef medallion next to the puree. Artfully place a few charred broccoli florets. Spoon a small pool of the tomato-garlic-mustard jus beside the beef. Gently stand one crispy rice tuile upright or lean it against the beef. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Quick Pickled Root Vegetable & Tofu Pâté with Miso Cream
recipes.special_requests: vegetarian, vegan cream spread type, fermented
recipes.visual_description: A single starter portion is elegantly presented on a handcrafted ceramic plate in a natural cream tone. The plate is light bamboo or reclaimed wood. The primary element is a smooth, off-white tofu pâté, scooped into a organic, slightly irregular mound. Its texture is soft and inviting. Drizzled over and around the pâté is a contrasting, pale yellow miso cream, forming natural, flowing lines. Finely sliced green chives are scattered over the cream, adding a pop of fresh color and delicate texture. A sprinkle of black sesame seeds provides a subtle contrast. The arrangement is clean, with ample white space on the plate. Natural lighting highlights the ingredients' inherent beauty. The background is minimalist, with subtle hints of natural elements like green plants or undyed linen. A simple, natural wood fork rests beside the plate.
instructions: Prepare quick pickled vegetables: Peel carrots and daikon. Cut into 5 cm long, 3 mm thin batons. In a clean jar, combine rice vinegar, 150 ml water, sugar, and salt. Stir until dissolved. Add carrot and daikon batons. Seal jar. Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours for stronger flavor.
Press tofu: Wrap tofu block in a clean kitchen towel. Place on a plate. Top with a heavy object. Press for 20 minutes to remove excess water.

Prepare tofu pâté: Mince garlic and ginger finely. In a food processor, combine pressed tofu, minced garlic, minced ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper. Pulse until smooth and creamy. Do not over-process. Transfer to a bowl.
Prepare miso cream: In a small bowl, whisk together vegan cream cheese, white miso paste, and 30 ml water until smooth and creamy. Add more water if needed to reach a drizzleable consistency.

Assemble and garnish: Drain quick pickled vegetables. Finely chop 50g of the pickled vegetables. Fold chopped pickled vegetables into the tofu pâté. Divide pâté among four small serving plates. Create a slight indentation in the center of each pâté portion. Drizzle miso cream generously into the indentation and around the pâté. Thinly slice chives. Garnish each plate with sliced chives and a sprinkle of black sesame seeds. Serve immediately with crusty bread or plant-based crackers.

recipes.recipe_name: Smoky Beef & Bacon Cheddar Patties
recipes.visual_description: A single, thick, seared beef patty sits centered on a clean, white porcelain dinner plate. A generous slice of sharp cheddar cheese is melted and gently draped over the rich brown patty. Scattered atop the melted cheese are crispy, golden-brown bacon lardons, adding texture and a contrasting color. A glossy, rich red chili glaze, made with finely diced aromatics, is artfully spooned beside the patty, with some gently cascading onto its base. The entire dish is garnished with a sprinkle of freshly chopped vibrant green chives. The presentation is professional and approachable, with ample negative space around the central dish. The plate rests on a simple wooden table surface, accompanied by standard silver flatware and a folded grey cotton napkin, under natural, even lighting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a side of crispy potato wedges or a simple green salad for a complete meal.
Often enjoyed with classic American condiments like ketchup or mustard, though the glaze provides ample flavor.
instructions: Dice bacon into small lardons. Cook bacon in a cold pan over medium heat until crispy. Remove bacon with a slotted spoon. Reserve 5 ml bacon fat.
Form beef mince into two thick, round patties (approx. 200g each). Season generously with salt and black pepper.

Heat remaining bacon fat and 5 ml vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Sear beef patties for 4-5 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness is reached. Remove patties from pan. Keep warm.
For the chili glaze: finely dice red onion and mince garlic. Finely chop fresh red chili. Add 10 ml vegetable oil to the same skillet.
Sauté red onion for 3 minutes until softened. Add garlic and chopped chili. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in tomato paste, smoked paprika, and ground cumin. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly.

Pour in beef stock and Worcestershire sauce. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Simmer for 5-7 minutes, stirring occasionally, until glaze thickens. Season glaze with salt and pepper to taste.

Place a thick slice of cheddar cheese on each warm beef patty. Return patties to the skillet or a baking sheet. Melt cheese under a broiler or with a lid on the skillet for 1-2 minutes until bubbling and slightly draped.

Plate each patty on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. Spoon a generous amount of chili glaze beside and partially over each patty. Sprinkle crispy bacon lardons over the melted cheddar. Garnish with freshly chopped chives.
Serve immediately.
notes: Adjust chili quantity based on desired spice level.
For extra smoky flavor, add a dash of liquid smoke to the beef mince before forming patties.

recipes.recipe_name: Seared Beef with Roasted Vegetables and Creamy Garlic Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single serving of seared beef with roasted vegetables and creamy garlic sauce is presented on a clean, round white porcelain dinner plate. The beef sirloin, cut into thick, juicy medallions with a deep brown sear, is the central focus, positioned slightly off-center. Alongside the beef, a vibrant medley of roasted vegetables is neatly arranged: bright green broccoli florets, orange carrot batons, golden-brown potato wedges, and slightly blistered red cherry tomatoes. Each vegetable shows distinct cooking marks, indicating a tender-crisp texture. A swirl of pale yellow, creamy garlic sauce is artfully drizzled over the beef and around the plate, contrasting with the darker tones. A small mound of fluffy white basmati rice sits adjacent to the vegetables. The dish is garnished with a sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green parsley. The overall composition is balanced, professional, and inviting. The setting is a modern bistro, with a simple wooden table surface, standard silver flatware, and a folded white cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its textures and colors against a soft, blurred background consistent with a casual restaurant atmosphere.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Toss potato wedges, broccoli florets, carrot batons, and cherry tomatoes with 30 ml olive oil, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast vegetables for 25-30 minutes, or until tender-crisp and slightly caramelized.
Rinse basmati rice. Cook according to package directions.
While rice cooks, pat beef sirloin dry. Season generously with salt and pepper.
Heat remaining 30 ml olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear beef for 3-4 minutes per side for medium-rare, or until desired doneness.
Remove beef from pan. Let rest 5 minutes.
In the same pan, add diced onion and minced garlic. Sauté 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Deglaze with beef broth. Scrape up browned bits.
Whisk in mayonnaise and Dijon mustard. Simmer 1 minute. Season sauce with salt and pepper.
Slice beef into thick medallions.
Plate by placing a portion of rice on one side. Arrange roasted vegetables next to rice. Place beef medallions beside vegetables. Spoon creamy garlic sauce over beef and around plate.
Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Pineapple Chicken Stir-fry
recipes.visual_description: A single portion of Pineapple Chicken Stir-fry is presented on a clean white porcelain dinner plate. A neat mound of fluffy jasmine rice occupies one side, while the vibrant stir-fry is artfully mounded beside it. Diced chicken pieces, golden-brown and glistening with sauce, are interspersed with bright yellow pineapple chunks, translucent onion wedges, and crisp red and green bell pepper squares. Each ingredient retains its distinct shape and texture. The dish is coated in a glossy, savory-sweet glaze. A generous sprinkle of thinly sliced green spring onions and toasted white sesame seeds provides a fresh garnish. The setting is a modern bistro: a simple wooden table, a white cotton napkin beside the plate, and a pair of dark wooden chopsticks resting on a small, elegant white rice bowl. Natural, even lighting illuminates the dish, highlighting its fresh colors and textures against a softly blurred, casual restaurant background.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with chopsticks and a small rice bowl.
instructions: Cut chicken breast into 2cm cubes.
Cut pineapple into 2cm chunks.
Cut onion into thick 2cm wedges.
Cut bell peppers into 2cm squares.
Mince garlic and grate ginger.
In a bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, brown sugar, cornstarch, water, and sesame oil for the sauce. Set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat.
Add chicken cubes. Stir-fry until golden brown and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C.
Remove chicken from wok.
Add remaining 1 tbsp vegetable oil to the wok. Add onion, bell peppers, garlic, and ginger. Stir-fry for 3-4 minutes until vegetables are tender-crisp.
Return chicken to the wok. Add pineapple chunks.
Re-whisk the sauce and pour into the wok. Cook, stirring constantly, until sauce thickens and coats ingredients, about 1-2 minutes.
Serve immediately over jasmine rice. Garnish with sliced spring onions and toasted sesame seeds.

recipes.recipe_name: Strawberry-Walnut Mille-Feuille Bites with Cacao-Ginger Crème
recipes.visual_description: A minimalist and artfully composed snack presented on a pristine white Carrara marble serving board. Three to four individual Strawberry-Walnut Mille-Feuille Bites are arranged with ample negative space. Each bite showcases delicate layers: vibrant red, thinly sliced strawberry 'leaves' (approximately 2-3mm thick), alternating with a rich, dark cacao-ginger crème. A subtle, golden-brown walnut praline is visible between the layers, adding textural contrast. A small, glossy dot of deep amber date reduction is strategically placed alongside each bite, offering a visual accent. Each bite is crowned with a single, vivid green micro-basil leaf, providing a fresh pop of color. The composition is organic and flowing, emphasizing the natural beauty of the ingredients. Professional, dramatic lighting casts soft shadows, enhancing the depth and luxurious feel. The overall presentation is one of sophisticated simplicity and precision.
instructions: Prepare Walnut Praline: Toast walnuts in a dry pan until fragrant. Cool. Combine sugar and 15 ml water in a small saucepan. Heat over medium heat until sugar dissolves. Increase heat to medium-high. Cook without stirring until amber caramel forms. Add toasted walnuts and butter. Stir quickly to coat. Pour onto a silicone mat or parchment paper. Cool completely. Break praline into pieces. Process in a food processor until a coarse, sandy texture forms. Do not over-process. Set aside.

Prepare Cacao-Ginger Crème: Finely grate ginger. Squeeze through a fine-mesh sieve to extract ginger juice. Discard pulp. Chop dark chocolate finely. Place in a heatproof bowl. Heat heavy cream in a small saucepan until just simmering. Remove from heat. Pour hot cream over chopped chocolate. Let stand 1 minute. Stir gently until smooth and glossy. Whisk in egg yolk and ginger juice until fully incorporated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours, or until firm enough to pipe.

Prepare Date Reduction: Combine pitted dates, 30 ml water, and a pinch of salt in a small saucepan. Simmer over low heat, stirring occasionally, until dates soften and liquid reduces to a thick, syrupy consistency. Remove from heat. Blend with an immersion blender until very smooth. Pass through a fine-mesh sieve. Cool completely.

Assemble Mille-Feuille Bites: Wash and hull strawberries. Slice strawberries lengthwise into very thin, uniform slices (about 2-3 mm thick). Use a mandoline for precision. Pipe small dots of Cacao-Ginger Crème onto one strawberry slice. Sprinkle a thin layer of walnut praline over the crème. Top with another strawberry slice. Repeat layers: crème, praline, strawberry slice. Aim for 3-4 strawberry layers per bite. Carefully trim edges of the assembled bites to create clean, refined shapes.

recipes.recipe_name: Pan-Seared Chicken with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
recipes.visual_description: A single, perfectly pan-seared chicken breast, golden-brown and whole, rests centrally on a clean white porcelain plate. It is generously coated with a rich, creamy mushroom sauce. The sauce features irregularly sliced, deeply browned cremini mushrooms and finely diced shallots, creating a rustic yet refined texture. Bright green chopped parsley is sprinkled over the chicken and sauce, adding a fresh color contrast. The chicken breast shows a crisp exterior and a tender interior. A small pool of sauce surrounds the base of the chicken. The dish is presented on a simple wooden table, with a folded cotton napkin beside the plate. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's warmth and texture. A single portion, balanced and appealing.
instructions: Pat chicken breasts dry. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in a large pan over medium-high heat.
Sear chicken breasts 5-7 minutes per side until golden brown and cooked through. Ensure internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F). Remove chicken from pan and set aside.
Reduce heat to medium. Add butter to the pan.
Add sliced shallot. Sauté 2 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic. Sauté 1 minute until fragrant.
Add irregularly sliced mushrooms. Cook 5-7 minutes until softened and browned.
Sprinkle flour over mushrooms. Stir for 1 minute to coat.
Pour in chicken broth. Bring to a simmer. Scrape up any browned bits from the pan.
Stir in heavy cream. Simmer for 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Return chicken breasts to the pan. Turn to coat with sauce.
Garnish with chopped fresh parsley. Serve immediately.

recipes.recipe_name: Italian Sausage Risotto
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Italian Sausage Risotto is presented in a shallow, clean white porcelain bowl. The risotto is creamy, fluid, and naturally flows, not molded. It has a warm, inviting off-white hue from the rice and Parmesan. Irregularly shaped, browned chunks of Italian sausage are evenly distributed throughout the risotto, adding depth and a contrasting dark golden-brown color. A light sprinkle of bright green, finely chopped fresh parsley garnishes the top, providing a fresh pop of color. The setting is a modern bistro, with the bowl resting on a simple light wooden table surface. A white cotton napkin is neatly folded beside the bowl. Natural, even lighting highlights the dish's texture and warmth. Traditional Italian flatware is placed alongside the bowl, hinting at authentic dining. The background is minimal, suggesting a casual restaurant atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve immediately, as risotto loses its creamy texture quickly.
Offer extra grated Parmesan cheese at the table.
Serve with a side of crusty Italian bread to sop up any remaining sauce.
instructions: Remove sausage from casings. Break into small chunks.

Heat olive oil in a large, heavy-bottomed pan over medium-high heat. Add sausage chunks. Brown thoroughly, breaking up with a spoon. Cook until no pink remains. Remove sausage to a plate. Reserve rendered fat in the pan.
Finely dice onion. Add to the pan with rendered fat. Cook over medium heat until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes.
Finely mince garlic. Add to the pan. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add Arborio rice to the pan. Stir for 2 minutes to toast the grains.
Pour in white wine. Stir constantly until liquid is fully absorbed.
Heat chicken broth in a separate pot. Keep it simmering hot.

Add one ladle of hot broth to the rice. Stir continuously until broth is absorbed. Continue adding broth one ladle at a time, stirring until each addition is absorbed before adding more. This process takes about 18-20 minutes.
When rice is al dente, creamy but still firm to the bite, return cooked sausage to the pan. Stir to combine.
Remove pan from heat. Add butter and grated Parmesan cheese. Stir vigorously for 1-2 minutes. This is called 'manteca' and creates a creamy, emulsified texture. Risotto should be fluid, not stiff.
Season with salt and pepper to taste. Stir in chopped fresh parsley.
Serve immediately in warm bowls.

recipes.recipe_name: Asian Chicken and Potato Curry with Mango
recipes.visual_description: A single, generous serving of Asian Chicken and Potato Curry with Mango is presented in a rustic, subtly patterned ceramic bowl, centrally placed on a well-worn, light wooden dining table. The curry is a rich, golden-orange hue, featuring substantial chunks of tender, cooked chicken and soft, cubed potatoes. Interspersed throughout are bright yellow, diced pieces of ripe mango, adding a vibrant visual contrast. A sprinkle of fresh, finely chopped green coriander leaves garnishes the top, providing a pop of color and freshness. The bowl is adequately filled, showcasing a hearty, comforting portion. Adjacent to the curry bowl, a small, simple white rice bowl holds a mound of fluffy steamed jasmine rice, and a plain metal spoon rests casually on the table. The scene is illuminated by warm, inviting light, evoking a cozy, lived-in family kitchen atmosphere with natural imperfections and minimal, unobtrusive background elements, emphasizing the homely and appetizing dish.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed jasmine rice.
Offer a side of cooling cucumber raita or a simple green salad.
instructions: Cut chicken thighs into 3-4 cm chunks.
Peel and cut potatoes into 2-3 cm cubes.
Peel and dice mango.
Dice onion. Mince garlic. Grate ginger.
Heat vegetable oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Add chicken chunks. Sear until lightly browned on all sides. Remove chicken from pot.
Add diced onion to the pot. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in curry powder. Cook 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Add canned diced tomatoes to the pot. Cook 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened.
Return seared chicken to the pot. Add cubed potatoes, coconut milk, and chicken broth.
Season with salt and black pepper.
Bring the mixture to a simmer. Reduce heat to low. Cover and cook 20-25 minutes, or until chicken is cooked through and potatoes are tender. Ensure chicken internal temperature reaches 75°C (167°F).
Stir in diced mango. Cook 5 minutes until heated through.
Chop fresh coriander. Garnish curry with chopped coriander before serving.
notes: This recipe is inspired by the comforting flavors of South and Southeast Asian curries, adapted for a home cooking style. It serves 4 people.

recipes.recipe_name: Bratwurst, Potato, and Spätzle Skillet
recipes.visual_description: A hearty single portion of Bratwurst, Potato, and Spätzle Skillet is presented centrally on a round white porcelain dinner plate. The dish features chunky, browned bratwurst pieces intermingled with tender, golden-brown potato cubes and irregular, soft Spätzle noodles. All components are coated in a rich, savory, slightly glistening sauce infused with sauerkraut. A generous sprinkle of vibrant green chopped fresh flat-leaf parsley garnishes the top. The overall color palette is warm, with golden-browns, creamy yellows, and hints of green. The texture is varied, showing the firm exterior of the bratwurst and the soft, yielding potatoes and noodles. The plating is organized yet natural, allowing moderate negative space around the mounded dish. The plate rests on a simple light wooden table surface. A folded grey cotton napkin is placed to the left. Natural, even overhead lighting illuminates the scene. The background is softly blurred, suggesting a modern bistro setting.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with a dollop of whole grain German mustard on the side.
Accompanied by a crisp lager beer.

ingredients.name: Waxy potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500g, peeled and cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add bratwurst. Brown on all sides. Cook thoroughly. Remove bratwurst from skillet. Slice into 2 cm thick chunks. Set aside.
Add diced onion to the same skillet. Sauté until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic and caraway seeds. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Add potato cubes to the skillet. Cook, stirring occasionally, until lightly browned, about 8-10 minutes.
Stir in drained sauerkraut, broth, and mustard. Bring to a simmer. Reduce heat to medium-low. Cover and cook for 15-20 minutes, or until potatoes are tender.
While potatoes cook, prepare Spätzle according to package instructions. Drain well.
Once potatoes are tender, return sliced bratwurst chunks to the skillet. Stir in cooked Spätzle and butter. Toss gently to combine and heat through.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve immediately. Garnish with fresh chopped parsley.

recipes.recipe_name: Savory Beef & Broccoli Potato Bites
recipes.visual_description: An elegant platter showcases 10-12 savory canapés, each a vibrant bite-sized piece. Golden-brown roasted potato rounds, approximately 1 cm thick, form the base. Each potato slice is topped generously with a mound of rich, browned ground beef, finely diced, showing its tender, seasoned texture. Scattered over the beef are small, bright green pieces of blanched broccoli, adding a fresh pop of color and slight texture contrast. A sprinkle of finely chopped fresh chives or parsley provides a final touch of green and freshness. The canapés are arranged naturally and casually on a simple, rustic wooden serving board or a light-colored ceramic platter. The setting is a homely family kitchen, with a warm, cozy light illuminating the food. A casually placed, light-colored linen napkin sits nearby. The focus is entirely on the inviting, comforting appearance of the food, presented as if for a family gathering.
instructions: Preheat oven to 200°C.
Wash potatoes. Slice potatoes into 1 cm thick rounds.
Toss potato rounds with 15ml olive oil, salt, and pepper. Spread on a baking tray.
Roast potatoes for 20-25 minutes, or until tender and golden. Flip halfway.
While potatoes roast, heat remaining 15ml olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground beef to skillet. Break it apart with a spoon. Cook until browned.
Drain excess fat from beef. Add minced garlic to beef. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Season beef with salt and pepper. Set aside.
Bring a small pot of salted water to a boil. Add broccoli florets.
Blanch broccoli for 2-3 minutes until tender-crisp. Drain immediately.
Chop blanched broccoli into small, fine pieces.
Remove roasted potatoes from oven. Let cool slightly.
Top each potato round with a spoonful of seasoned ground beef.
Sprinkle chopped broccoli over the beef.
Arrange bites on a serving platter. Garnish with fresh chives or parsley. Serve warm.
notes: These canapés are best served warm but can be assembled ahead of time and gently reheated. Ensure potatoes are cooked through but still firm enough to hold toppings.

recipes.recipe_name: Central Asian Lamb & Potato Stew
recipes.visual_description: A hearty Central Asian Lamb & Potato Stew is presented in a deep, rustic, earthy-toned ceramic bowl. Large, tender lamb chunks are nestled amongst substantial, irregularly cut potato and sweet potato pieces. The rich, savory tomato-based broth coats all ingredients, showcasing shades of deep reddish-brown and orange. A generous sprinkle of freshly chopped green dill and cilantro provides a vibrant contrast on top. The bowl sits on a well-worn, natural wooden dining table. A simple, off-white ceramic side plate is placed beside it, with a torn piece of traditional Central Asian flatbread (non) ready for dipping. A folded, textured linen napkin and a rustic metal spoon complete the homely setting. Warm, soft light emanates from an overhead kitchen fixture, casting gentle shadows and highlighting the comforting steam rising from the stew.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve with fresh, torn flatbread (non) for dipping into the broth.
Often accompanied by a simple side salad of thinly sliced onions and cucumbers.

ingredients.name: Potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 500g, peeled and cut into 3-4 cm chunks

ingredients.name: Sweet potatoes
ingredients.quantity: 300g, peeled and cut into 3-4 cm chunks

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium-high heat.
Brown lamb chunks on all sides. Remove lamb from pot.
Add chopped onions to the pot. Cook until softened, about 5-7 minutes.
Add minced garlic. Cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Return lamb to the pot. Add diced tomatoes, broth, cumin, coriander, paprika, salt, and pepper. Stir well.
Bring to a boil. Reduce heat to low. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Add potato and sweet potato chunks to the pot. Stir.
Cover and simmer for another 30-40 minutes, or until lamb and potatoes are tender.
Adjust seasoning if needed. Serve hot, garnished with fresh dill or cilantro.
notes: Ensure lamb is cut into generous, rustic chunks for a hearty stew.
The stew should be thick and comforting, not watery.

recipes.recipe_name: Lamb and Cottage Cheese Curry
recipes.visual_description: A single generous portion of Lamb and Cottage Cheese Curry is presented in a deep, rustic ceramic bowl with a warm, earthy tone. The rich, reddish-brown curry sauce, infused with aromatic spices, coats tender, thick chunks of slow-cooked lamb and soft, white cubes of cottage cheese. The lamb pieces are irregularly shaped, showcasing their hearty texture, while the cottage cheese cubes maintain their form, offering a gentle contrast. A scattering of freshly chopped vibrant green coriander leaves garnishes the top, adding a pop of color and freshness. The curry's surface reveals a slight shimmer from the oil, indicating a well-balanced, flavorful dish. The bowl sits on a well-worn, dark wooden dining table, alongside a simple, off-white cloth napkin and a polished metal spoon. The scene is bathed in soft, warm, natural light, evoking a comforting, homely atmosphere.
cultural_serving_suggestions: Serve hot with steamed Basmati rice or warm naan bread.
Offer a side of cooling raita (yogurt dip) or sliced red onions.

ingredients.name: Cottage Cheese
ingredients.quantity: 200 g, pressed and cut into 2 cm cubes

instructions: Heat oil in a large pot over medium-high heat.
Add lamb chunks. Sear until browned on all sides. Remove lamb from pot. Set aside.
Add diced onions to the pot. Sauté until golden brown and softened, about 8-10 minutes.
Add minced garlic and grated ginger. Cook for 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in ground cumin, ground coriander, turmeric powder, and chilli powder. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly.
Pour in crushed tomatoes. Cook, stirring occasionally, for 5-7 minutes until the sauce thickens and oil separates.
Return seared lamb to the pot. Add water and salt. Bring to a simmer.
Cover the pot. Reduce heat to low. Simmer for 60-90 minutes, or until lamb is tender. Ensure internal lamb temperature reaches 75°C.
Gently fold in the cubed cottage cheese during the last 5 minutes of cooking. Do not overmix.
Stir in garam masala. Cook for 1 minute.
Garnish with fresh chopped coriander before serving.
notes: For best results, press cottage cheese for 30 minutes to remove excess water before cubing.
Adjust chilli powder to suit your preferred spice level.

recipes.recipe_name: Cacao Walnut Parfait with Strawberry Ginger Compote
recipes.visual_description: A single elegant dessert parfait is presented in a clear glass, revealing distinct, vibrant layers. The bottom layer is a rich, golden-brown date caramel, smooth and glistening. Above it sits a creamy, dark chocolate cacao walnut cream, speckled with small, irregularly chopped toasted walnuts. The next layer is a vibrant red strawberry ginger compote, showing tender, diced strawberry pieces.
